leg-V2401-start.caption: Leg 1 of 13: New York to Miami. Chief scientist J.L. Worzel.
leg-V2401-start.spoken: Leg one of thirteen begins. Vema sails from New York for Miami, with J. L. Worzel as chief scientist.

day-1967-01-17.caption: Tuesday, January 17th, 1967. Day 1 of the voyage, at sea, bound from New York for Miami.
day-1967-01-17.spoken: Good morning. It's Tuesday, January seventeenth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day one of the voyage, at sea, bound from New York for Miami.

sum-1967-01-17.caption: We were about 100 nautical miles northeast of Cape Hatteras, in the North Atlantic. The crew took 5 samples at a depth of 1610 fathoms.
sum-1967-01-17.spoken: We were about one hundred nautical miles northeast of Cape Hatteras, in the North Atlantic. The crew took five samples at a depth of sixteen ten fathoms.

day-1967-01-18.caption: Wednesday, January 18th, 1967. Day 2 of the voyage, at sea, bound from New York for Miami.
day-1967-01-18.spoken: Good morning. It's Wednesday, January eighteenth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day two of the voyage, at sea, bound from New York for Miami.

log-p324-1.caption: NEPHLOMETER 13: DID NOT TRIP - STARTER NEGLECT POINT FIGURED ON WITH PADDLET AT 90° TO MAGNET ON RIG.
log-p324-1.spoken: The nephelometer did not trip. The starter neglect point was figured on with the paddlet at ninety degrees to the magnet on the rig.

log-p324-3.caption: WATER BARREL 1A: BARREL TRIPPED ON WAY DOWN BY TELLTALE SLIDE BARREL DID NOT PASS MESSENGER TO ARM CORE SAMPLE DISCARDED
log-p324-3.spoken: Water barrel 1A tripped on the way down by the telltale slide. The barrel did not pass the messenger to arm, so the core sample was discarded.

log-p324-2.caption: CORE CAMERA 13: RAW FILM OUT WHILE RIGGING WATER BARREL. - CAMERA IS TO FAST FOR. CORE HEAD CAMERA, SWITCHING TO SLOWER CAMERA. WITH CORE 2
log-p324-2.spoken: The raw film ran out while rigging the water barrel. The camera was too fast for the core head, so they switched to a slower camera with core two.

sum-1967-01-18.caption: We were about 200 nautical miles east of Cape Hatteras, in the North Atlantic. The day at 2415 fathoms included 7 stations. We faced some trouble when an instrument failed to trip, camera film ran out, and a sampler triggered early, losing the sample.
sum-1967-01-18.spoken: We were about two hundred nautical miles east of Cape Hatteras, in the North Atlantic. The day at two thousand four hundred fifteen fathoms included seven stations. We faced some trouble when an instrument failed to trip, camera film ran out, and a sampler triggered early, losing the sample.

day-1967-01-19.caption: Thursday, January 19th, 1967. Day 3 of the voyage, at sea, bound from New York for Miami.
day-1967-01-19.spoken: Good morning. It's Thursday, January nineteenth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day three of the voyage, at sea, bound from New York for Miami.

log-p323-2.caption: Depth Camera 1c: CAMERA FUNCTIONED PROPERLY, LIGHT BULB BROKE - BULB HOLDER EXTENDS TOO FAR FORWARD OF BATTERIES OR ONE OF THE BATTERY CASES, WILL BE CORRECTED. - ABOUT 1 FT. OF USABLE DATA
log-p323-2.spoken: Depth camera 1c functioned properly, but the light bulb broke. This left about one foot of usable data.

log-p323-3.caption: Core Camera 1c: GROUND WIRE RIPPED OFF CAMERA BEFORE CORE HEAD WAS DROPPED. WIRE TO BE REPLACED BY CABLE.
log-p323-3.spoken: The ground wire ripped off the core camera 1c before the core head was dropped. The wire was to be replaced by a cable.

log-p323-0.caption: Water Barrel L.B.: BARREL TRIPPED ON WAY DOWN - SAMPLE DISCARDED
log-p323-0.spoken: Water barrel L.B. tripped on the way down, so the sample was discarded.

log-p324-5.caption: Core 3: Depth of penetration 679 cm Core length Light brown lutite overlying gray and blue lutites. Lutite is moderately foraminiferal. Pipe bent due to extremely hard pull out
log-p324-5.spoken: Piston core three penetrated six hundred seventy-nine centimeters. The pipe bent due to an extremely hard pull out.

log-p324-6.caption: T-GRAD 2A: NO RECORD DUE TO LOOSE CONNECTION TO LIGHT SOURCE
log-p324-6.spoken: Heat-flow station 2A got no record. The connection to the light source was loose.

sum-1967-01-19.caption: We worked 7 stations about 200 nautical miles south of Cape Hatteras. A pipe bent from a hard pull, and a loose connection left no record. The sampler failed, and the camera bulb broke, limiting our data.
sum-1967-01-19.spoken: We worked seven stations about two hundred nautical miles south of Cape Hatteras. A pipe bent from a hard pull, and a loose connection left no record. The sampler failed, and the camera bulb broke, limiting our data.

day-1967-01-20.caption: Friday, January 20th, 1967. Day 4 of the voyage, at sea, bound from New York for Miami.
day-1967-01-20.spoken: Good morning. It's Friday, January twentieth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day four of the voyage, at sea, bound from New York for Miami.

sum-1967-01-20.caption: We were about 300 nautical miles northeast of the Bahamas, in the North Atlantic. The crew deployed 1 sonobuoy and collected 1 Millipore filter sample.
sum-1967-01-20.spoken: We were about three hundred nautical miles northeast of the Bahamas, in the North Atlantic. The crew deployed one sonobuoy and collected one Millipore filter sample.

day-1967-01-21.caption: Saturday, January 21st, 1967. Day 5 of the voyage, at sea, bound from New York for Miami.
day-1967-01-21.spoken: Good morning. It's Saturday, January twenty-first, nineteen sixty-seven. Day five of the voyage, at sea, bound from New York for Miami.

log-p322-0.caption: Water Barrel 1C: BARREL DID NOT CLOSE - SAMPLE DISCARDED
log-p322-0.spoken: Water barrel 1C came back without closing, so the sample was thrown away.

log-p322-5.caption: Core Camera 1d.: STARTING PIN WAS NOT REMOVED.
log-p322-5.spoken: The starting pin on core camera 1d was not removed.

log-p322-6.caption: Milli 5 6-V 7-V 8-SF: Abundant sargasso; poor net hauls Rapid descent caused wire to foul on 2nd haul.
log-p322-6.spoken: The wire fouled on the second haul of the Millipore filters. The net hauls were poor, but abundant sargasso was caught.

sum-1967-01-21.caption: We worked about 200 nautical miles northeast of the Bahamas, in the North Atlantic. Seven stations were attempted at a depth of 2494 fathoms. Some equipment failed, including a lost sample and a fouled wire.
sum-1967-01-21.spoken: We worked about two hundred nautical miles northeast of the Bahamas, in the North Atlantic. Seven stations were attempted at a depth of two thousand four hundred ninety-four fathoms. Some equipment failed, including a lost sample and a fouled wire.

day-1967-01-22.caption: Sunday, January 22nd, 1967. Day 6 of the voyage, at sea, bound from New York for Miami.
day-1967-01-22.spoken: Good morning. It's Sunday, January twenty-second, nineteen sixty-seven. Day six of the voyage, at sea, bound from New York for Miami.

log-p321-1.caption: T-GRAD 3A: No Record - Motor Froze Before Hit
log-p321-1.spoken: Heat-flow station 3A got no record because the motor froze before it hit the bottom.

log-p321-2.caption: Water Barrel 1D: Barrel Did Not Close - Sample Discarded
log-p321-2.spoken: Water barrel 1D came back without closing, so the sample was thrown away.

log-p321-5.caption: Core Camera 1e: Teller Dialer Did Not Function - Jammed because of uneven tightening.
log-p321-5.spoken: The core camera 1e dialer did not function because it jammed from uneven tightening.

sum-1967-01-22.caption: We worked about 400 nautical miles southwest of Bermuda in the North Atlantic. The motor froze and the sampler failed, so we lost some data. The camera dialer also jammed during our 7 stations.
sum-1967-01-22.spoken: We worked about four hundred nautical miles southwest of Bermuda in the North Atlantic. The motor froze and the sampler failed, so we lost some data. The camera dialer also jammed during our seven stations.

day-1967-01-23.caption: Monday, January 23rd, 1967. Day 7 of the voyage, at sea, bound from New York for Miami.
day-1967-01-23.spoken: Good morning. It's Monday, January twenty-third, nineteen sixty-seven. Day seven of the voyage, at sea, bound from New York for Miami.

log-p320-0.caption: Core 6: Core length - 800 cm. Core pipe bent at coupling with second core pipe. Brown lutite overlying intercalated layers of brown, gray & and greenish ashy lutite. Smaller firmer units exist within core.
log-p320-0.spoken: Piston core six came up with its pipe bent at the coupling. The core was eight hundred centimeters long.

log-p320-1.caption: T-Grad 3B: No Record - Motor Freeze P2 P3 P4 Ripped off or ruined
log-p320-1.spoken: Heat-flow station 3B got no record because the motor froze. Probes two, three, and four were ripped off or ruined.

log-p320-3.caption: Camera 6A: 0 - 10 Hits. Bad light strob or bad film. Developed piece of film from original spool; showed light strob or bad film.
log-p320-3.spoken: Camera 6A took ten pictures, but the light was bad. It was either the strobe or the film.

log-p320-5.caption: Core Camera 1F: Camera advanced but showed only 5 negatives. Strobe light did not flash under pressure.
log-p320-5.spoken: Core camera 1F advanced but only showed five negatives. The strobe light did not flash under pressure.

log-p320-6.caption: Bio 13-V, 14-V, 15-SF, 16-SF, Milli #7: This series covered a very active upward migration of small scatterers at dusk
log-p320-6.spoken: The bio series covered a very active upward migration of small scatterers at dusk.

sum-1967-01-23.caption: We were about 400 nautical miles east of the Bahamas, in the North Atlantic. The crew completed 7 stations, though a bent core pipe and a frozen motor caused some trouble. We also faced bad light and a failed strobe.
sum-1967-01-23.spoken: We were about four hundred nautical miles east of the Bahamas, in the North Atlantic. The crew completed seven stations, though a bent core pipe and a frozen motor caused some trouble. We also faced bad light and a failed strobe.

day-1967-01-24.caption: Tuesday, January 24th, 1967. Day 8 of the voyage, at sea, bound from New York for Miami.
day-1967-01-24.spoken: Good morning. It's Tuesday, January twenty-fourth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day eight of the voyage, at sea, bound from New York for Miami.

log-p319-3.caption: Core Camera 1F: Film advanced but stereolight didn't flash.
log-p319-3.spoken: The core camera 1F advanced its film, but the stereolight did not flash.

sum-1967-01-24.caption: The day's work, about 300 nautical miles east of the Bahamas, in the North Atlantic: 4 bottom-camera lowerings, 2 piston cores, 2 cameras on the corer, 2 water-barrel samples and 2 plankton tows. Soundings from 2506 to 2585 fathoms.
sum-1967-01-24.spoken: The day's work, about three hundred nautical miles east of the Bahamas, in the North Atlantic: four bottom-camera lowerings, two piston cores, two cameras on the corer, two water-barrel samples and two plankton tows. Soundings from two thousand five hundred six to two thousand five hundred eighty-five fathoms.

log-p318-1.caption: Camera 7: 5-6 / SCRATCHED. VERY BUMPY BOTTOM - CORRECT PIPES
log-p318-1.spoken: Camera seven came back with five to six scratched frames. The bottom was very bumpy, so they corrected the pipes.

log-p318-3.caption: Core Camera 16: DID NOT SEND DOWN. PREVIOUS LIGHT HEAD + MAKING NEW CROSS OVER HEAD.
log-p318-3.spoken: Core camera sixteen did not go down because the previous light head was broken. They were making a new cross over head.

log-p319-5.caption: Water Barrel 3A: Telltale slide indicates barrel tripped about one third of way down. Sample discarded
log-p319-5.spoken: Water barrel 3A tripped about one third of the way down, so the sample was discarded.

day-1967-01-25.caption: Wednesday, January 25th, 1967. Day 9 of the voyage, at sea, bound from New York for Miami.
day-1967-01-25.spoken: Good morning. It's Wednesday, January twenty-fifth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day nine of the voyage, at sea, bound from New York for Miami.

log-p318-6.caption: Water Barrel 3B: Telltale Slide shows that Barrel Cured Soon After Lowering. Sample Discarded
log-p318-6.spoken: Water barrel 3B closed soon after lowering, so the sample was discarded.

log-p317-2.caption: Core Camera 1: 30 NEG. NO BOTTOM PICTURES
log-p317-2.spoken: Core camera one developed thirty negatives, but none showed the sea floor.

log-p316-4.caption: Bio 23-V 24-V: SARGASSO INTERFERED WITH FLOWMETER. THESE TOWS SAMPLED THE DENSE SURFACE SL (0-40 Fm) WHALES + SHARKS OBSERVED THIS AREA.
log-p316-4.spoken: Sargasso interfered with the flowmeter during the plankton tows. Whales and sharks were observed in the area.

log-p316-0.caption: Water Barrel 3C: TELLTALE SLIDE SHOWS THAT BARREL CLOSED AT SURFACE SAMPLE DISCARDED
log-p316-0.spoken: Water barrel 3C came back with the telltale slide showing it closed at the surface. The sample was discarded.

log-p317-5.caption: Core Camera 2: 16 NEG. NO BOTTOM PICTURES
log-p317-5.spoken: Core camera two developed sixteen negatives, but none showed the sea floor.

sum-1967-01-25.caption: We worked in the North Atlantic, 300 nautical miles east of the Bahamas. The sea floor lay at 2526 fathoms. We made 18 stations, though some samplers and cameras failed.
sum-1967-01-25.spoken: We worked in the North Atlantic, three hundred nautical miles east of the Bahamas. The sea floor lay at two thousand five hundred twenty-six fathoms. We made eighteen stations, though some samplers and cameras failed.

log-p316-2.caption: Core 11: BEDDED BROWN & GRAY LUTITES CONTAINING A BAND, IN DURATICAL LIMESTONE LAYER. DEPTH OF PENETRATION 1782 CM. CORE LENGTH 932 CM. PIPE WAS BENT & CUTTING EDGE DAMAGED. BOTTOM TOPOGRAPHY: RIPPLEY NEAR BASE OF STEEP SLOPE.
log-p316-2.spoken: Piston core eleven brought up bedded lutites with a band in a duratical limestone layer. The pipe was bent and the cutting edge was damaged.

log-p316-5.caption: Camera 10A: NEGATIVES WERE DESTROYED IN DARK ROOM ACCIDENT 0-6
log-p316-5.spoken: The negatives from camera 10A were destroyed in a dark room accident.

log-p316-7.caption: Deepo Camera 8A: LIGHT WENT OUT ON BATHY HITS COULDN'T BRIGHT ENOUGH ON WAY DOWN FOR NEPHO READING.
log-p316-7.spoken: The light went out on the bathythermograph for deepo camera 8A. It could not get bright enough on the way down for a nephelometer reading.

day-1967-01-26.caption: Thursday, January 26th, 1967. Day 10 of the voyage, at sea, bound from New York for Miami.
day-1967-01-26.spoken: Good morning. It's Thursday, January twenty-sixth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day ten of the voyage, at sea, bound from New York for Miami.

sum-1967-01-26.caption: We worked about 200 nautical miles east of the Bahamas in the North Atlantic. The day brought 9 samples, but we lost a sampler and light source. We also faced broken pipes and failed probes.
sum-1967-01-26.spoken: We worked about two hundred nautical miles east of the Bahamas in the North Atlantic. The day brought nine samples, but we lost a sampler and light source. We also faced broken pipes and failed probes.

log-p315-6.caption: Camera 8: LIGHT IN STRENGTH - 650 FMS. LIGHT SOURCE DIVED AFTER BOTTOM SHOTS.
log-p315-6.spoken: Camera eight took shots at six hundred fifty fathoms. The light source dived after the bottom shots.

log-p315-2.caption: Water Barrel 4A: TELLTALE SHOWS THAT BARREL TRIPPED HALF WAY DOWN SAMPLE DISCARDED
log-p315-2.spoken: Water barrel 4A tripped halfway down, so the sample was discarded.

log-p315-3.caption: Core 12: Brown and pale yellow lutite, moist, firm and compacted containing a 39 cm calcareous sand layer. Depth of penetration: 315 cm; Core length 487 cm. Pipe bent, cutting edge slightly damaged. Bottom Topography - flat, gently dipping.
log-p315-3.spoken: Piston core twelve came up with a bent pipe and a slightly damaged cutting edge. It contained a thirty-nine centimeter layer of calcareous sand.

log-p315-4.caption: T-Grad 5: WATER TEMP RECORD BUT NO PROBES P4 RIPPED OFF P3 DEFECTIVE AT HIT P2 AND P1 DID NOT PENETRATE
log-p315-4.spoken: Heat-flow station five recorded water temperature, but the probes failed. Probe four ripped off, probe three was defective, and probes two and one did not penetrate.

log-p315-7.caption: Core 4: NO BOTTOM SHOTS - SHOWS TRIGGER WEIGHT & CABLE.
log-p315-7.spoken: Core four had no bottom shots. The film showed the trigger weight and cable.

day-1967-01-27.caption: Friday, January 27th, 1967. Day 11 of the voyage, at sea, bound from New York for Miami.
day-1967-01-27.spoken: Good morning. It's Friday, January twenty-seventh, nineteen sixty-seven. Day eleven of the voyage, at sea, bound from New York for Miami.

log-p314-4.caption: Water Barrel 4B: Telltale slide indicates barrel trigger soon after lowering Sample discarded
log-p314-4.spoken: Water barrel 4B triggered soon after lowering. The sample was discarded.

log-p314-6.caption: Neph 9A: Felt came of side of camera + jammed into collecting wheel no reading.
log-p314-6.spoken: The felt on the nephelometer came off and jammed the collecting wheel. No reading was obtained.

log-p313-4.caption: Camera 12: 12-05 HITS ROCK FORMATIONS, MOUNDS OF SEDIMENT, HOLE LIKE TRAPS, CLOUDS OF SEDIMENT.
log-p313-4.spoken: Camera twelve photographed rock formations, mounds of sediment, and hole-like traps. Clouds of sediment were also visible.

log-p313-5.caption: DEAD 48.: SPIRE SHAFT LOCK GARBED LOSTED.
log-p313-5.spoken: The spire shaft lock garbed losted, according to the log entry.

log-p313-0.caption: T-Grad 7: GOOD RECORD - ONE PROBE PENETRATION H.F. = 6.700 ucal/cm2/sec (?) No Conductivity Record Since Core Not Extruded Core could not be extruded. Penetration 280cm.
log-p313-0.spoken: Heat-flow station seven recorded six point seven zero zero microcalories per square centimeter per second. The core could not be pushed out, so no conductivity record was taken.

log-p313-1.caption: Core 14: Core length 432cm. Pipe bent, cutting edge good. Topography: flat with some ripples.
log-p313-1.spoken: Piston core fourteen came up with a bent pipe, though the cutting edge was good. It measured four hundred thirty-two centimeters long.

log-p313-6.caption: Core Camera 6A.: MOTOR BURNED OUT. TO BE REPLACED.
log-p313-6.spoken: The motor on Core Camera 6A burned out. It needed to be replaced.

sum-1967-01-27.caption: We were about 200 nautical miles east of the Bahamas, in the North Atlantic. The team completed 14 stations, including 2 piston cores and 2 heat-flow measurements. A sampler triggered early, and a pipe bent, but the core was recovered.
sum-1967-01-27.spoken: We were about two hundred nautical miles east of the Bahamas, in the North Atlantic. The team completed fourteen stations, including two piston cores and two heat-flow measurements. A sampler triggered early, and a pipe bent, but the core was recovered.

log-p312-2.caption: Camera 13: 1-9 TRIGGER STUCK OR CHANGED. POOR FORMATIONS.
log-p312-2.spoken: Camera thirteen had a stuck trigger, and the resulting pictures were of poor quality.

log-p312-4.caption: Core Camera 68: STRONG DID NOT FLASH.
log-p312-4.spoken: The flash on Core Camera sixty-eight did not fire, so no pictures were taken.

log-p312-5.caption: Core 15: Core could not be extruded. Penetration 434cm. Core length 627cm. Cutting edge good, pipe bent. Topography - ripply. Discoasters found in core contained in cutting edge of pipe
log-p312-5.spoken: Piston core fifteen came up with a bent pipe, and the core could not be pushed out. Discoasters were found in the cutting edge of the pipe.

day-1967-01-28.caption: Saturday, January 28th, 1967. Day 12 of the voyage, at sea, bound from New York for Miami.
day-1967-01-28.spoken: Good morning. It's Saturday, January twenty-eighth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day twelve of the voyage, at sea, bound from New York for Miami.

log-p311-2.caption: Core Camera 10: STROBE DID NOT FLASH.
log-p311-2.spoken: The core camera for station ten came up with a problem. Its strobe light did not flash.

log-p311-3.caption: Core 16: Brown lutite overlying large manganese nodules. Penetration 40cm. Core length 32cm. Topography: gently rolling. Pipe bent, cutting edge torn off and lost on bottom with core catcher. No trigger core.
log-p311-3.spoken: Piston core sixteen found brown mud over large manganese nodules. The pipe bent and the cutting edge tore off, so the core catcher was lost on the bottom.

sum-1967-01-28.caption: We were about 200 nautical miles east of the Bahamas, in the North Atlantic. The crew completed 12 stations, including 3 bottom-camera lowerings and 2 water-barrel samples. We faced some technical issues, such as a stuck trigger and a failed camera flash.
sum-1967-01-28.spoken: We were about two hundred nautical miles east of the Bahamas, in the North Atlantic. The crew completed twelve stations, including three bottom-camera lowerings and two water-barrel samples. We faced some technical issues, such as a stuck trigger and a failed camera flash.

day-1967-01-29.caption: Sunday, January 29th, 1967. Day 13 of the voyage, at sea, bound from New York for Miami.
day-1967-01-29.spoken: Good morning. It's Sunday, January twenty-ninth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day thirteen of the voyage, at sea, bound from New York for Miami.

leg-V2401-end.caption: Arriving Miami. Log: Moderate weather - successful shakedown. On this leg: 2,695 miles, 266 hours under way and 44 hours on station, averaging 9.4 knots.
leg-V2401-end.spoken: Vema arrives in Miami. From the voyage log: Moderate weather. A successful shakedown. On this leg: two thousand six hundred ninety-five miles, two hundred sixty-six hours under way and forty-four hours on station, averaging nine point four knots.

day-1967-01-30.caption: Monday, January 30th, 1967. Day 14 of the voyage, in port at Miami.
day-1967-01-30.spoken: Good morning. It's Monday, January thirtieth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day fourteen of the voyage, in port at Miami.

day-1967-01-31.caption: Tuesday, January 31st, 1967. Day 15 of the voyage, in port at Miami.
day-1967-01-31.spoken: Good morning. It's Tuesday, January thirty-first, nineteen sixty-seven. Day fifteen of the voyage, in port at Miami.

leg-V2402-start.caption: Leg 2 of 13: Miami to Cristobal. Chief scientist J.L. Worzel.
leg-V2402-start.spoken: Leg two of thirteen begins. Vema sails from Miami for Cristobal, with J. L. Worzel as chief scientist.

sum-1967-01-31.caption: We were about 90 nautical miles southwest of Miami, in the Gulf of Mexico. The team collected 1 Millipore filter sample.
sum-1967-01-31.spoken: We were about ninety nautical miles southwest of Miami, in the Gulf of Mexico. The team collected one Millipore filter sample.

day-1967-02-01.caption: Wednesday, February 1st, 1967. Day 16 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Miami for Cristobal.
day-1967-02-01.spoken: Good morning. It's Wednesday, February first, nineteen sixty-seven. Day sixteen of the voyage, at sea, bound from Miami for Cristobal.

sum-1967-02-01.caption: We were about 300 nautical miles northeast of the Yucatan, in the Gulf of Mexico. The crew deployed 1 sonobuoy during the day.
sum-1967-02-01.spoken: We were about three hundred nautical miles northeast of the Yucatan, in the Gulf of Mexico. The crew deployed one sonobuoy during the day.

day-1967-02-02.caption: Thursday, February 2nd, 1967. Day 17 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Miami for Cristobal.
day-1967-02-02.spoken: Good morning. It's Thursday, February second, nineteen sixty-seven. Day seventeen of the voyage, at sea, bound from Miami for Cristobal.

log-p310-5.caption: Camera 15A: Camera case flooded, removed & replaced O ring cleaned surfaces. Spot down 10th cut camera to 100 ft. Leakage found to be from front seal.
log-p310-5.spoken: Camera 15A flooded, so the O ring was removed and cleaned. The leak was found to be from the front seal.

log-p310-1.caption: Core 17: Brown lutite. Depth of penetration 585cm. Core length app. 11 cm. Messenger was lost somewhere during its course down cable, hence trigger mechanism was never armed. Bottom topography: flat
log-p310-1.spoken: Piston core seventeen went down into brown lutite, but the messenger was lost on the cable. The trigger mechanism was never armed, so only eleven centimeters of core came up.

log-p310-3.caption: Water Barrel 7A: Barrel did not trip Sample discarded
log-p310-3.spoken: Water barrel 7A did not trip, so the sample was discarded.

sum-1967-02-02.caption: We worked about 300 nautical miles west of Miami in the Gulf of Mexico. Eleven stations were completed, though a lost messenger and a failed sampler caused us to lose two samples. The camera seal was also repaired after flooding.
sum-1967-02-02.spoken: We worked about three hundred nautical miles west of Miami in the Gulf of Mexico. Eleven stations were completed, though a lost messenger and a failed sampler caused us to lose two samples. The camera seal was also repaired after flooding.

day-1967-02-03.caption: Friday, February 3rd, 1967. Day 18 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Miami for Cristobal.
day-1967-02-03.spoken: Good morning. It's Friday, February third, nineteen sixty-seven. Day eighteen of the voyage, at sea, bound from Miami for Cristobal.

log-p308-3.caption: Core Camera 8A: Pin was pulled but recognized and inserted in slot. (will be fixed) camera did not trigger.
log-p308-3.spoken: On core camera 8A, the pin was pulled but recognized and inserted in the slot. The camera did not trigger.

log-p308-1.caption: Camera 16: 11 hits - 9 wet. smelly impressions, odd loops nice creature encrinal from small mound of sediment. bottom is relatively smooth.
log-p308-1.spoken: Camera sixteen took eleven hits, with nine wet and smelly impressions. The photos showed an odd loop and a nice creature encrinal from a small mound of sediment.

log-p308-4.caption: Milli 16 Bio 33-V 34-V: Tows 33-V and 34-V no good because of extreme wire L.
log-p308-4.spoken: Plankton tows thirty-three-V and thirty-four-V were no good because of extreme wire L.

sum-1967-02-03.caption: We worked in the Gulf of Mexico, 400 nautical miles west of Miami, at a depth of 1616 fathoms. We completed 10 stations, including a heat-flow measurement of 0.95. A living creature appeared in photos, though the camera failed to trigger and tows failed due to wire issues.
sum-1967-02-03.spoken: We worked in the Gulf of Mexico, four hundred nautical miles west of Miami, at a depth of sixteen sixteen fathoms. We completed ten stations, including a heat-flow measurement of zero point nine five. A living creature appeared in photos, though the camera failed to trigger and tows failed due to wire issues.

day-1967-02-04.caption: Saturday, February 4th, 1967. Day 19 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Miami for Cristobal.
day-1967-02-04.spoken: Good morning. It's Saturday, February fourth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day nineteen of the voyage, at sea, bound from Miami for Cristobal.

log-p307-1.caption: Camera 17: Camera 17 hits - 16 neg. One wet 3" showol excessive mud flood, starfish print- bottom ripped slightly through out. Correct. - Approx 30.
log-p307-1.spoken: Camera seventeen took sixteen negatives. One showed a starfish print on the bottom, but the water was very muddy.

sum-1967-02-04.caption: We were about 400 nautical miles north of the Yucatan in the Gulf of Mexico. The crew completed 10 stations, including a piston core and a bottom camera. We saw a starfish print in the muddy water.
sum-1967-02-04.spoken: We were about four hundred nautical miles north of the Yucatan in the Gulf of Mexico. The crew completed ten stations, including a piston core and a bottom camera. We saw a starfish print in the muddy water.

day-1967-02-05.caption: Sunday, February 5th, 1967. Day 20 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Miami for Cristobal.
day-1967-02-05.spoken: Good morning. It's Sunday, February fifth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day twenty of the voyage, at sea, bound from Miami for Cristobal.

log-p305-4.caption: Camera 18: 8 Hits - 7 neg. Robot and signs of animal life.
log-p305-4.spoken: Camera eighteen took eight hits, with seven negatives showing the bottom. The photos showed a robot and signs of animal life.

log-p304-1.caption: Bio 35-V: Sampled surface SL which extended down to 60 Fm. Conspicuous lack of usual deeper SLs. On 35-V, nylon thread from net may have interfered with flowmeter.
log-p304-1.spoken: The plankton tow caught the surface scattering layer, which extended down to sixty fathoms. There was a conspicuous lack of the usual deeper scattering layers.

sum-1967-02-05.caption: We were about 200 nautical miles north of the Yucatan, in the Gulf of Mexico. The water was 1942 fathoms deep. We completed 11 stations and saw animal life on camera.
sum-1967-02-05.spoken: We were about two hundred nautical miles north of the Yucatan, in the Gulf of Mexico. The water was nineteen forty-two fathoms deep. We completed eleven stations and saw animal life on camera.

day-1967-02-06.caption: Monday, February 6th, 1967. Day 21 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Miami for Cristobal.
day-1967-02-06.spoken: Good morning. It's Monday, February sixth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day twenty-one of the voyage, at sea, bound from Miami for Cristobal.

sum-1967-02-06.caption: We were about 200 nautical miles northwest of the Yucatan, in the Gulf of Mexico. The crew deployed 2 sonobuoys that day.
sum-1967-02-06.spoken: We were about two hundred nautical miles northwest of the Yucatan, in the Gulf of Mexico. The crew deployed two sonobuoys that day.

day-1967-02-07.caption: Tuesday, February 7th, 1967. Day 22 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Miami for Cristobal.
day-1967-02-07.spoken: Good morning. It's Tuesday, February seventh, nineteen sixty-seven. Day twenty-two of the voyage, at sea, bound from Miami for Cristobal.

day-1967-02-08.caption: Wednesday, February 8th, 1967. Day 23 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Miami for Cristobal.
day-1967-02-08.spoken: Good morning. It's Wednesday, February eighth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day twenty-three of the voyage, at sea, bound from Miami for Cristobal.

sum-1967-02-08.caption: We were about 300 nautical miles west of the Yucatan, in the Gulf of Mexico. The crew deployed 1 sonobuoy to gather data.
sum-1967-02-08.spoken: We were about three hundred nautical miles west of the Yucatan, in the Gulf of Mexico. The crew deployed one sonobuoy to gather data.

day-1967-02-09.caption: Thursday, February 9th, 1967. Day 24 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Miami for Cristobal.
day-1967-02-09.spoken: Good morning. It's Thursday, February ninth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day twenty-four of the voyage, at sea, bound from Miami for Cristobal.

sum-1967-02-09.caption: We were about 200 nautical miles west of the Yucatan, in the Gulf of Mexico. The crew collected 1 Millipore filter sample and 1 sonobuoy.
sum-1967-02-09.spoken: We were about two hundred nautical miles west of the Yucatan, in the Gulf of Mexico. The crew collected one Millipore filter sample and one sonobuoy.

day-1967-02-10.caption: Friday, February 10th, 1967. Day 25 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Miami for Cristobal.
day-1967-02-10.spoken: Good morning. It's Friday, February tenth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day twenty-five of the voyage, at sea, bound from Miami for Cristobal.

log-p303-5.caption: Water Barrel 10A: Barrel tripped at surface from telltale slide. Sample discarded
log-p303-5.spoken: Water barrel 10A tripped at the surface from the telltale slide. The sample was discarded.

log-p303-6.caption: Milli 20 Bio 37-V 38-V: Routine millipore, but the 2 vertical tows, 37-V + 38-V, yielded myriads of planktonic tunicates - probably salps. An additional surface tow confirmed the suspicion that these masses of salps were a surface phenomenon.
log-p303-6.spoken: The vertical tows thirty-seven-V and thirty-eight-V yielded myriads of planktonic tunicates, probably salps. A surface tow confirmed these masses were a surface phenomenon.

sum-1967-02-10.caption: We worked about 300 nautical miles northwest of the Yucatan in the Gulf of Mexico. The day included 8 stations, though a sampler failed at the surface. We also saw an unusual abundance of salps.
sum-1967-02-10.spoken: We worked about three hundred nautical miles northwest of the Yucatan in the Gulf of Mexico. The day included eight stations, though a sampler failed at the surface. We also saw an unusual abundance of salps.

day-1967-02-11.caption: Saturday, February 11th, 1967. Day 26 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Miami for Cristobal.
day-1967-02-11.spoken: Good morning. It's Saturday, February eleventh, nineteen sixty-seven. Day twenty-six of the voyage, at sea, bound from Miami for Cristobal.

sum-1967-02-11.caption: We were about 100 nautical miles north of the Yucatan, in the Gulf of Mexico. The team deployed 1 sonobuoy and collected 1 Millipore filter sample.
sum-1967-02-11.spoken: We were about one hundred nautical miles north of the Yucatan, in the Gulf of Mexico. The team deployed one sonobuoy and collected one Millipore filter sample.

day-1967-02-12.caption: Sunday, February 12th, 1967. Day 27 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Miami for Cristobal.
day-1967-02-12.spoken: Good morning. It's Sunday, February twelfth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day twenty-seven of the voyage, at sea, bound from Miami for Cristobal.

log-p301-2.caption: Camera 20: 14 NEG 20 HITS CORRECT 340° SLIDES OF BOTTOM LIFE Purple macks thrown out, does not appear to be smooth mud type sediment, very whitey coalesce. 1 shot looks like an out crop float.
log-p301-2.spoken: Camera twenty captured fourteen negatives showing purple macks on the bottom. The sediment looked very white and coalesced, not like smooth mud.

log-p301-4.caption: Core Camera 11: 16 NEG, NO BOTTOM SHOTS. FILM Stretched by safelight.
log-p301-4.spoken: Core camera eleven returned sixteen negatives, but there were no bottom shots. The film had been stretched by the safelight.

sum-1967-02-12.caption: We were about 200 nautical miles east of the Yucatan in the Gulf of Mexico. The team completed 7 stations, including 1 heat-flow measurement and 1 piston core. We saw unusual bottom life, but the film was damaged.
sum-1967-02-12.spoken: We were about two hundred nautical miles east of the Yucatan in the Gulf of Mexico. The team completed seven stations, including one heat-flow measurement and one piston core. We saw unusual bottom life, but the film was damaged.

day-1967-02-13.caption: Monday, February 13th, 1967. Day 28 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Miami for Cristobal.
day-1967-02-13.spoken: Good morning. It's Monday, February thirteenth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day twenty-eight of the voyage, at sea, bound from Miami for Cristobal.

log-p300-0.caption: Core Camera 12: 2700 ft. NO BOTTOM SHOTS.
log-p300-0.spoken: Core camera twelve was lowered to two thousand seven hundred feet. It did not take any bottom shots.

log-p300-1.caption: Water Barrel 11A: BARREL DID NOT CLOSE SAMPLE DISCARDED
log-p300-1.spoken: Water barrel 11A came back without closing. The sample was discarded.

log-p300-5.caption: Bio 41-V 42-V Milli 23: This area not especially prolific with respect to numbers of plankton, but there was an extraordinary diversity of organisms in this pair of tows. Indistinct boundaries between the 3 SLs present: 0-100 Fm, 120-140 Fm, 220-290 Fm.
log-p300-5.spoken: The plankton tows showed an extraordinary diversity of organisms. There were three sound-scattering layers with indistinct boundaries.

sum-1967-02-13.caption: We worked about 300 nautical miles east of the Yucatan in the Gulf of Mexico. The camera failed to capture the bottom, and a sampler was lost. Yet we noted extraordinary diversity and saw living things on the bottom.
sum-1967-02-13.spoken: We worked about three hundred nautical miles east of the Yucatan in the Gulf of Mexico. The camera failed to capture the bottom, and a sampler was lost. Yet we noted extraordinary diversity and saw living things on the bottom.

log-p299-0.caption: Camera 22: 11/168. 13 HITS CURRENT 220° Bottom life Brainy type bottom - no ripple marks.
log-p299-0.spoken: Camera twenty-two found brainy type bottom with no ripple marks. It also caught bottom life.

log-p299-5.caption: Core 26: Int. redded lutite and foram sand. Penetration 725cm. Core length 683. Bottom topography: trench. Pipe bent: extrusion hard
log-p299-5.spoken: Piston core twenty-six went seven hundred twenty-five centimeters into reddened lutite and foram sand. The pipe bent, making extrusion hard.

log-p298-0.caption: Bio 43-V 44-V: Three SLs discernable: 0-90 Fm, 140-180 Fm 220-300 Fm. These tows + observations made immediately after dawn migrations.
log-p298-0.spoken: The plankton tows happened right after the dawn migrations. The echo sounder showed three sound-scattering layers.

day-1967-02-14.caption: Tuesday, February 14th, 1967. Day 29 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Miami for Cristobal.
day-1967-02-14.spoken: Good morning. It's Tuesday, February fourteenth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day twenty-nine of the voyage, at sea, bound from Miami for Cristobal.

log-p297-0.caption: Camera 23: 5 neg 7 hits. Current 225°. Very bumpy from bottom life - worm marks.
log-p297-0.spoken: Camera twenty-three took five negatives with seven hits. The sea floor was bumpy with worm marks, and the current ran at two hundred twenty-five degrees.

log-p298-1.caption: T-Grad 16A: NO RECORD - P4 x P3 DEFECTIVE P2 x P1 NO PENETRATOR
log-p298-1.spoken: Heat-flow station 16A failed to get a record. Probes four and three were defective, and probes two and one did not penetrate.

log-p298-3.caption: Water Barrel 13A: TELLTALE SLIDE INDICATES BARREL TRIPPED ABOUT HALF WAY DOWN SAMPLE DISCARDED
log-p298-3.spoken: Water barrel 13A triggered about halfway down the water column. The sample was discarded.

sum-1967-02-14.caption: We worked about 100 nautical miles west of Jamaica in the Caribbean. The team took 4 piston cores and 2 water-barrel samples. A bent pipe made extrusion hard, and a sampler triggered early, so a sample was lost.
sum-1967-02-14.spoken: We worked about one hundred nautical miles west of Jamaica in the Caribbean. The team took four piston cores and two water-barrel samples. A bent pipe made extrusion hard, and a sampler triggered early, so a sample was lost.

day-1967-02-15.caption: Wednesday, February 15th, 1967. Day 30 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Miami for Cristobal.
day-1967-02-15.spoken: Good morning. It's Wednesday, February fifteenth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day thirty of the voyage, at sea, bound from Miami for Cristobal.

log-p297-5.caption: Core Camera 16A: Trigger jaded.
log-p297-5.spoken: The trigger on core camera 16A was jaded.

log-p297-3.caption: Camera 24: 9 neg 10 shots. Current 330° ripple marks - signs of bottom life.
log-p297-3.spoken: Camera twenty-four captured nine negatives from ten shots. The floor showed ripple marks and signs of bottom life, with a current at three hundred thirty degrees.

sum-1967-02-15.caption: We worked about 200 nautical miles south of Jamaica in the Caribbean. The team completed 7 stations and took 1 piston core. We saw ripple marks and life signs, though a trigger mechanism failed.
sum-1967-02-15.spoken: We worked about two hundred nautical miles south of Jamaica in the Caribbean. The team completed seven stations and took one piston core. We saw ripple marks and life signs, though a trigger mechanism failed.

log-p296-0.caption: Core 29: Dotted sand and lutites. Penetration 137(?) core length 675cm. Bottom topography: flat - Columbia Basin. Core hit bottom before trigger trippedarming device. Hit was not noticed.
log-p296-0.spoken: Piston core twenty-nine hit the bottom before the trigger tripped, and the crew did not notice the hit. The core was six hundred seventy-five centimeters long.

log-p296-2.caption: Water Barrel 14A: TELLTALE SLIDE INDICATES BARREL TRIPPED PART WAY DOWN SAMPLE DISCARDED
log-p296-2.spoken: Water barrel 14A tripped part way down, so the sample was discarded.

log-p296-3.caption: Camera 25: 500ft 6hrs Current 195° wriggle marks - signs of bottom life.
log-p296-3.spoken: Camera twenty-five was lowered to five hundred feet for six hours. The pictures showed wriggle marks, which were signs of bottom life.

log-p296-5.caption: Camera 16: Strong. no bottom shots - sediment in water.
log-p296-5.spoken: Camera sixteen did not get any bottom shots because there was sediment in the water.

day-1967-02-16.caption: Thursday, February 16th, 1967. Day 31 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Miami for Cristobal.
day-1967-02-16.spoken: Good morning. It's Thursday, February sixteenth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day thirty-one of the voyage, at sea, bound from Miami for Cristobal.

log-p295-1.caption: Camera 26: 6mg 7 hits. Current 280°. ripple marks. signs of bottom life.
log-p295-1.spoken: Bottom camera twenty-six took six pictures. The photos showed ripple marks and signs of bottom life.

log-p295-4.caption: Water Barrel 14B: TELLTALE SLIDE INDICATES BARREL TRIPPED SOON AFTER LOWERING. SAMPLE DISCARDED
log-p295-4.spoken: Water barrel 14B tripped soon after being lowered. The sample was discarded.

sum-1967-02-16.caption: We worked about 300 nautical miles northeast of Cristobal, in the Caribbean. The day included 19 stations, with soundings of 1928 and 2143 fathoms. We saw signs of bottom life, though sediment blocked the pictures.
sum-1967-02-16.spoken: We worked about three hundred nautical miles northeast of Cristobal, in the Caribbean. The day included nineteen stations, with soundings of nineteen twenty-eight and two thousand one hundred forty-three fathoms. We saw signs of bottom life, though sediment blocked the pictures.

log-p295-5.caption: Camera 27: 5mg 6 hits. Current? ripple marks - bottom life.
log-p295-5.spoken: Bottom camera twenty-seven took six pictures. The photos showed ripple marks and bottom life.

log-p294-0.caption: Camera 18: Bottom whor to close.
log-p294-0.spoken: Camera eighteen came back with its shutter stuck open, so no pictures were taken.

log-p294-3.caption: Water Barrel 15A: Telltale slide indicates barrel tripped on way down. Sample discarded
log-p294-3.spoken: Water barrel 15A tripped on its way down. The sample was discarded.

log-p294-4.caption: Camera 28: Among 13 hits current? Bottom life, ripple marks.
log-p294-4.spoken: Camera twenty-eight took thirteen pictures of the bottom. They showed living things and ripple marks in the sediment.

day-1967-02-17.caption: Friday, February 17th, 1967. Day 32 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Miami for Cristobal.
day-1967-02-17.spoken: Good morning. It's Friday, February seventeenth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day thirty-two of the voyage, at sea, bound from Miami for Cristobal.

sum-1967-02-17.caption: We were about 200 nautical miles northeast of Balboa, in the Caribbean. The crew completed 12 stations, including 2 water-barrel samples and 2 bottom-camera lowerings. Living things and ripple marks were seen, though one sample was lost and a core was hard to extract.
sum-1967-02-17.spoken: We were about two hundred nautical miles northeast of Balboa, in the Caribbean. The crew completed twelve stations, including two water-barrel samples and two bottom-camera lowerings. Living things and ripple marks were seen, though one sample was lost and a core was hard to extract.

log-p292-0.caption: Camera 89: Gang & Lts Current? imple marks, signs of bottom life
log-p292-0.spoken: Camera eighty-nine showed simple marks and signs of bottom life. The crew wondered if a current had moved the sediment.

log-p293-5.caption: Core 33: Bedded green lutites and thixotropic sand. Penetration 934; Core length 813. Bottom topography: Flat (Columbia Basin) Difficult extrusion due to bend in pipe
log-p293-5.spoken: Piston core thirty-three was hard to push out because of a bend in the pipe. It collected bedded green lutites and thixotropic sand.

day-1967-02-18.caption: Saturday, February 18th, 1967. Day 33 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Miami for Cristobal.
day-1967-02-18.spoken: Good morning. It's Saturday, February eighteenth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day thirty-three of the voyage, at sea, bound from Miami for Cristobal.

log-p291-0.caption: Camera 30: 6 met 7 hits. Current 135° ripple marks - starfish imprint signs of bottom life
log-p291-0.spoken: Camera thirty took seven hits on six meters of film. The pictures showed ripple marks and a starfish imprint, signs of bottom life.

log-p292-3.caption: Water Barrel 16A: TELLTALE SLIDE INDICATES BARREL TRIPPED ON WAY
log-p292-3.spoken: Water barrel 16A tripped on the way down. The telltale slide showed it had closed before reaching the bottom.

sum-1967-02-18.caption: We worked about 90 nautical miles northeast of Cristobal, in the Caribbean. The sampler tripped early, but we saw a starfish imprint on the bottom.
sum-1967-02-18.spoken: We worked about ninety nautical miles northeast of Cristobal, in the Caribbean. The sampler tripped early, but we saw a starfish imprint on the bottom.

leg-V2402-end.caption: Arriving Cristobal. Log: Typical Gulf of Mexico weather (sloppy) - berthed Cristobal (transit 21st). On this leg: 3,879 miles, 436 hours under way and 39 hours on station, averaging 9.3 knots.
leg-V2402-end.spoken: Vema arrives in Cristobal. From the voyage log: Typical Gulf of Mexico weather: sloppy. Berthed at Cristobal, for the canal transit on the twenty-first. On this leg: three thousand eight hundred seventy-nine miles, four hundred thirty-six hours under way and thirty-nine hours on station, averaging nine point three knots.

day-1967-02-19.caption: Sunday, February 19th, 1967. Day 34 of the voyage, in port at Cristobal.
day-1967-02-19.spoken: Good morning. It's Sunday, February nineteenth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day thirty-four of the voyage, in port at Cristobal.

day-1967-02-20.caption: Monday, February 20th, 1967. Day 35 of the voyage, in port at Cristobal.
day-1967-02-20.spoken: Good morning. It's Monday, February twentieth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day thirty-five of the voyage, in port at Cristobal.

day-1967-02-21.caption: Tuesday, February 21st, 1967. Day 36 of the voyage, in port at Cristobal.
day-1967-02-21.spoken: Good morning. It's Tuesday, February twenty-first, nineteen sixty-seven. Day thirty-six of the voyage, in port at Cristobal.

event-1967-02-21-panama-canal.caption: Panama Canal. Transited the Panama Canal from Cristobal to Balboa (10 hours).
event-1967-02-21-panama-canal.spoken: Vema passes through the Panama Canal, from Cristobal on the Atlantic side to Balboa on the Pacific. About ten hours.

leg-V2403-start.caption: Leg 3 of 13: Balboa to Honolulu. Chief scientist J.L. Worzel.
leg-V2403-start.spoken: Leg three of thirteen begins. Vema sails from Balboa for Honolulu, with J. L. Worzel as chief scientist.

day-1967-02-22.caption: Wednesday, February 22nd, 1967. Day 37 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Balboa for Honolulu.
day-1967-02-22.spoken: Good morning. It's Wednesday, February twenty-second, nineteen sixty-seven. Day thirty-seven of the voyage, at sea, bound from Balboa for Honolulu.

log-p290-0.caption: T-Grad 22A: No RECORD
log-p290-0.spoken: Heat-flow station 22A failed to get a record.

log-p290-1.caption: Core 35: Grayish olive lutite, hard compact. Homogeneous throughout. Penetr. 231' (?) Core length 152+. Core not completely extruded on ship. Trigger core sediment disturbed & rearranged during extrusion due to faulty core catcher. Bottom topography steep slope
log-p290-1.spoken: Piston core thirty-five brought up hard, grayish olive mud. The trigger core sediment was disturbed during extrusion because the core catcher was faulty.

log-p290-2.caption: Camera 31: 6 NEG 9 HITS CURRENT. 020° Sides of bottom life. Light color of bottom.
log-p290-2.spoken: The bottom camera took six negatives. It showed life on the sides of the bottom and a light color of the sea floor.

log-p290-5.caption: Water Barrel 16: Door unlatched when it surfaced. Slide does not indicate door flapped.
log-p290-5.spoken: Water barrel sixteen surfaced with its door unlatched. The slide did not indicate the door had flapped.

log-p290-6.caption: Bio 49-V Milli 25: Very large volume + variety of planktonic organisms. Three SLs: 0-40 Fm. 110-140 Fm. 160-220 Fm.
log-p290-6.spoken: The plankton tow caught a very large volume and variety of organisms. Three sound-scattering layers were seen.

sum-1967-02-22.caption: We worked 7 stations about 100 nautical miles south of Balboa, in the North Pacific. A probe failed to record data, and a faulty core catcher disturbed sediment. We saw living things on the bottom, though a sampler door failed to latch.
sum-1967-02-22.spoken: We worked seven stations about one hundred nautical miles south of Balboa, in the North Pacific. A probe failed to record data, and a faulty core catcher disturbed sediment. We saw living things on the bottom, though a sampler door failed to latch.

day-1967-02-23.caption: Thursday, February 23rd, 1967. Day 38 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Balboa for Honolulu.
day-1967-02-23.spoken: Good morning. It's Thursday, February twenty-third, nineteen sixty-seven. Day thirty-eight of the voyage, at sea, bound from Balboa for Honolulu.

log-p289-0.caption: JN-1: The relatively large numbers of very motile animals in this initial jet-net tow suggests that avoidance may have been a significant factor in standard vertical tows taken up to this point.. Tow duration 60 min. with 100 Fm of wire out to sample surface SL, 0-50 Fm.
log-p289-0.spoken: The first jet-net tow caught large numbers of very active animals. This suggests they may have been avoiding the standard nets used earlier.

sum-1967-02-23.caption: We were about 400 nautical miles southwest of Cristobal, in the North Pacific. The crew completed 2 stations, including 1 jet-net tow. We noted unusual animal behavior.
sum-1967-02-23.spoken: We were about four hundred nautical miles southwest of Cristobal, in the North Pacific. The crew completed two stations, including one jet-net tow. We noted unusual animal behavior.

log-p289-2.caption: Core 36: Foram ooz containing 4 volcanic ash layers. Penetration 815cm, Core length 788cm. Bottom topography: ridge & valley. + Time zone change.
log-p289-2.spoken: Piston core thirty-six brought up foraminiferal ooze containing four volcanic ash layers. The sea floor there had a ridge and valley shape.

log-p289-3.caption: Camera 32: Ding. 12 hits current 315° signs of bottom life. Starfish present bottom pectin like.
log-p289-3.spoken: Bottom camera thirty-two took twelve pictures. Starfish were present on the bottom, which looked like pectin.

day-1967-02-24.caption: Friday, February 24th, 1967. Day 39 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Balboa for Honolulu.
day-1967-02-24.spoken: Good morning. It's Friday, February twenty-fourth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day thirty-nine of the voyage, at sea, bound from Balboa for Honolulu.

log-p288-0.caption: Core 33: 6mug 11 hits. current 140° mag. light. blue. It is because of dark sediment. Two bottom creatures. Have moved compass to opposite side of rig.
log-p288-0.spoken: Piston core thirty-three brought up two bottom creatures. The crew moved the compass to the other side of the rig.

sum-1967-02-24.caption: We were about 500 nautical miles west of Cristobal, in the North Pacific. The team took 14 samples and saw volcanic ash layers. Starfish and other bottom creatures were spotted, and the compass moved.
sum-1967-02-24.spoken: We were about five hundred nautical miles west of Cristobal, in the North Pacific. The team took fourteen samples and saw volcanic ash layers. Starfish and other bottom creatures were spotted, and the compass moved.

day-1967-02-25.caption: Saturday, February 25th, 1967. Day 40 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Balboa for Honolulu.
day-1967-02-25.spoken: Good morning. It's Saturday, February twenty-fifth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day forty of the voyage, at sea, bound from Balboa for Honolulu.

log-p287-3.caption: DEPHO 50: 3 mg. 14 miles - Trigger line keening up. Cement? bottom life present, bottom seems pumice like.
log-p287-3.spoken: The nephelometer tow found bottom life present. The bottom seemed pumice like.

log-p286-1.caption: Bio 54-V 55-V: Duration of tow longer than usual due to wire drifting under hull. Three SLs: 0-70 Fm, 170-200 Fm, 220-250 Fm. Middle SL consists of alternating light and dark bands 10 Fm thick. Large volumes of plankton abounding in this area.
log-p286-1.spoken: The tow ran longer than usual because the wire drifted under the hull. Large volumes of plankton abounded in the area.

log-p286-2.caption: JN-3: This was the first attempt to tow jet-net at full speed. Successful. No TDR accompanied this tow because of modifications being made in the mounting. The greater part of this tow took place after dusk and sampled heart of nighttime SL.
log-p286-2.spoken: This was the first attempt to tow the jet net at full speed, and it was successful. Most of the tow happened after dusk.

sum-1967-02-25.caption: We were about 400 nautical miles north of the Galapagos Islands, in the North Pacific. The crew completed 9 stations, including a piston core and heat-flow measurement. We saw bottom life and pumice-like bottom, along with unusual wire drift and dense plankton.
sum-1967-02-25.spoken: We were about four hundred nautical miles north of the Galapagos Islands, in the North Pacific. The crew completed nine stations, including a piston core and heat-flow measurement. We saw bottom life and pumice-like bottom, along with unusual wire drift and dense plankton.

day-1967-02-26.caption: Sunday, February 26th, 1967. Day 41 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Balboa for Honolulu.
day-1967-02-26.spoken: Good morning. It's Sunday, February twenty-sixth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day forty-one of the voyage, at sea, bound from Balboa for Honolulu.

log-p285-2.caption: Camera 35: 6 NEG HITS BOTTOM LIFE - LOTH APPARENT CURRENT 220°.
log-p285-2.spoken: Camera thirty-five got six negatives showing bottom life. An apparent current was at two hundred twenty degrees.

log-p285-0.caption: JN-4: This is the first jet-net tow to have a reliable TDR record. The sampling was at 60 Fm for a duration of 3 hrs at an average speed of 8.5 kt. The main constituents of the sample were again euphausiids.
log-p285-0.spoken: Jet net four was the first tow to have a reliable TDR record. The main catch was euphausiids.

sum-1967-02-26.caption: We worked about 400 nautical miles northwest of the Galapagos Islands in the North Pacific. The team completed 8 stations, including a heat-flow measurement of 0.69. We saw bottom life and noted a current.
sum-1967-02-26.spoken: We worked about four hundred nautical miles northwest of the Galapagos Islands in the North Pacific. The team completed eight stations, including a heat-flow measurement of zero point six nine. We saw bottom life and noted a current.

day-1967-02-27.caption: Monday, February 27th, 1967. Day 42 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Balboa for Honolulu.
day-1967-02-27.spoken: Good morning. It's Monday, February twenty-seventh, nineteen sixty-seven. Day forty-two of the voyage, at sea, bound from Balboa for Honolulu.

log-p284-3.caption: Core Camera 27: 20mg. 2 bottom shots (fails)
log-p284-3.spoken: Core camera twenty-seven took two bottom shots, but both failed.

log-p284-1.caption: Camera 36: 7mg 8hrs. Current 260° light crupling. Tension fairly coarse. - cotton life. mg. Impaired by new reflector. Shattered.
log-p284-1.spoken: Camera thirty-six was impaired by a new reflector that shattered. The current was light and the tension fairly coarse.

log-p283-0.caption: JN-5: TDR showed that depresser was separated from jet-net after about 1 hr. of towing. Wire connecting jet-net with depresser parted where copper macpress fitting had been used to make an eye. Electrolytic corrosion probably weakened wire.
log-p283-0.spoken: The jet net five lost its depresser after about one hour of towing. The wire parted where a copper fitting had been used.

sum-1967-02-27.caption: We worked 8 stations about 500 nautical miles northwest of the Galapagos Islands. The camera reflector shattered and the jet net gear broke, impairing our images and gear.
sum-1967-02-27.spoken: We worked eight stations about five hundred nautical miles northwest of the Galapagos Islands. The camera reflector shattered and the jet net gear broke, impairing our images and gear.

day-1967-02-28.caption: Tuesday, February 28th, 1967. Day 43 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Balboa for Honolulu.
day-1967-02-28.spoken: Good morning. It's Tuesday, February twenty-eighth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day forty-three of the voyage, at sea, bound from Balboa for Honolulu.

log-p282-0.caption: Camera 32: 5 wet. 8 hits. Bottom life + Tenuis - Ripple dunes. Current? Compass moved up on right side of rig to remove shadow in picture.
log-p282-0.spoken: Camera thirty-two captured ripple dunes and bottom life. The crew moved the compass to remove a shadow from the picture.

log-p284-6.caption: T-Grad 27A: NO RECORD - INSTRUMENT FLOODED
log-p284-6.spoken: Heat-flow station 27A got no record because the instrument flooded.

log-p283-2.caption: Bio 56-V 57-V: Whales + sharks observed this area. Three well-defined SLs: 0-35 Fm, 120-145 Fm, 145-265 Fm. Sampler reached into but not through middle SL. Lower SL very faint and lying just below middle SL.
log-p283-2.spoken: Whales and sharks were observed in this area. The sampler reached into the middle sound-scattering layer but did not go through it.

sum-1967-02-28.caption: In the North Pacific, the team took 14 samples at 1640 and 2065 fathoms. Whales and sharks were seen, and ripple dunes appeared on camera. One instrument flooded, and a core hit bedrock.
sum-1967-02-28.spoken: In the North Pacific, the team took fourteen samples at sixteen forty and twenty sixty-five fathoms. Whales and sharks were seen, and ripple dunes appeared on camera. One instrument flooded, and a core hit bedrock.

log-p283-5.caption: Core 42: Obsidian grading from sand at top to pebbles at bottom. Core hit bed rock. No trigger wt. core. Core length 187 cm. Bottom topography: ridge & trough. Time zone change. No RECORD - No PENETRATION
log-p283-5.spoken: Piston core forty-two hit bedrock and showed no penetration. The core length was one hundred eighty-seven centimeters, containing obsidian grading from sand to pebbles.

log-p282-3.caption: Camera 38: 13 wet. 14 hits. Current 270° sediment and. Pieces of lava. No. 142 show recent movement of lava fragments. Bottom life present.
log-p282-3.spoken: Camera thirty-eight showed pieces of lava and bottom life. Frame one hundred forty-two indicated recent movement of the lava fragments.

log-p281-0.caption: Bio 58-V: Three SLs: 0-80 Fm, 120-180 Fm, 210-250 Fm. An unusually deep SL can be seen at 380 Fm. During this station it gradually ascended.
log-p281-0.spoken: During the plankton tow, an unusually deep sound-scattering layer appeared at three hundred eighty fathoms. It gradually ascended while the station was underway.

log-p281-1.caption: Core 43: Bedded brown & pale orange lutites with pieces of obsidian present near bottom of core. Penetration 435cm. Core length 348cm. Bottom topography: ridges & troughs. Pipe penetrated through sediments and hit bedrock. Cutting edge bashed in, Pipe bent in 3 places.
log-p281-1.spoken: Piston core forty-three hit bedrock, which bashed the cutting edge and bent the pipe in three places. The core contained brown and pale orange lutites with pieces of obsidian.

log-p281-2.caption: T-Grad 27C: No RECORD - SPOOL FROZE DUE TO GEARS BINDING
log-p281-2.spoken: Heat-flow station 27C failed to record because the spool froze. The gears were binding.

log-p281-3.caption: Camera 39A: Trigger weight wrapped around compensator. Over 10 hits.
log-p281-3.spoken: Bottom camera 39A had its trigger weight wrapped around the compensator. It still took over ten hits.

day-1967-03-01.caption: Wednesday, March 1st, 1967. Day 44 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Balboa for Honolulu.
day-1967-03-01.spoken: Good morning. It's Wednesday, March first, nineteen sixty-seven. Day forty-four of the voyage, at sea, bound from Balboa for Honolulu.

log-p280-3.caption: CAMERA 37: 6 neg 8 hits. Current & suspended sediment; bottom, life present & visible
log-p280-3.spoken: Bottom camera thirty-seven took six negatives with eight hits. The pictures showed current and suspended sediment, with life present and visible on the bottom.

sum-1967-03-01.caption: In the North Pacific, the crew took 21 samples at depths of 1670 and 1842 fathoms. They saw an unusually deep scattering layer, though the corer hit bedrock and the recorder spool froze.
sum-1967-03-01.spoken: In the North Pacific, the crew took twenty-one samples at depths of sixteen seventy and eighteen forty-two fathoms. They saw an unusually deep scattering layer, though the corer hit bedrock and the recorder spool froze.

log-p279-3.caption: Camera 40: 11 neg 12 hits current 165° bottom trails & life - sediment rippled.
log-p279-3.spoken: Camera forty captured eleven negatives. The bottom showed trails and life, with rippled sediment.

log-p279-6.caption: Bio 62-1 63-1 Milli 30: Abundant squid on surface. Two SLs: 0-80 Fm. 130-160 Fm. Bone fish and euphausiids present in sample.
log-p279-6.spoken: Abundant squid were seen on the surface. Two sound-scattering layers appeared, and the sample contained bone fish and euphausiids.

log-p278-3.caption: Camera 41: 8 mg 10 hrs. Current 40° Signs of bottom life, sediment rippled
log-p278-3.spoken: Camera forty-one stayed on the bottom for ten hours. The pictures showed signs of bottom life and rippled sediment.

day-1967-03-02.caption: Thursday, March 2nd, 1967. Day 45 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Balboa for Honolulu.
day-1967-03-02.spoken: Good morning. It's Thursday, March second, nineteen sixty-seven. Day forty-five of the voyage, at sea, bound from Balboa for Honolulu.

log-p277-1.caption: Core 417: Bedded forams and vadidorian ooze. Penetration 1019cm. Core length, 817cm. Bottom topography: flat, gently sloping. Core was gaseous. Bottom part of core poured out from cutting edge when core was handled aboard. Part of this liquid was retained and stored in plastic jar.
log-p277-1.spoken: Piston core four hundred seventeen came up gaseous. Part of the liquid poured out from the cutting edge when the core was handled aboard.

log-p277-5.caption: Bio 64-V 65-V: Three SLs: 0-30 Fm, 120-160 Fm, 180-220 Fm. Two lower SLs consist of multiple dark bands. Schools of bonito + squid seen in ship's lights during station
log-p277-5.spoken: Schools of bonito and squid were seen in the ship's lights during the station. Three sound-scattering layers were recorded.

sum-1967-03-02.caption: In the North Pacific, the Vema completed 15 stations at 1934 fathoms. We saw signs of bottom life, though a gaseous core leaked during handling. Bonito and squid were also seen in the lights.
sum-1967-03-02.spoken: In the North Pacific, the Vema completed fifteen stations at nineteen thirty-four fathoms. We saw signs of bottom life, though a gaseous core leaked during handling. Bonito and squid were also seen in the lights.

day-1967-03-03.caption: Friday, March 3rd, 1967. Day 46 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Balboa for Honolulu.
day-1967-03-03.spoken: Good morning. It's Friday, March third, nineteen sixty-seven. Day forty-six of the voyage, at sea, bound from Balboa for Honolulu.

log-p276-0.caption: Camera 43: 7 NEG 10 HITS. Current 90° Variable 0.6 bottom life. Sediment is dark leaf cluttered coral trails.
log-p276-0.spoken: The camera at station forty-three caught ten hits on seven negatives. The sea floor showed dark leaf cluttered coral trails and bottom life.

log-p276-3.caption: Core 48: Bedded forams and radiolarian ooze. Penetration 780 cm. Core length 567 cm. Bottom topography hilly, with parallel sub-bottom layers. Scope entangled on compass arm. Effective length of scope reduced. Good Record - 3 probes
log-p276-3.spoken: Piston core forty-eight went seven hundred eighty centimeters into the bedded forams and radiolarian ooze. The scope became entangled on the compass arm, which reduced its effective length.

log-p275-5.caption: Sonobuoy 220: Chipping hammer fish caused large background noise. Believe redone with USA blue
log-p275-5.spoken: Sonobuoy two hundred twenty recorded large background noise from chipping hammer fish. The crew believed it was redone with USA blue.

sum-1967-03-03.caption: In the North Pacific, the crew took 7 stations at 1987 fathoms. They saw bottom life and coral trails, though a scope entanglement and fish noise caused some trouble.
sum-1967-03-03.spoken: In the North Pacific, the crew took seven stations at nineteen eighty-seven fathoms. They saw bottom life and coral trails, though a scope entanglement and fish noise caused some trouble.

day-1967-03-04.caption: Saturday, March 4th, 1967. Day 47 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Balboa for Honolulu.
day-1967-03-04.spoken: Good morning. It's Saturday, March fourth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day forty-seven of the voyage, at sea, bound from Balboa for Honolulu.

log-p275-3.caption: CAMERA 44A: Trigger Wt Hung up on way down. Came up 8 fms
log-p275-3.spoken: Camera 44A had its trigger weight hang up on the way down. It came up eight fathoms.

log-p274-5.caption: Bio 66-V: Flowmeter #1452 showed eccentric reading on 67-V. Two SLs: 0-45 Fm, 190-250 Fm. One specimen of Phronema sedentaria (amphipod) was using its transparent cylindrical case as a perambulator for transporting it's larval young. (Rarely preserved intact in vertical tows.)
log-p274-5.spoken: A flowmeter gave an eccentric reading during the tow. One amphipod was seen using its transparent case to carry its larval young, a rare sight.

sum-1967-03-04.caption: We worked in the North Pacific at 2054 fathoms, completing 17 stations. A trigger weight hung up, and a camera returned upside down. We also saw a rare amphipod with young.
sum-1967-03-04.spoken: We worked in the North Pacific at twenty fifty-four fathoms, completing seventeen stations. A trigger weight hung up, and a camera returned upside down. We also saw a rare amphipod with young.

log-p273-0.caption: Core 50: Bedded ooze and radiolarian ooze. Penetration 1010 cm. Core length 1800 cm. Good core: 617 cm. Bottom topography: hilly rolling. Pipe bent opp. 35°. Mud present on piston of core.
log-p273-0.spoken: Piston core fifty came up with its pipe bent thirty-five degrees. Mud was present on the piston of the core.

log-p274-2.caption: Camera 44B: Amg. 8 hits - camera returned upside down.
log-p274-2.spoken: Camera 44B got eight hits, but it came back upside down.

day-1967-03-05.caption: Sunday, March 5th, 1967. Day 48 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Balboa for Honolulu.
day-1967-03-05.spoken: Good morning. It's Sunday, March fifth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day forty-eight of the voyage, at sea, bound from Balboa for Honolulu.

log-p272-0.caption: Core 51A: Messenger did not trip core cutting device. No piston core. Trigger core length: 49cm. Trigger core is a foran & radiolarian ooze. Bottom topography: hilly rolling. Pipe bent app. 40°
log-p272-0.spoken: The messenger failed to trip the cutting device at Core 51A, so no piston core was taken. The trigger core was forty-nine centimeters long, and the pipe was bent about forty degrees.

log-p272-1.caption: Water barrel #32A: Core did not trigger hence no water barrel sample:
log-p272-1.spoken: Water barrel 32A did not close because the core did not trigger. Consequently, no water sample was collected.

log-p273-5.caption: Core Camera 38: Shows cable hooked on core pipe.
log-p273-5.spoken: Core camera thirty-eight showed the cable hooked on the core pipe.

log-p272-2.caption: Bio 68-5F 69-5F: Fast current prevented use of vertical net. Two dark SLs: 0-50Fm, 160-200Fm. Large volumes of plankton in usual proportions encountered at surface.
log-p272-2.spoken: A fast current prevented the use of the vertical net during Bio sixty-eight-5F and sixty-nine-5F. Large volumes of plankton were encountered at the surface.

sum-1967-03-05.caption: In the North Pacific, the crew took 9 samples at 2167 fathoms. A cable hooked on the core pipe, bending it and causing the sampler to fail. The current also prevented the net from being used.
sum-1967-03-05.spoken: In the North Pacific, the crew took nine samples at two thousand one hundred sixty-seven fathoms. A cable hooked on the core pipe, bending it and causing the sampler to fail. The current also prevented the net from being used.

day-1967-03-06.caption: Monday, March 6th, 1967. Day 49 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Balboa for Honolulu.
day-1967-03-06.spoken: Good morning. It's Monday, March sixth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day forty-nine of the voyage, at sea, bound from Balboa for Honolulu.

log-p271-6.caption: Camera 45A: Omg 6 hits. Trigger cable hung up.
log-p271-6.spoken: Camera 45A took six hits. The trigger cable hung up.

log-p271-0.caption: Water barrel 32B.: Core closed prematurely thus no sample.
log-p271-0.spoken: Water barrel 32B closed too early, so no sample was taken.

sum-1967-03-06.caption: In the North Pacific, the crew took 9 samples at depths of 2361 and 2475 fathoms. Some gear failed, including a lost sample and a bent pipe, but the team kept working.
sum-1967-03-06.spoken: In the North Pacific, the crew took nine samples at depths of two thousand three hundred sixty-one and two thousand four hundred seventy-five fathoms. Some gear failed, including a lost sample and a bent pipe, but the team kept working.

log-p271-3.caption: Core 52A: No piston core. Messenger did not arm tripping mechanism because trip arm was bent. Trigger core length 39cm. containing a radiolarian ooze. Pipe bent, cutting edge good. Bottom topography, hilly, rolling with multiple sub-bottom reflections NO RECORD
log-p271-3.spoken: Piston core 52A failed because the trip arm was bent. The trigger core held thirty-nine centimeters of radiolarian ooze.

log-p271-5.caption: Water barrel #32C: Core did not trigger thus barrel did not close. no sample.
log-p271-5.spoken: Water barrel 32C did not close because the core did not trigger. No sample was taken.

day-1967-03-07.caption: Tuesday, March 7th, 1967. Day 50 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Balboa for Honolulu.
day-1967-03-07.spoken: Good morning. It's Tuesday, March seventh, nineteen sixty-seven. Day fifty of the voyage, at sea, bound from Balboa for Honolulu.

log-p269-0.caption: CORE 52B: No piston core. Messenger did not trip triggering mechanism (spring too stiff). Trigger core length 38cm. containing a radiolarian core. Pipe bent cutting edge good. Bottom topography lilly rolling with multiple sub-bottom reflections
log-p269-0.spoken: The piston core failed because the spring was too stiff, so only a thirty-eight centimeter trigger core came up. The pipe was bent, and the bottom had rolling topography with multiple sub-bottom reflections.

log-p268-3.caption: Bio 72-V: Fouled with camera wire. Relative positions of Bio and camera wires were safe until net was at about 60Fm. Apparently a surface current moving contrary to the deeper water carried Bio net into camera wire. Neither wire was damaged. Two SLs: 0-50Fm, 160-240Fm.
log-p268-3.spoken: Bio seventy-two-V got fouled with the camera wire because a surface current carried the net into it. Neither wire was damaged.

log-p268-1.caption: Core 52C: No piston core. Messenger did not arm tripping mechanism. Trigger core length 38cm. containing a radiolarian ooze. Pipe bent, cutting edge speed. Bottom topography: hilly, rolling with multiple sub-bottom reflections
log-p268-1.spoken: Piston core 52C failed to trigger, and the pipe came up bent. The trigger core was thirty-eight centimeters long and contained radiolarian ooze.

log-p268-2.caption: Water barrel 32E: Core did not trigger but water barrel closed prematurely on the way down.
log-p268-2.spoken: Water barrel 32E closed prematurely on the way down. The core did not trigger.

sum-1967-03-07.caption: Aboard Vema in the North Pacific, the team completed 13 stations. They faced challenges like a bent pipe and a fouled net, but gathered core samples and camera footage from depths of 2438 and 2492 fathoms.
sum-1967-03-07.spoken: Aboard Vema in the North Pacific, the team completed thirteen stations. They faced challenges like a bent pipe and a fouled net, but gathered core samples and camera footage from depths of two thousand four hundred thirty-eight and two thousand four hundred ninety-two fathoms.

day-1967-03-08.caption: Wednesday, March 8th, 1967. Day 51 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Balboa for Honolulu.
day-1967-03-08.spoken: Good morning. It's Wednesday, March eighth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day fifty-one of the voyage, at sea, bound from Balboa for Honolulu.

log-p267-4.caption: DEPHO 49: Can not make reading
log-p267-4.spoken: The nephelometer at station forty-nine could not make a reading.

sum-1967-03-08.caption: We worked in the North Pacific at 2394 fathoms. Eleven stations included cores, heat-flow readings, and a jet-net tow. An instrument failed to read, but the catch included squid and fish.
sum-1967-03-08.spoken: We worked in the North Pacific at two thousand three hundred ninety-four fathoms. Eleven stations included cores, heat-flow readings, and a jet-net tow. An instrument failed to read, but the catch included squid and fish.

log-p266-3.caption: JN-9: JN-9 was towed through the night time surface SL for 3hr 11min, averaging 9.6 Kt. It yielded a large volume of nekton-plankton, including squid, numerous teleosts, and large euphausiids.
log-p266-3.spoken: Jet net nine was towed through the night surface layer for three hours and eleven minutes. It caught a large volume of nekton-plankton, including squid, numerous teleosts, and large euphausiids.

day-1967-03-09.caption: Thursday, March 9th, 1967. Day 52 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Balboa for Honolulu.
day-1967-03-09.spoken: Good morning. It's Thursday, March ninth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day fifty-two of the voyage, at sea, bound from Balboa for Honolulu.

log-p266-4.caption: Water barrel #33A: Water barrel did not close

log-p263-2.caption: Camera 48: 5mg. Photo Current. 045° Signs of bottom life - Sediment grading.
log-p263-2.spoken: Camera forty-eight took five frames. The photos showed signs of bottom life and sediment grading.

log-p263-4.caption: Core Camera 45: 29mg 2 bottomings. Cable wrapped around core pipe.
log-p263-4.spoken: Core camera forty-five recorded two bottomings. The cable wrapped around the core pipe.

log-p265-0.caption: JN-10: This was a 3hr 13min tow at 9.5 kt. which sampled the surface SL before + after the dusk migrations. Vast numbers of organisms taken - primarily phytoplankton with a high proportion of pteropods + polychaet worms.
log-p265-0.spoken: The jet net tow lasted three hours and thirteen minutes at nine point five knots. It caught vast numbers of organisms, including phytoplankton, pteropods, and polychaet worms.

sum-1967-03-09.caption: In the North Pacific, the crew took 7 samples at 2400 fathoms. A sampler failed to close, and a cable wrapped around the core pipe. They saw vast numbers of organisms during dusk migration and signs of bottom life.
sum-1967-03-09.spoken: In the North Pacific, the crew took seven samples at two thousand four hundred fathoms. A sampler failed to close, and a cable wrapped around the core pipe. They saw vast numbers of organisms during dusk migration and signs of bottom life.

day-1967-03-10.caption: Friday, March 10th, 1967. Day 53 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Balboa for Honolulu.
day-1967-03-10.spoken: Good morning. It's Friday, March tenth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day fifty-three of the voyage, at sea, bound from Balboa for Honolulu.

log-p265-6.caption: Water Barrel #33 B: Barrel returned to surface open, Lanyard used to close barrel parted but single martin used to prevent premature closing did not part.
log-p265-6.spoken: Water barrel thirty-three B returned to the surface open. The lanyard used to close it parted, but the single martin did not.

log-p264-2.caption: Bio 73-V 74-V: At the time of this sampling, extremely dense schools of fish appeared on the PDR at about 170 Fm. These dark parabolic masses seemed to be independent of the existing horizontal SLs: 0-40 Fm, 160-220 Fm.
log-p264-2.spoken: During the plankton tows, extremely dense schools of fish showed up on the echo sounder, at about one hundred seventy fathoms. These dark masses seemed independent of the existing horizontal sound-scattering layers.

log-p264-0.caption: Sonobuoy 23: Brits noisy. Some topography trouble.
log-p264-0.spoken: Sonobuoy twenty-three had noisy brits and some topography trouble.

sum-1967-03-10.caption: In the North Pacific, the Vema took 16 samples at depths of 2238 and 2318 fathoms. A lanyard parted, and noisy equipment caused trouble. Yet, dense fish schools and signs of bottom life were seen.
sum-1967-03-10.spoken: In the North Pacific, the Vema took sixteen samples at depths of two thousand two hundred thirty-eight and two thousand three hundred eighteen fathoms. A lanyard parted, and noisy equipment caused trouble. Yet, dense fish schools and signs of bottom life were seen.

log-p264-4.caption: Camera 50: 9 mg/1/2 hrs. Current 100° Signs of bottom life, sediment rippled.
log-p264-4.spoken: Camera fifty took nine frames in half an hour. It showed signs of bottom life, and the sediment was rippled.

day-1967-03-11.caption: Saturday, March 11th, 1967. Day 54 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Balboa for Honolulu.
day-1967-03-11.spoken: Good morning. It's Saturday, March eleventh, nineteen sixty-seven. Day fifty-four of the voyage, at sea, bound from Balboa for Honolulu.

log-p263-5.caption: Sonobuoy 47: Noisy - Refractions very doubtful
log-p263-5.spoken: Sonobuoy forty-seven recorded noisy data. The refractions were very doubtful.

log-p262-1.caption: Camera 57: 11 mar 13 kilo Current 2750. Signs of bottom life; sediment ripples.
log-p262-1.spoken: The bottom camera at station fifty-seven showed signs of bottom life and sediment ripples.

log-p262-5.caption: Bio 75-MPS: This initial core MPS sampled all SL visible on PDR: 0-50, 70-120. Third (shallow) net failed to open completely causing some contamination of "middle" net with "shallow" plankton. Also, wind destroyed shallow flowmeter reading.
log-p262-5.spoken: The shallow net failed to open completely, contaminating the middle net. Wind also destroyed the shallow flowmeter reading.

sum-1967-03-11.caption: In the North Pacific, the Vema took 9 stations at 2270 fathoms. We saw signs of bottom life, though noisy data and a net failure made the day tricky.
sum-1967-03-11.spoken: In the North Pacific, the Vema took nine stations at two thousand two hundred seventy fathoms. We saw signs of bottom life, though noisy data and a net failure made the day tricky.

day-1967-03-12.caption: Sunday, March 12th, 1967. Day 55 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Balboa for Honolulu.
day-1967-03-12.spoken: Good morning. It's Sunday, March twelfth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day fifty-five of the voyage, at sea, bound from Balboa for Honolulu.

log-p261-2.caption: Camera 57A: Omg O hits. didn't hit bottom.
log-p261-2.spoken: Camera 57A did not hit the bottom, so it got no pictures.

log-p260-0.caption: Bio 75: This net and core MPS sampled all SLs from 548 Fm -> surface. The shallow net failed to open completely, so that it received only 1/4 of its sample, the other 3/4 contaminating the middle net
log-p260-0.spoken: The shallow net for Bio seventy-five failed to open completely. It caught only one/four of its sample, and the rest contaminated the middle net.

sum-1967-03-12.caption: In the North Pacific, the crew took 9 stations at 2395 fathoms. The camera failed to hit the bottom, and the net failed to open, leaving the sample contaminated.
