sum-1967-03-12.spoken: In the North Pacific, the crew took nine stations at two thousand three hundred ninety-five fathoms. The camera failed to hit the bottom, and the net failed to open, leaving the sample contaminated.

day-1967-03-13.caption: Monday, March 13th, 1967. Day 57 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Balboa for Honolulu.
day-1967-03-13.spoken: Good morning. It's Monday, March thirteenth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day fifty-seven of the voyage, at sea, bound from Balboa for Honolulu.

log-p257-5.caption: JN 13: This tow was intended to sample beneath the surface SL, but by the end of the tow, the SL had increased in thickness by 40Fm, so that the JN was in the SL during the last few minutes. Very few plankton taken.
log-p257-5.spoken: Jet net thirteen was meant to sample beneath the surface layer. The layer thickened by forty fathoms, so the net ended up inside it.

sum-1967-03-13.caption: In the North Pacific, we took 7 samples at 2483 fathoms. The net entered a thickening layer. We also lowered a camera and sonobuoy.
sum-1967-03-13.spoken: In the North Pacific, we took seven samples at two thousand four hundred eighty-three fathoms. The net entered a thickening layer. We also lowered a camera and sonobuoy.

day-1967-03-14.caption: Tuesday, March 14th, 1967. Day 58 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Balboa for Honolulu.
day-1967-03-14.spoken: Good morning. It's Tuesday, March fourteenth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day fifty-eight of the voyage, at sea, bound from Balboa for Honolulu.

log-p259-0.caption: Core 60: Extensively burrowed and mottled silicious ooze. Age: Pliocene Penetration 1885cm, core length 1786, good core 1314cm. Bottom topography hilly with highly stratified, undulating sub-bottom GOOD RECORD 3 PROBES
log-p259-0.spoken: Piston core sixty brought up extensively burrowed silicious ooze, dated to the Pliocene. The bottom topography was hilly with highly stratified, undulating sub-bottom.

log-p259-3.caption: Core Camera 49: 29 mg. no bottom pictures
log-p259-3.spoken: Core camera forty-nine did not get any bottom pictures.

log-p258-0.caption: Core 61: Silicious core containing manganese pebble layer at bottom of Unit P. pe broken between 2nd & 3rd couple. Penetration 607cm, core length 344cm. Bottom topography: hilly with basement nearing top of undulating sediments. 13mug 14'lite. Current 270°. Signs of bottom life present.
log-p258-0.spoken: Piston core sixty-one broke between the second and third coupling. It contained a manganese pebble layer and signs of bottom life.

log-p259-6.caption: T-Grad 46A: NO RECORD - INSTRUMENT FLOODED THROUGH PASS - TARN
log-p259-6.spoken: Heat-flow station 46A got no record because the instrument flooded through the pass.

log-p258-4.caption: Water Barrel #38A: Barrel closed on the way down.
log-p258-4.spoken: Water barrel 38A closed on the way down.

sum-1967-03-14.caption: We worked in the North Pacific, taking 14 samples and measurements. The bottom was hilly with Pliocene age, and we found manganese and bottom life in a broken core. No pictures were taken because an instrument flooded.
sum-1967-03-14.spoken: We worked in the North Pacific, taking fourteen samples and measurements. The bottom was hilly with Pliocene age, and we found manganese and bottom life in a broken core. No pictures were taken because an instrument flooded.

day-1967-03-15.caption: Wednesday, March 15th, 1967. Day 59 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Balboa for Honolulu.
day-1967-03-15.spoken: Good morning. It's Wednesday, March fifteenth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day fifty-nine of the voyage, at sea, bound from Balboa for Honolulu.

log-p257-1.caption: Core Camera 53: 34mg. no bottom hits Shake trigger cable over compus arm.
log-p257-1.spoken: Core camera fifty-three took thirty-four frames but got no bottom hits. The trigger cable shook over the compass arm.

log-p258-5.caption: Core 62 A: Piston pipe and trigger core did not retain any sediment. Penetration 704cm.
log-p258-5.spoken: Piston core sixty-two A and its trigger core did not retain any sediment.

sum-1967-03-15.caption: In the North Pacific, the crew took 15 samples at 2570 and 2686 fathoms. They saw signs of bottom life, though the camera failed to trip and sediment collection was unsuccessful.
sum-1967-03-15.spoken: In the North Pacific, the crew took fifteen samples at two thousand five hundred seventy and two thousand six hundred eighty-six fathoms. They saw signs of bottom life, though the camera failed to trip and sediment collection was unsuccessful.

log-p255-0.caption: Bio 79-V 80-V: Three SLs: 0-60, 60-100, 170-220F. Surface SL intensity diminishes with increasing depth, so that it merges with lighter middle SL. This tow sampled the 2 upper SLs in their entirety, and yielded a fine variety of marine organisms.
log-p255-0.spoken: The tow sampled the upper sound-scattering layers and found a fine variety of marine organisms.

log-p256-3.caption: CAMERA 56: 8mg 9 hits Current? signs of bottom life.
log-p256-3.spoken: Bottom camera fifty-six took nine hits. The photos showed signs of bottom life.

log-p256-4.caption: CORE CAMERA 54A: DIDN'T TRIP
log-p256-4.spoken: Core camera 54A did not trip, so no pictures were taken.

day-1967-03-16.caption: Thursday, March 16th, 1967. Day 60 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Balboa for Honolulu.
day-1967-03-16.spoken: Good morning. It's Thursday, March sixteenth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day sixty of the voyage, at sea, bound from Balboa for Honolulu.

log-p254-0.caption: CORE 63A: No sediment retained in core, Penetration 1707cm. Pipe broken at top of 2nd pipe, 1st pipe slightly bent. 30cc. of sediment retained on outside of core by first thermograph probe. Silicious calcareous ooze. Age: Miocene
log-p254-0.spoken: Piston core 63A came up with a broken pipe and no sediment inside. It had penetrated seventeen oh-seven centimeters into the floor.

log-p254-1.caption: Water Barrel #39A: Barrel did not close, hence no sample. Core trigger wire caught around compass and prevented proper triggering at Core Core however did trigger.
log-p254-1.spoken: Water barrel 39A did not close because the trigger wire caught on the compass. The core still triggered, but the water sample was lost.

log-p255-3.caption: CAMERA 57A: Towing Cable hung up.
log-p255-3.spoken: The towing cable for the bottom camera hung up.

log-p255-4.caption: CORE CAMERA 54: 29mgs. Trigger weight wrapped around anchor arm. 0.8m. is broken off at hit
log-p255-4.spoken: The trigger weight wrapped around the anchor arm, and zero point eight meters of the gear broke off.

log-p255-6.caption: T-GRAD 48A: No RECORD - No PENETRATION
log-p255-6.spoken: The heat-flow probe at station 48A got no record because it did not penetrate the sea floor.

sum-1967-03-16.caption: In the North Pacific, the crew completed 16 stations. They faced a hung cable and a broken trigger weight. A probe failed to penetrate, and a broken pipe lost the sediment.
sum-1967-03-16.spoken: In the North Pacific, the crew completed sixteen stations. They faced a hung cable and a broken trigger weight. A probe failed to penetrate, and a broken pipe lost the sediment.

log-p253-3.caption: Bio 81-V 82-V: Two SLs: 0-100 Fm, 220-280 Fm. Extremely dark upper SL yielded a large and varied sample, representing nearly all types of planktonic life. Unusually large numbers of gelatinous eggs present.
log-p253-3.spoken: The dark upper layer gave a large, varied plankton sample. It had unusually large numbers of gelatinous eggs.

day-1967-03-17.caption: Friday, March 17th, 1967. Day 61 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Balboa for Honolulu.
day-1967-03-17.spoken: Good morning. It's Friday, March seventeenth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day sixty-one of the voyage, at sea, bound from Balboa for Honolulu.

log-p252-0.caption: Camera 58: 10 ang 1 Milts. Current 315° 100 ftn. Camera covered with organisms of bottom life.
log-p252-0.spoken: Camera fifty-eight came back covered with organisms of bottom life. The current was three hundred fifteen degrees at one hundred feet.

log-p252-3.caption: Water Barrel #40A: Barrel did not close. Surface closed open. No sample.
log-p252-3.spoken: Water barrel 40A did not close. The surface closed open, so there was no sample.

log-p253-6.caption: CORE 64: Bedded calcareous ooze, sand and gravel. Age Recent. Penetration 642 cm, core length 530 cm. good core 311 cm. Pipe broken at top of crust. Pipe below topography at base of outcropping peak. Highly stratified, including seams.
log-p253-6.spoken: Piston core sixty-four hit bedded calcareous ooze, sand, and gravel. The pipe broke at the top of the crust.

log-p253-4.caption: JN-16: Lost depressor due to parted cable. 2 Fair refractions
log-p253-4.spoken: Jet net sixteen lost its depressor because the cable parted. It got two fair refractions.

sum-1967-03-17.caption: In the North Pacific, the Vema took 8 samples at 2102 fathoms. We lost gear to a cable break and a broken pipe, but the camera found bottom life. One sampler failed, so we got no sample.
sum-1967-03-17.spoken: In the North Pacific, the Vema took eight samples at two thousand one hundred two fathoms. We lost gear to a cable break and a broken pipe, but the camera found bottom life. One sampler failed, so we got no sample.

sum-1967-03-18.caption: We worked in the North Pacific. The ship took 6 samples at 2510 fathoms. This included a piston core and a heat-flow measurement.
sum-1967-03-18.spoken: We worked in the North Pacific. The ship took six samples at two thousand five hundred ten fathoms. This included a piston core and a heat-flow measurement.

day-1967-03-19.caption: Sunday, March 19th, 1967. Day 63 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Balboa for Honolulu.
day-1967-03-19.spoken: Good morning. It's Sunday, March nineteenth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day sixty-three of the voyage, at sea, bound from Balboa for Honolulu.

log-p250-1.caption: Core 66: Bedded lutites overlying radiolarian ooze. Age Eocene. Penetration 1625cm. Core length 2017cm. Good core 1577cm. Bottom topography: hilly with small peak. Pipe bent at 30°
log-p250-1.spoken: Piston core sixty-six brought up bedded lutites over radiolarian ooze, dated to the Eocene. The pipe was bent at thirty degrees, and the core length was twenty seventeen centimeters.

log-p250-2.caption: Water barrel #41A: Barrel failed to close returned to surface open.
log-p250-2.spoken: Water barrel 41A failed to close and returned to the surface open.

log-p250-3.caption: Bio 85-V 86-V: Three SLs: 0-60, 60-80, 180-280 Fm. Surface SL, consisting of parabolic traces, unusually thick + dark for daytime SL. Plankton numbers and variety increased.
log-p250-3.spoken: During the plankton tows, the surface sound-scattering layer was unusually thick and dark for daytime. Plankton numbers and variety increased.

log-p251-5.caption: Camera 60: 13 mg 15 hits Current 250° Starfish krill present
log-p251-5.spoken: Camera sixty took fifteen hits. Starfish and krill were present on the bottom.

log-p250-6.caption: Camera 61: 14 neg 19 hits. Current? Bottom covered with manganese nodules.
log-p250-6.spoken: Camera sixty-one took fourteen negatives with nineteen hits. The bottom was covered with manganese nodules.

log-p249-2.caption: Core 67: Lute bedded lutite and radiolarian ooze. Age Eocene. Penetration 706cm. Core length 532cm. Good core. 484cm. Broken pipe resulted in loss of sediment above 1st pipe. Difficult extrusion reduced good core length. Bottom topography: rolling, highly stratified seds. Two poor refractions
log-p249-2.spoken: Piston core sixty-seven hit a broken pipe, which caused the loss of sediment above the first pipe. The core contained lutite and radiolarian ooze from the Eocene age.

log-p249-5.caption: Bio 87-V: Two SLs: 0-80, 160-900 Fm. Surface SL very dark. Several new species of amphipod appear in this sample. One type possesses large, heavily pigmented eyes, flattened, crescent-shaped pleopods, and pigment spots on transparent carapace. Masses of eggs also present.
log-p249-5.spoken: The plankton tow found several new species of amphipod. One type had large, heavily pigmented eyes and flattened, crescent-shaped pleopods.

sum-1967-03-19.caption: In the North Pacific, we took 16 samples at 2803 fathoms. We saw living things on camera and recovered a bent pipe with an Eocene age core. The water sampler failed to close, but we noted an unusually thick daytime scattering layer.
sum-1967-03-19.spoken: In the North Pacific, we took sixteen samples at two thousand eight hundred three fathoms. We saw living things on camera and recovered a bent pipe with an Eocene age core. The water sampler failed to close, but we noted an unusually thick daytime scattering layer.

day-1967-03-20.caption: Monday, March 20th, 1967. Day 64 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Balboa for Honolulu.
day-1967-03-20.spoken: Good morning. It's Monday, March twentieth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day sixty-four of the voyage, at sea, bound from Balboa for Honolulu.

log-p248-0.caption: Core 68: Radiolarian ooze overlying lutite Age Eocene. Penetration 607cm, Core length 605cm, good core 405cm. Piston core had "sidescar" attached to it. Pipe bent 930° cutting edge bashed in. Bottom topography: flat, rolling
log-p248-0.spoken: Piston core sixty-eight came up with a bent pipe and a bashed cutting edge. It had penetrated six hundred seven centimeters into the sea floor.

sum-1967-03-20.caption: We were about 500 nautical miles south of the Hawaiian Islands, in the North Pacific. The day brought 14 stations, including 2 heat-flow measurements and 2 piston cores. We faced a damaged corer and a camera that returned upside down, but also enjoyed a new rig and an unusual catch.
sum-1967-03-20.spoken: We were about five hundred nautical miles south of the Hawaiian Islands, in the North Pacific. The day brought fourteen stations, including two heat-flow measurements and two piston cores. We faced a damaged corer and a camera that returned upside down, but also enjoyed a new rig and an unusual catch.

log-p247-1.caption: Camera 63A: Camera returned upside down.
log-p247-1.spoken: Camera 63A came back from the deep upside down.

log-p247-3.caption: Bio 88 89: New vertical rig. SL's extremely dark and more or less continuous down to 220 Fm, however less plankton taken than would be expected. Ostracods + arrow worms reappearing. Few representatives of the encarida.
log-p247-3.spoken: A new vertical rig was used for the plankton tows. The sound-scattering layer was extremely dark and continuous down to two hundred twenty fathoms, but less plankton was taken than expected.

day-1967-03-21.caption: Tuesday, March 21st, 1967. Day 65 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Balboa for Honolulu.
day-1967-03-21.spoken: Good morning. It's Tuesday, March twenty-first, nineteen sixty-seven. Day sixty-five of the voyage, at sea, bound from Balboa for Honolulu.

log-p246-0.caption: Core 70: Two dark sand layers in an otherwise structureless and homogeneous brown lutite. Penetration 551cm. Core length 911cm. Pipe bent below 186 cm. Couple. Bottom topography: hilly, with subbottom sediments outcropping on surface. 16mwa DHIS Current 280°
log-p246-0.spoken: Piston core seventy came up with its pipe bent below one hundred eighty-six centimeters. The sea floor was hilly, with sediments outcropping on the surface.

log-p246-1.caption: Camera 63: LOT YOUNG STAGES OF ROTOUN LIFE. BOTTOM RIPPLED MORE THAN OTHERS.
log-p246-1.spoken: Camera sixty-three photographed young stages of rotoun life. The bottom was rippled more than at other stations.

sum-1967-03-21.caption: We were about 400 nautical miles south of the Hawaiian Islands in the North Pacific. The crew took 8 samples and found a bent pipe with unusual bottom topography. Young life forms were seen on the camera.
sum-1967-03-21.spoken: We were about four hundred nautical miles south of the Hawaiian Islands in the North Pacific. The crew took eight samples and found a bent pipe with unusual bottom topography. Young life forms were seen on the camera.

day-1967-03-22.caption: Wednesday, March 22nd, 1967. Day 66 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Balboa for Honolulu.
day-1967-03-22.spoken: Good morning. It's Wednesday, March twenty-second, nineteen sixty-seven. Day sixty-six of the voyage, at sea, bound from Balboa for Honolulu.

leg-V2403-end.caption: Arriving Honolulu. Log: Proceeded along Lats. 1-5 degs. to approx. 150W. All good weather. On this leg: 6,062 miles, 612 hours under way and 94 hours on station, averaging 9.7 knots.
leg-V2403-end.spoken: Vema arrives in Honolulu. From the voyage log: Proceeded along latitudes one to five degrees north, to about one hundred fifty degrees west. All good weather. On this leg: six thousand sixty-two miles, six hundred twelve hours under way and ninety-four hours on station, averaging nine point seven knots.

day-1967-03-23.caption: Thursday, March 23rd, 1967. Day 67 of the voyage, in port at Honolulu.
day-1967-03-23.spoken: Good morning. It's Thursday, March twenty-third, nineteen sixty-seven. Day sixty-seven of the voyage, in port at Honolulu.

day-1967-03-24.caption: Friday, March 24th, 1967. Day 68 of the voyage, in port at Honolulu.
day-1967-03-24.spoken: Good morning. It's Friday, March twenty-fourth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day sixty-eight of the voyage, in port at Honolulu.

day-1967-03-25.caption: Saturday, March 25th, 1967. Day 69 of the voyage, in port at Honolulu.
day-1967-03-25.spoken: Good morning. It's Saturday, March twenty-fifth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day sixty-nine of the voyage, in port at Honolulu.

day-1967-03-26.caption: Sunday, March 26th, 1967. Day 70 of the voyage, in port at Honolulu.
day-1967-03-26.spoken: Good morning. It's Sunday, March twenty-sixth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day seventy of the voyage, in port at Honolulu.

day-1967-03-27.caption: Monday, March 27th, 1967. Day 71 of the voyage, in port at Honolulu.
day-1967-03-27.spoken: Good morning. It's Monday, March twenty-seventh, nineteen sixty-seven. Day seventy-one of the voyage, in port at Honolulu.

leg-V2404-start.caption: Leg 4 of 13: Honolulu to Midway. Chief scientist G.M. Bryan.
leg-V2404-start.spoken: Leg four of thirteen begins. Vema sails from Honolulu for Midway, with G. M. Bryan as chief scientist.

day-1967-03-28.caption: Tuesday, March 28th, 1967. Day 72 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Honolulu for Midway.
day-1967-03-28.spoken: Good morning. It's Tuesday, March twenty-eighth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day seventy-two of the voyage, at sea, bound from Honolulu for Midway.

log-p245-3.caption: Camera 61A: Camera returned upside down. adding weights.
log-p245-3.spoken: Camera 61A came back upside down. The crew added weights to fix it.

log-p245-0.caption: Core M1: Core could not be extruded aboard ship. Penetration 298cm. Pipe bent 6' below. Just couple. Bottom topography: gently rolling hills with moderately stratified undulating sediments. GOOD RECORD - 2 PROBES
log-p245-0.spoken: Piston core M1 could not be pushed out of the pipe because it was bent. It had gone two hundred ninety-eight centimeters into the sea floor.

log-p245-6.caption: Bio 90-V 91-V: Unusual SL configuration. Sound scattering confined to upper 120m. Intensity, medium. Small volume of sample indicates plankton-poor waters.
log-p245-6.spoken: The sound scattering layer was unusual, confined to the upper one hundred twenty meters. The small sample showed the waters were poor in plankton.

sum-1967-03-28.caption: We worked about 200 nautical miles southwest of Honolulu in the North Pacific. The core stuck in a bent pipe, and the camera returned upside down. We also found an unusual sound scattering layer.
sum-1967-03-28.spoken: We worked about two hundred nautical miles southwest of Honolulu in the North Pacific. The core stuck in a bent pipe, and the camera returned upside down. We also found an unusual sound scattering layer.

day-1967-03-29.caption: Wednesday, March 29th, 1967. Day 73 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Honolulu for Midway.
day-1967-03-29.spoken: Good morning. It's Wednesday, March twenty-ninth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day seventy-three of the voyage, at sea, bound from Honolulu for Midway.

log-p244-3.caption: Camera 61: Smooth sediment - appears to be sediment in water, pictures blurry from sediment; little sign of bottom life.
log-p244-3.spoken: Camera sixty-one saw smooth sediment, but the pictures were blurry from sediment in the water. There was little sign of bottom life.

log-p244-1.caption: Core 72: Structureless brown lutite Penetration 607cm. Core length 532cm. Bottom topography: very hilly with highly stratified bottom beds. Pipe bent, piston caught before bend in pipe. GOOD RECORD - 3 PROBES
log-p244-1.spoken: Piston core seventy-two went six hundred seven centimeters into the floor, but the pipe bent. The piston caught before the bend, and the core length was five hundred thirty-two centimeters.

log-p244-5.caption: Core Camera 63A: Trigger pin not removed.
log-p244-5.spoken: Core camera 63A failed because the trigger pin was not removed.

log-p243-0.caption: 92-CMPS: All nets triggered properly, but event marker attached to TDR failed to record opening of middle + shallow nets. Deep net opened at 927m, and was recorded by event marker.
log-p243-0.spoken: The event marker failed to record the opening of the middle and shallow nets. The deep net opened at nine hundred twenty-seven meters and was recorded.

sum-1967-03-29.caption: We were about 400 nautical miles southwest of Honolulu, in the North Pacific. The pipe bent and the piston caught. Pictures were blurry with little life. The trigger pin was not removed. The event marker failed to record net opening.
sum-1967-03-29.spoken: We were about four hundred nautical miles southwest of Honolulu, in the North Pacific. The pipe bent and the piston caught. Pictures were blurry with little life. The trigger pin was not removed. The event marker failed to record net opening.

day-1967-03-30.caption: Thursday, March 30th, 1967. Day 74 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Honolulu for Midway.
day-1967-03-30.spoken: Good morning. It's Thursday, March thirtieth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day seventy-four of the voyage, at sea, bound from Honolulu for Midway.

log-p242-4.caption: Camera 65: 7mug. 840mug. opal blue. Because of turbulent water, disc. from view. No rock on bottom left
log-p242-4.spoken: Camera sixty-five found the water too turbulent to see the bottom clearly. No rock was left on the sea floor.

sum-1967-03-30.caption: In the North Pacific, we took 14 samples at 2813 fathoms. The water was turbulent, which obscured our view.
sum-1967-03-30.spoken: In the North Pacific, we took fourteen samples at two thousand eight hundred thirteen fathoms. The water was turbulent, which obscured our view.

day-1967-03-31.caption: Friday, March 31st, 1967. Day 75 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Honolulu for Midway.
day-1967-03-31.spoken: Good morning. It's Friday, March thirty-first, nineteen sixty-seven. Day seventy-five of the voyage, at sea, bound from Honolulu for Midway.

log-p241-2.caption: Camera 66: Phyng 15%?o. mug again filled by sediment. In 0 water.
log-p241-2.spoken: Bottom camera sixty-six came back with its mug filled by sediment. The water was clear.

log-p241-0.caption: Core 74: Brown lutite containing numerous authigenic minerals. Penetration app 294cm. core length 243cm. Bottom toposeephin - gently dipping men base of sea mount. Highly stratified sed. Cocoon age??
log-p241-0.spoken: Piston core seventy-four brought up brown mud full of unusual minerals. The sea floor there was gently sloping rock at the base of a seamount.

log-p241-1.caption: T-Grad 59A: No RECORD
log-p241-1.spoken: Heat-flow station 59A failed to get a record.

sum-1967-03-31.caption: In the North Pacific, the team took 8 samples at 2996 fathoms. They noted unusual minerals, though one measurement failed and the camera filled with sediment.
sum-1967-03-31.spoken: In the North Pacific, the team took eight samples at two thousand nine hundred ninety-six fathoms. They noted unusual minerals, though one measurement failed and the camera filled with sediment.

log-p240-2.caption: Core 75: Brown lutite overlying basalt. Penetration 193 cm. Core length 73 cm. Bottom topography: steep slope along side seamount. Cutting edge bashed in; pipe bent (15°) 6' above cutting edge. Some sediment poured out from cutting edge.
log-p240-2.spoken: Piston core seventy-five hit a steep slope and the cutting edge was bashed in. The pipe bent fifteen degrees, and some sediment poured out.

day-1967-04-01.caption: Saturday, April 1st, 1967. Day 76 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Honolulu for Midway.
day-1967-04-01.spoken: Good morning. It's Saturday, April first, nineteen sixty-seven. Day seventy-six of the voyage, at sea, bound from Honolulu for Midway.

log-p239-1.caption: NEPHO 74: 10 layers. Film stopped after some of hits.
log-p239-1.spoken: Nephelometer seventy-four recorded ten layers. The film stopped after some of the hits.

log-p240-3.caption: Core 76: Brown structureless lutite. Penetration 642 cm. Core length 422. Pipe bent (120°) at bottom of second pipe. Bottom topography: hills & valleys moderately stratified, pendular ring sands.
log-p240-3.spoken: Piston core seventy-six came up with its pipe bent one hundred twenty degrees at the bottom. It collected brown structureless lutite from a depth of three thousand twelve fathoms.

log-p240-6.caption: Core Camera 65: 55 deg. No ORIENTATION.
log-p240-6.spoken: Core camera sixty-five recorded a depth of fifty-five degrees. However, it failed to record any orientation data.

sum-1967-04-01.caption: In the North Pacific, the team completed 16 stations. A damaged corer lost sediment, and a pipe bent severely. The nephelometer film stopped early, and orientation data was missing.
sum-1967-04-01.spoken: In the North Pacific, the team completed sixteen stations. A damaged corer lost sediment, and a pipe bent severely. The nephelometer film stopped early, and orientation data was missing.

day-1967-04-02.caption: Sunday, April 2nd, 1967. Day 77 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Honolulu for Midway.
day-1967-04-02.spoken: Good morning. It's Sunday, April second, nineteen sixty-seven. Day seventy-seven of the voyage, at sea, bound from Honolulu for Midway.

log-p237-2.caption: TKMT-3: Hauling net in at 40 Fm/min, at half ahead placed too much strain on the depresser, causing it to warp and break several welds. No gear lost. This is the first tow to include multiple cod-end which functioned smoothly.
log-p237-2.spoken: Hauling the net at forty fathoms per minute strained the depresser, warping it and breaking several welds. No gear was lost in this first tow with multiple cod-ends.

log-p237-0.caption: Core 77: Brown lutites containing large pebble size Manganese nodules Penetration 1260+ - Full penetration - mud on core head and piston. Core length 1244 cm. Bottom topography rolling Slightly hilly with stratified pendulating subbottom GOOD RECORD - 3 PROBES
log-p237-0.spoken: Piston core seventy-seven brought up brown mud with large pebble size manganese nodules. It penetrated twelve sixty+ centimeters into the rolling sea floor.

log-p238-4.caption: NEPHO. 25: NEPHO CAMERA NOT SENT DOWN. CASE LEAKED SLIGHTLY ON LAST LOWERING. I DIDN'T WANT TO TAKE A CHANCE OF FLOODING WITH THE CAMERA IN CASE.
log-p238-4.spoken: The nephelometer camera was not sent down. Its case had leaked slightly on the last lowering, so the crew avoided risking a flood.

log-p238-5.caption: CORE CAMERA 66: STILL NO DELIGHTATION.
log-p238-5.spoken: Core camera sixty-six did not take any pictures. The log noted there was still no delightation.

log-p238-6.caption: WATER BARREL 50A: BARREL DIDN'T TRIP
log-p238-6.spoken: Water barrel 50A did not trip. The sampler failed to close on its way up.

sum-1967-04-02.caption: In the North Pacific, we took 9 stations at 2798 fathoms. A leaking case and a failed sampler caused trouble, but we found large manganese nodules in the core.
sum-1967-04-02.spoken: In the North Pacific, we took nine stations at two thousand seven hundred ninety-eight fathoms. A leaking case and a failed sampler caused trouble, but we found large manganese nodules in the core.

day-1967-04-03.caption: Monday, April 3rd, 1967. Day 78 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Honolulu for Midway.
day-1967-04-03.spoken: Good morning. It's Monday, April third, nineteen sixty-seven. Day seventy-eight of the voyage, at sea, bound from Honolulu for Midway.

log-p237-5.caption: Core 78: Unbedded silicious sand and ooze very firm and indurated Penetration 280cm. Good core length 14cm. Piston caught before broken pipe. Mud on piston. Relative orientation GOOD RECORD - 2 PROBES
log-p237-5.spoken: Piston core seventy-eight caught on a broken pipe before it could finish. It recovered only fourteen centimeters of firm, indurated silicious sand and ooze.

sum-1967-04-03.caption: In the North Pacific, the crew took 9 samples at 2850 fathoms. They recorded a heat flow of 1.66. A broken pipe caused a short core.
sum-1967-04-03.spoken: In the North Pacific, the crew took nine samples at two thousand eight hundred fifty fathoms. They recorded a heat flow of one point six six. A broken pipe caused a short core.

event-1967-04-04-crossed-the-internation.caption: Crossed the International Date Line. Westbound: the calendar jumps a day ahead.
event-1967-04-04-crossed-the-internation.spoken: Crossed the International Date Line. Westbound: the calendar jumps a day ahead.

day-1967-04-05.caption: Wednesday, April 5th, 1967. Day 79 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Honolulu for Midway.
day-1967-04-05.spoken: Good morning. It's Wednesday, April fifth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day seventy-nine of the voyage, at sea, bound from Honolulu for Midway.

log-p235-4.caption: Core Camera 68: 41 neg. DEVELOPMENT POSSIBLE. - BEST DEVELOPMENT SHOT SOFAR. BOTTOM CLEAN. O 100 LAYER.
log-p235-4.spoken: Core camera sixty-eight produced forty-one negatives. The log called it the best development shot so far, showing a clean bottom.

log-p234-1.caption: Bio 124-V: Dense band 40-60Fm thick, exists in surface SL. Scatterers forming this band made an unusual mid-morning migration to this level from a range of 240-300Fm. They began moving upward at 7Fm/min when descending core entered layer.
log-p234-1.spoken: A dense band of scatterers migrated up from two hundred forty to three hundred fathoms. They began moving upward at seven fathoms per minute when the descending core entered the layer.

log-p235-6.caption: Dredge 1: Dredge contained 10 manganese nodules the size of baseballs plus 4 large flat rocks containing radiolarian ooze, thin layers of silica, pycnulite lutites and manganese.
log-p235-6.spoken: Dredge one came up with ten manganese nodules the size of baseballs. It also caught four large flat rocks with radiolarian ooze.

log-p234-0.caption: EKMT-4: Swivel parted; lost entire rig.
log-p234-0.spoken: The swivel on the IKMT-four rig parted. The entire rig was lost.

sum-1967-04-05.caption: We were in the North Pacific. A swivel broke and the rig was lost. A core triggered an unusual migration. We completed 1 other station and 1 plankton tow.
sum-1967-04-05.spoken: We were in the North Pacific. A swivel broke and the rig was lost. A core triggered an unusual migration. We completed one other station and one plankton tow.

sum-1967-04-04.caption: We worked in the North Pacific at 3070 fathoms. We took 9 samples and measured heat flow of 1.60. We recovered large nodules and rocks, capturing the best development shot so far.
sum-1967-04-04.spoken: We worked in the North Pacific at three thousand seventy fathoms. We took nine samples and measured heat flow of one point six zero. We recovered large nodules and rocks, capturing the best development shot so far.

day-1967-04-06.caption: Thursday, April 6th, 1967. Day 80 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Honolulu for Midway.
day-1967-04-06.spoken: Good morning. It's Thursday, April sixth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day eighty of the voyage, at sea, bound from Honolulu for Midway.

sum-1967-04-06.caption: We were in the North Pacific. The crew completed 1 jet-net tow.
sum-1967-04-06.spoken: We were in the North Pacific. The crew completed one jet-net tow.

day-1967-04-07.caption: Friday, April 7th, 1967. Day 81 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Honolulu for Midway.
day-1967-04-07.spoken: Good morning. It's Friday, April seventh, nineteen sixty-seven. Day eighty-one of the voyage, at sea, bound from Honolulu for Midway.

log-p233-0.caption: CAMERA 72: 16 DEC. 19 HITS. SEDIMENT WORK SIGNS OF BOTTOM LIFE. LIGHT-WRACKING OF MAGNUS WADLUSO.
log-p233-0.spoken: Camera seventy-two took nineteen pictures of the sea floor. The images showed signs of bottom life.

sum-1967-04-07.caption: In the North Pacific, the crew took 12 samples at 2840 fathoms. They recorded a heat flow of 1.78. Photos showed signs of bottom life.
sum-1967-04-07.spoken: In the North Pacific, the crew took twelve samples at two thousand eight hundred forty fathoms. They recorded a heat flow of one point seven eight. Photos showed signs of bottom life.

day-1967-04-08.caption: Saturday, April 8th, 1967. Day 82 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Honolulu for Midway.
day-1967-04-08.spoken: Good morning. It's Saturday, April eighth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day eighty-two of the voyage, at sea, bound from Honolulu for Midway.

log-p232-5.caption: Camera 73: 2 hits. Fairly smooth sediment, bottom shows plenty of bottom life, some crabs. Compus reading not constant.
log-p232-5.spoken: Camera seventy-three took two hits of a fairly smooth sediment. The bottom showed plenty of life, including some crabs.

log-p232-2.caption: Core Camera 70: DID NOT SEND DOWN. REPAIRS ON COMPUS. P16.
log-p232-2.spoken: Core camera seventy did not go down because of repairs on the compus.

sum-1967-04-08.caption: We worked about 500 nautical miles south of Wake Island, in the North Pacific. The camera failed to deploy due to repairs, but we saw living things on the bottom.
sum-1967-04-08.spoken: We worked about five hundred nautical miles south of Wake Island, in the North Pacific. The camera failed to deploy due to repairs, but we saw living things on the bottom.

day-1967-04-09.caption: Sunday, April 9th, 1967. Day 83 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Honolulu for Midway.
day-1967-04-09.spoken: Good morning. It's Sunday, April ninth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day eighty-three of the voyage, at sea, bound from Honolulu for Midway.

log-p231-4.caption: CORE 82 (hit) 1401: Interbedded brown sand with brown oaf and brown white. Penetration 785cm. Core length 519cm. Bottom topography flat with stratified silt bottom. Cutting edge good, pipe bent
log-p231-4.spoken: Piston core eighty-two came up with a bent pipe. It brought up interbedded brown sand and brown ooze, penetrating seven hundred eighty-five centimeters.

log-p231-5.caption: CORE CAMERA 70A: Trigger Malfunction.
log-p231-5.spoken: Core camera 70A suffered a trigger malfunction.

sum-1967-04-09.caption: We worked about 300 nautical miles south of Wake Island in the North Pacific. The day included 7 stations and a 2962 fathom sounding. A core bent and the camera trigger malfunctioned.
sum-1967-04-09.spoken: We worked about three hundred nautical miles south of Wake Island in the North Pacific. The day included seven stations and a two thousand nine hundred sixty-two fathom sounding. A core bent and the camera trigger malfunctioned.

day-1967-04-10.caption: Monday, April 10th, 1967. Day 84 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Honolulu for Midway.
day-1967-04-10.spoken: Good morning. It's Monday, April tenth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day eighty-four of the voyage, at sea, bound from Honolulu for Midway.

log-p229-1.caption: CAMERA 75: 8000-9000 ft. Sediment + Nodules. - Compos readings not concentric - nodules not round as expected - scattered on sediment. - 3 pieces in drudge, no core.
log-p229-1.spoken: Camera seventy-five photographed sediment and nodules between eight thousand and nine thousand feet. The nodules were not round as expected, but scattered on the sediment.

log-p230-3.caption: Core 83: Brown white overlying reddish orange white. Possibly containing Cretaceous forams. Penetration 600 cm. Core length 573 cm. Bottom topography: gently rolling with stratified undulating subbottom. Outting stop bashed in pipe bent 35 deg. Core orientation possible.
log-p230-3.spoken: Piston core eighty-three had a bent pipe, but the core length was five hundred seventy-three centimeters. It may contain Cretaceous forams.

log-p230-6.caption: T-Grad 66A: No record - one probe penetration. P4 is leaking
log-p230-6.spoken: Heat-flow station 66A got no record because one probe was leaking.

sum-1967-04-10.caption: We worked about 300 nautical miles southwest of Wake Island in the North Pacific. The team collected 11 samples and found a bent pipe with possible fossils. We also noted unusual nodule shapes and a leaking probe.
sum-1967-04-10.spoken: We worked about three hundred nautical miles southwest of Wake Island in the North Pacific. The team collected eleven samples and found a bent pipe with possible fossils. We also noted unusual nodule shapes and a leaking probe.

day-1967-04-11.caption: Tuesday, April 11th, 1967. Day 85 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Honolulu for Midway.
day-1967-04-11.spoken: Good morning. It's Tuesday, April eleventh, nineteen sixty-seven. Day eighty-five of the voyage, at sea, bound from Honolulu for Midway.

log-p228-5.caption: Camera 76: 19 deg - 20 hits. Camera didn't seem to orient it out in current, more like as if it was side ways. Bottom shows signs of manganese.
log-p228-5.spoken: Camera seventy-six took twenty hits at nineteen degrees, but it did not orient correctly in the current. The bottom showed signs of manganese.

log-p228-0.caption: Core 84: Structure basan lutite containing mostly Mn nodules and an authigenic mineral. Penetration 1240 cm. Core length 1794 cm. Bottom topography: flat with stratified slightly undulating sub bottom. Cutting edge good, pipe bent
log-p228-0.spoken: Piston core eighty-four came up with a bent pipe. It contained basan lutite with mostly manganese nodules and an authigenic mineral.

log-p228-2.caption: T-Grad 66B: NO RECORD FILM STOPPED BEFORE HIT
log-p228-2.spoken: Heat-flow station 66B got no record because the film stopped before the hit.

log-p227-2.caption: JN 38: Entire effort of this tow wasted because of leaky storage bag.
log-p227-2.spoken: The jet net thirty-eight tow was wasted because the storage bag leaked.

sum-1967-04-11.caption: We worked about 300 nautical miles southwest of Wake Island, in the North Pacific. The day brought 12 stations, including a piston core with manganese nodules. A leaky bag wasted one tow, and a film issue meant no record was obtained.
sum-1967-04-11.spoken: We worked about three hundred nautical miles southwest of Wake Island, in the North Pacific. The day brought twelve stations, including a piston core with manganese nodules. A leaky bag wasted one tow, and a film issue meant no record was obtained.

day-1967-04-12.caption: Wednesday, April 12th, 1967. Day 86 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Honolulu for Midway.
day-1967-04-12.spoken: Good morning. It's Wednesday, April twelfth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day eighty-six of the voyage, at sea, bound from Honolulu for Midway.

log-p226-2.caption: Camera 77: 16 neg 17 hits. - Manganese Nodules. Largest seen so far. 9 Sampling dredge.
log-p226-2.spoken: Camera seventy-seven took sixteen negatives with seventeen hits. It showed manganese nodules, the largest seen so far.

log-p226-1.caption: Core Camera 72: Hang. No orientador
log-p226-1.spoken: Core camera seventy-two was hung up, and the orientador was missing.

log-p227-6.caption: T-Grad 66C: No record - short in battery pack
log-p227-6.spoken: Heat-flow station 66C got no record because the battery pack was short.

sum-1967-04-12.caption: We worked about 400 nautical miles west of Wake Island in the North Pacific. A battery failure prevented recording, and we saw the largest nodules so far.
sum-1967-04-12.spoken: We worked about four hundred nautical miles west of Wake Island in the North Pacific. A battery failure prevented recording, and we saw the largest nodules so far.

day-1967-04-13.caption: Thursday, April 13th, 1967. Day 87 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Honolulu for Midway.
day-1967-04-13.spoken: Good morning. It's Thursday, April thirteenth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day eighty-seven of the voyage, at sea, bound from Honolulu for Midway.

log-p225-7.caption: T-Grad 66D: No Record. One Probe Penetration. Pipe Laid Down. No Equilibrium.
log-p225-7.spoken: Heat-flow station 66D got no record because the pipe laid down. Only one probe penetrated, and no equilibrium was reached.

log-p225-4.caption: Core Camera 73: 73A. Trigger pin not pulled.
log-p225-4.spoken: Core camera 73A failed because the trigger pin was not pulled.

log-p225-6.caption: Core 86: Manganese Nodule bed overlying reddish brown lutite. Penetration - Pipe laid down. Good core length 56 cm. Core length 434 cm. Bottom topography: Steeply sloping over crest of Aleutian. PDR depth difficult to determine.
log-p225-6.spoken: Piston core eighty-six found a manganese nodule bed over reddish brown lutite. The pipe laid down on a steep slope, and the depth was hard to determine.

log-p224-0.caption: Core 87: Structureless brown lutite with a very low coarse fraction. Penetration 1242 cm. Core length 1169 cm. Bottom topography steep slope over crest of sea mount. P.D.R. depth at hit difficult to determine.
log-p224-0.spoken: Piston core eighty-seven hit a steep slope over the crest of a sea mount. The depth at the hit was difficult to determine.

sum-1967-04-13.caption: We were about 300 nautical miles west of Wake Island in the North Pacific. The team completed 17 stations, including 6 plankton tows and 3 piston cores. A steep slope made depth readings hard, and one trigger pin was not pulled.
sum-1967-04-13.spoken: We were about three hundred nautical miles west of Wake Island in the North Pacific. The team completed seventeen stations, including six plankton tows and three piston cores. A steep slope made depth readings hard, and one trigger pin was not pulled.

day-1967-04-14.caption: Friday, April 14th, 1967. Day 88 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Honolulu for Midway.
day-1967-04-14.spoken: Good morning. It's Friday, April fourteenth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day eighty-eight of the voyage, at sea, bound from Honolulu for Midway.

sum-1967-04-14.caption: We were about 200 nautical miles west of Wake Island, in the North Pacific. The team completed 10 stations, including 2 plankton tows and 1 piston core. We also recorded a heat-flow value of 1.92.
sum-1967-04-14.spoken: We were about two hundred nautical miles west of Wake Island, in the North Pacific. The team completed ten stations, including two plankton tows and one piston core. We also recorded a heat-flow value of one point nine two.

day-1967-04-15.caption: Saturday, April 15th, 1967. Day 89 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Honolulu for Midway.
day-1967-04-15.spoken: Good morning. It's Saturday, April fifteenth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day eighty-nine of the voyage, at sea, bound from Honolulu for Midway.

sum-1967-04-15.caption: We worked about 100 nautical miles northwest of Wake Island in the North Pacific. The crew took 9 samples and measured a heat flow of 0.91 at 2940 fathoms.
sum-1967-04-15.spoken: We worked about one hundred nautical miles northwest of Wake Island in the North Pacific. The crew took nine samples and measured a heat flow of zero point nine one at two thousand nine hundred forty fathoms.

day-1967-04-16.caption: Sunday, April 16th, 1967. Day 90 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Honolulu for Midway.
day-1967-04-16.spoken: Good morning. It's Sunday, April sixteenth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day ninety of the voyage, at sea, bound from Honolulu for Midway.

log-p220-3.caption: CORE 90: Bedded brown lutite containing foraminifer micromodules. Penetration 919 cm. Core length 1479 cm. Good core length 20 cm. Bottom topography by slightly hilly, rolling. Trigger line fouled on water barrel - Piston Core did not trip.
log-p220-3.spoken: Piston core ninety did not trip because the trigger line fouled on the water barrel. It penetrated nine hundred nineteen centimeters, but only twenty centimeters of good core was recovered.

sum-1967-04-16.caption: We were about 200 nautical miles northeast of Wake Island, in the North Pacific. The team completed 9 stations, including a heat-flow measurement of 1.30. A trigger line fouled, so the core failed.
sum-1967-04-16.spoken: We were about two hundred nautical miles northeast of Wake Island, in the North Pacific. The team completed nine stations, including a heat-flow measurement of one point three zero. A trigger line fouled, so the core failed.

day-1967-04-17.caption: Monday, April 17th, 1967. Day 91 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Honolulu for Midway.
day-1967-04-17.spoken: Good morning. It's Monday, April seventeenth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day ninety-one of the voyage, at sea, bound from Honolulu for Midway.

log-p218-1.caption: NEPHO 88: Couldn't attempt in rough weather. 300 Fm. lay light.
log-p218-1.spoken: The crew could not attempt the nephelometer work because of rough weather. The ship lay light at three hundred fathoms.

log-p218-0.caption: CAMERA 83: 7 for 10. Sediment - Little wear of bottom cable - Possible scattering of manganese nodules. - Descope at 1000 w/ 2000 ft wire, tungsten camera, open 10m opened possible more than likely due to strong current areas.
log-p218-0.spoken: Bottom camera eighty-three got seven out of ten pictures. The camera likely opened too early, possibly because of strong currents.

log-p219-3.caption: CORE 91: Brown lutite containing orange calcareous bed. Penetration 1024cm, core length 150.7. Good core length 800cm. Bottom topography flat, slightly rolling with small peaks in stratified undulating sed. Trigger weight lost during pullout or retrieve
log-p219-3.spoken: Piston core ninety-one recovered a brown mud with an orange calcareous bed. The trigger weight was lost during the pullout.

sum-1967-04-17.caption: We were about 400 nautical miles northeast of Wake Island in the North Pacific. Rough weather prevented sampling, and a trigger weight was lost during recovery. The camera likely opened due to strong current.
sum-1967-04-17.spoken: We were about four hundred nautical miles northeast of Wake Island in the North Pacific. Rough weather prevented sampling, and a trigger weight was lost during recovery. The camera likely opened due to strong current.

day-1967-04-18.caption: Tuesday, April 18th, 1967. Day 92 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Honolulu for Midway.
day-1967-04-18.spoken: Good morning. It's Tuesday, April eighteenth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day ninety-two of the voyage, at sea, bound from Honolulu for Midway.

sum-1967-04-18.caption: We worked about 500 nautical miles west of Midway in the North Pacific. The sea floor lay at 3126 fathoms. We completed 9 stations, including a heat flow measurement of 1.10.
sum-1967-04-18.spoken: We worked about five hundred nautical miles west of Midway in the North Pacific. The sea floor lay at three thousand one hundred twenty-six fathoms. We completed nine stations, including a heat flow measurement of one point one zero.

day-1967-04-19.caption: Wednesday, April 19th, 1967. Day 93 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Honolulu for Midway.
day-1967-04-19.spoken: Good morning. It's Wednesday, April nineteenth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day ninety-three of the voyage, at sea, bound from Honolulu for Midway.

sum-1967-04-19.caption: We worked about 400 nautical miles west of Midway in the North Pacific. The crew completed 40 stations, including a piston core and a heat-flow measurement of 1.04.
sum-1967-04-19.spoken: We worked about four hundred nautical miles west of Midway in the North Pacific. The crew completed forty stations, including a piston core and a heat-flow measurement of one point zero four.

day-1967-04-20.caption: Thursday, April 20th, 1967. Day 94 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Honolulu for Midway.
day-1967-04-20.spoken: Good morning. It's Thursday, April twentieth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day ninety-four of the voyage, at sea, bound from Honolulu for Midway.

log-p214-6.caption: Dredge 2A: Dredge was empty
log-p214-6.spoken: Dredge 2A was lowered, but it came back empty.

event-1967-04-20-crossed-the-internation.caption: Crossed the International Date Line. Eastbound: the same date happens twice.
event-1967-04-20-crossed-the-internation.spoken: Crossed the International Date Line. Eastbound: the same date happens twice.

day-1967-04-20-again.caption: Thursday, April 20th, 1967 (again). Day 95 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Honolulu for Midway.
day-1967-04-20-again.spoken: Good morning. It's Thursday, April twentieth, nineteen sixty-seven, again. Having crossed the date line eastbound, Vema lives this date twice. Day ninety-five of the voyage, at sea, bound from Honolulu for Midway.

log-p213-5.caption: Camera 87: Ooze, soft bottom. 2 lines, ship stationary. Wire out 3rd hit, lost 3 hundred lbs. Smelady + wired up, stopping + checking. Wire a good surge light + water, read photos unwat. Camera was thin.
log-p213-5.spoken: Camera eighty-seven was lost on the third hit, dropping three hundred lbs. The crew had to stop and check the wire.

log-p212-0.caption: Water Barrel 64: Sample Centrifuged - discarded contaminated from dirty centrifuged
log-p212-0.spoken: Water barrel sixty-four was centrifuged, but the sample was discarded because it was contaminated from a dirty centrifuge.

sum-1967-04-20.caption: We worked about 300 nautical miles west of Midway in the North Pacific. The dredge came up empty, and one sample was discarded due to contamination. We completed 16 stations, including 4 plankton tows and 2 piston cores.
sum-1967-04-20.spoken: We worked about three hundred nautical miles west of Midway in the North Pacific. The dredge came up empty, and one sample was discarded due to contamination. We completed sixteen stations, including four plankton tows and two piston cores.

log-p212-3.caption: Core 96: Foram ooz overlying calcareous sand. Hammer vibration method of extrusion destroyed part of cores possible structure Age - Recent. Penetration could not be determined. Bottom topography - crest of seamount
log-p212-3.spoken: Piston core ninety-six brought up foraminiferal ooze over calcareous sand. The hammer vibration method used to extrude the core destroyed part of its structure.

log-p212-5.caption: Core Camera 82: No. Core Camera wks. Camera crank went down - Camera broken.
log-p212-5.spoken: Core camera eighty-two was working, but the camera crank went down and the camera broke.

day-1967-04-21.caption: Friday, April 21st, 1967. Day 96 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Honolulu for Midway.
day-1967-04-21.spoken: Good morning. It's Friday, April twenty-first, nineteen sixty-seven. Day ninety-six of the voyage, at sea, bound from Honolulu for Midway.

sum-1967-04-21.caption: We worked about 40 nautical miles southwest of Midway in the North Pacific. The camera was lost on the wire and broke during operation. A core was damaged by extrusion.
sum-1967-04-21.spoken: We worked about forty nautical miles southwest of Midway in the North Pacific. The camera was lost on the wire and broke during operation. A core was damaged by extrusion.

leg-V2404-end.caption: Arriving Midway. Log: Fine weather. On this leg: 4,436 miles, 474 hours under way and 149 hours on station, averaging 9.5 knots.
leg-V2404-end.spoken: Vema arrives in Midway. From the voyage log: Fine weather. On this leg: four thousand four hundred thirty-six miles, four hundred seventy-four hours under way and one hundred forty-nine hours on station, averaging nine point five knots.

day-1967-04-22.caption: Saturday, April 22nd, 1967. Day 97 of the voyage, in port at Midway.
day-1967-04-22.spoken: Good morning. It's Saturday, April twenty-second, nineteen sixty-seven. Day ninety-seven of the voyage, in port at Midway.

day-1967-04-23.caption: Sunday, April 23rd, 1967. Day 98 of the voyage, in port at Midway.
day-1967-04-23.spoken: Good morning. It's Sunday, April twenty-third, nineteen sixty-seven. Day ninety-eight of the voyage, in port at Midway.

day-1967-04-24.caption: Monday, April 24th, 1967. Day 99 of the voyage, in port at Midway.
day-1967-04-24.spoken: Good morning. It's Monday, April twenty-fourth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day ninety-nine of the voyage, in port at Midway.

day-1967-04-25.caption: Tuesday, April 25th, 1967. Day 100 of the voyage, in port at Midway.
day-1967-04-25.spoken: Good morning. It's Tuesday, April twenty-fifth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day one hundred of the voyage, in port at Midway.

leg-V2405-start.caption: Leg 5 of 13: Midway to Manila. Chief scientist G.M. Bryan.
leg-V2405-start.spoken: Leg five of thirteen begins. Vema sails from Midway for Manila, with G. M. Bryan as chief scientist.

log-p210-2.caption: Core Camera 881A: MISSED SWITCH SHOTING.
log-p210-2.spoken: Core camera 881A missed the switch, so it did not shoot.

log-p210-3.caption: Water Barrel 66: SAMPLE COULD NOT BE CENTRIFUGED. CENTRIFUGE ON THE BLIND, NEEDS BEARING AND UPPER PART OF HOUSING.
log-p210-3.spoken: The sample from water barrel sixty-six could not be spun. The centrifuge was on the blind and needed a bearing and upper housing.

day-1967-04-26.caption: Wednesday, April 26th, 1967. Day 101 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Midway for Manila.
day-1967-04-26.spoken: Good morning. It's Wednesday, April twenty-sixth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day one hundred one of the voyage, at sea, bound from Midway for Manila.

sum-1967-04-26.caption: We were about 200 nautical miles south of Midway, in the North Pacific. The camera failed to take pictures, and the centrifuge broke, making one sample unusable. We completed 10 stations at 2883 fathoms.
sum-1967-04-26.spoken: We were about two hundred nautical miles south of Midway, in the North Pacific. The camera failed to take pictures, and the centrifuge broke, making one sample unusable. We completed ten stations at two thousand eight hundred eighty-three fathoms.

day-1967-04-27.caption: Thursday, April 27th, 1967. Day 102 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Midway for Manila.
day-1967-04-27.spoken: Good morning. It's Thursday, April twenty-seventh, nineteen sixty-seven. Day one hundred two of the voyage, at sea, bound from Midway for Manila.

sum-1967-04-27.caption: We were about 400 nautical miles south of Midway, in the North Pacific. The crew took 7 samples, including a piston core and a heat-flow measurement of 1.46.
sum-1967-04-27.spoken: We were about four hundred nautical miles south of Midway, in the North Pacific. The crew took seven samples, including a piston core and a heat-flow measurement of one point four six.

log-p208-5.caption: CORE 99: Globigerina sand containing several hard compact layers. Penetration could not be determined. Core length 932 cm. Hammer vibration method used to extrude first 300 cm of core. Bottom topography crest of sea mount.
log-p208-5.spoken: Piston core ninety-nine brought up globigerina sand with several hard compact layers. The crew used a hammer vibration method to push out the first three hundred centimeters of the core.

day-1967-04-28.caption: Friday, April 28th, 1967. Day 103 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Midway for Manila.
day-1967-04-28.spoken: Good morning. It's Friday, April twenty-eighth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day one hundred three of the voyage, at sea, bound from Midway for Manila.

sum-1967-04-28.caption: We were about 600 nautical miles south of Midway, in the North Pacific. The crew took 1 piston core and 1 plankton tow. They also made 1 nephelometer lowering, 1 bottom-camera lowering, and 1 camera on the corer. A hammer was used on a sea mount crest.
sum-1967-04-28.spoken: We were about six hundred nautical miles south of Midway, in the North Pacific. The crew took one piston core and one plankton tow. They also made one nephelometer lowering, one bottom-camera lowering, and one camera on the corer. A hammer was used on a sea mount crest.

event-1967-04-29-crossed-the-internation.caption: Crossed the International Date Line. Westbound: the calendar jumps a day ahead.
event-1967-04-29-crossed-the-internation.spoken: Crossed the International Date Line. Westbound: the calendar jumps a day ahead.

day-1967-04-30.caption: Sunday, April 30th, 1967. Day 104 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Midway for Manila.
day-1967-04-30.spoken: Good morning. It's Sunday, April thirtieth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day one hundred four of the voyage, at sea, bound from Midway for Manila.

sum-1967-04-29.caption: In the North Pacific, the crew took 5 stations at 2828 fathoms. They recorded a heat flow of 1.30 and used a camera on the corer.
sum-1967-04-29.spoken: In the North Pacific, the crew took five stations at two thousand eight hundred twenty-eight fathoms. They recorded a heat flow of one point three zero and used a camera on the corer.

day-1967-05-01.caption: Monday, May 1st, 1967. Day 105 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Midway for Manila.
day-1967-05-01.spoken: Good morning. It's Monday, May first, nineteen sixty-seven. Day one hundred five of the voyage, at sea, bound from Midway for Manila.

log-p206-0.caption: Core 101: Brown ooze with basalt pebbles scattered through- out. Penetration could not be determined. Core length 71cm. Good core 57cm. Bottom depth overestimated. Core hit went unnoticed; ocean cable laid out. Bottom topography - alongside seamount.
log-p206-0.spoken: Piston core one hundred one brought up brown ooze with basalt pebbles. The core hit an ocean cable that was laid out nearby.

log-p207-6.caption: CAMERA 92A: Lost Camera
log-p207-6.spoken: The camera for station 92A was lost.

sum-1967-04-30.caption: The Vema worked in the North Pacific with 3 stations. We lost a camera at sea during the bottom-camera lowering.
sum-1967-04-30.spoken: The Vema worked in the North Pacific with three stations. We lost a camera at sea during the bottom-camera lowering.

sum-1967-05-01.caption: In the North Pacific, the Vema took 5 stations at 1818 fathoms. A core hit an ocean cable, and a heat-flow measurement read 2.38.
sum-1967-05-01.spoken: In the North Pacific, the Vema took five stations at eighteen eighteen fathoms. A core hit an ocean cable, and a heat-flow measurement read two point three eight.

day-1967-05-02.caption: Tuesday, May 2nd, 1967. Day 106 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Midway for Manila.
day-1967-05-02.spoken: Good morning. It's Tuesday, May second, nineteen sixty-seven. Day one hundred six of the voyage, at sea, bound from Midway for Manila.

sum-1967-05-02.caption: The Vema worked in the North Pacific. We completed 1 jet-net tow. A persistent flaw in the jet net was noted.
sum-1967-05-02.spoken: The Vema worked in the North Pacific. We completed one jet-net tow. A persistent flaw in the jet net was noted.

log-p205-0.caption: JN 37: Still unable to locate the flaw in the JN which reduces its capturing ability
log-p205-0.spoken: The crew was still unable to locate the flaw in the jet net that reduced its capturing ability.

log-p205-1.caption: CORE 102: Brown, homogeneous lutite containing hard indurated brown layers. Penetration 666 cm. Core length 1198 cm. Good core 668 cm. Cutting edge smashed. Trigger weight sediment lost. Highly stratified indurating sediments.
log-p205-1.spoken: Piston core one hundred two came up with a smashed cutting edge and lost trigger weight sediment. It recovered six hundred sixty-eight centimeters of good core from two thousand six hundred fifty-two fathoms.

day-1967-05-03.caption: Wednesday, May 3rd, 1967. Day 107 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Midway for Manila.
day-1967-05-03.spoken: Good morning. It's Wednesday, May third, nineteen sixty-seven. Day one hundred seven of the voyage, at sea, bound from Midway for Manila.

sum-1967-05-03.caption: In the North Pacific, the team took 6 samples at 2652 fathoms. A heat-flow measurement read 2.25. The piston core's cutting edge was smashed, and sediment was lost.
sum-1967-05-03.spoken: In the North Pacific, the team took six samples at two thousand six hundred fifty-two fathoms. A heat-flow measurement read two point two five. The piston core's cutting edge was smashed, and sediment was lost.

log-p204-1.caption: Core 103: Lutetoid radiolarian and foram ooze overlying a pebble conglomerate. Penetration 932cm. Core length 820cm. Good core 820cm. Cutting edge smashed in. Bottom topography hilly, with highly stratified muds having pelican?
log-p204-1.spoken: Piston core one hundred three brought up radiolarian and foraminiferal ooze over pebble conglomerate. The cutting edge was smashed in, and the bottom looked hilly.

day-1967-05-04.caption: Thursday, May 4th, 1967. Day 108 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Midway for Manila.
day-1967-05-04.spoken: Good morning. It's Thursday, May fourth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day one hundred eight of the voyage, at sea, bound from Midway for Manila.

log-p204-4.caption: Camera 93: 9 neg. 10 hits. Sediment-little. Bottom life - possible pieces of coral?
log-p204-4.spoken: Camera ninety-three took nine negatives and ten hits. The bottom had little sediment, with possible pieces of coral.

log-p203-1.caption: JN-38: For the first time we were able to eliminate the sample loss experienced previously. Due to the extremely large sample derived, towing time will be reduced from the standard 2hrs to 30 min in the future.
log-p203-1.spoken: For the first time, the crew eliminated the sample loss experienced previously. The large sample meant future tows would be reduced to thirty minutes.

sum-1967-05-04.caption: In the North Pacific, we took 10 stations at 2660 fathoms. A smashed cutting edge revealed unusual sediment, and we saw possible coral pieces. For the first time, sample loss was eliminated.
sum-1967-05-04.spoken: In the North Pacific, we took ten stations at two thousand six hundred sixty fathoms. A smashed cutting edge revealed unusual sediment, and we saw possible coral pieces. For the first time, sample loss was eliminated.

log-p202-0.caption: NEPHO 100A: DIDN'T TURN LIGHT SODECE ON.
log-p202-0.spoken: The nephelometer at station 100A did not turn on, so no light was recorded.

log-p202-3.caption: Bio 342-347: Good example of nemichthyida captured in 500m-1000m range of core net.
log-p202-3.spoken: The core net captured a good example of a nemichthyid fish in the five hundred to one thousand meter range.

day-1967-05-05.caption: Friday, May 5th, 1967. Day 109 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Midway for Manila.

log-p198-6.spoken: Bottom camera ninety-nine advanced its film in six foot portions. It captured one negative, but parts of the compass were not on the bottom.

On this leg: five thousand seven hundred ninety-two miles, six hundred ten hours under way and one hundred hours on station, averaging nine point five knots.

Weather terrible. On this leg: one thousand seven hundred miles, two hundred hours under way and one hundred twenty hours on station, averaging nine point five knots.

sum-1967-09-24.spoken: In the Indian Ocean, we took eight samples at fifteen fifty fathoms. The heat flow was one point eight two. We faced a camera failure, a net leak, and smoke flakes on our slides.
