day-1967-09-25.spoken: Good morning. It's Monday, September twenty-fifth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day two hundred fifty-two of the voyage, at sea, bound from Mauritius for Cape Town.

log-p099-0.caption: CORE CAMERA 171: 38 - PICTURES ORIENTABLE NOT POSSIBLE
log-p099-0.spoken: Core camera one hundred seventy-one took thirty-eight pictures, but it was not possible to orient them.

log-p099-1.caption: Bio 715-720: Shallow net of core MPS surfaced with hole in net.
log-p099-1.spoken: The shallow net for core MPS surfaced with a hole in it.

log-p098-1.caption: Water Barrel 82: On Core Telltale indicates bottom trip Sample discarded when centrifuge not working during processing
log-p098-1.spoken: Water barrel eighty-two triggered on the bottom. The sample was discarded because the centrifuge was not working.

log-p099-5.caption: JN 107: Rich sample, highly luminescent. Numerous copepods + other crustacea.
log-p099-5.spoken: Jet net one hundred seven caught a rich, highly luminescent sample. It contained numerous copepods and other crustaceans.

sum-1967-09-25.caption: In the Indian Ocean, the team took 9 samples at 2930 fathoms. A net surfaced with a hole, and pictures could not be oriented. They found a rich, luminescent sample with copepods, but lost a sample due to a broken centrifuge.
sum-1967-09-25.spoken: In the Indian Ocean, the team took nine samples at two thousand nine hundred thirty fathoms. A net surfaced with a hole, and pictures could not be oriented. They found a rich, luminescent sample with copepods, but lost a sample due to a broken centrifuge.

day-1967-09-26.caption: Tuesday, September 26th, 1967. Day 253 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Mauritius for Cape Town.
day-1967-09-26.spoken: Good morning. It's Tuesday, September twenty-sixth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day two hundred fifty-three of the voyage, at sea, bound from Mauritius for Cape Town.

log-p098-2.caption: Bio 721-725: Damage sustained on previous stn. made it necessary to install new net on shallow frame of core MPS. Deep flowmeter read "0" but net contained normal sample (flowmeter release failed). Shallow net failed to open.
log-p098-2.spoken: Damage from the previous station required a new net on the shallow frame. The deep flowmeter read zero, but the net caught a normal sample. The shallow net failed to open.

log-p098-0.caption: Core Camera 172: 33 - Pictures Orientation not possible
log-p098-0.spoken: Core camera one hundred seventy-two took thirty-three pictures. Orientation was not possible.

log-p098-5.caption: JN 108: Sample predominantly pink copepods. Blue copepod from warm waters of Indian + S. Pacific Oceans has disappeared. Luminescence in sample bright enough to be seen in bright sunlight! Fresh water causes discharge of light.
log-p098-5.spoken: The jet net caught mostly pink copepods. The luminescence in the sample was bright enough to be seen in bright sunlight.

sum-1967-09-26.caption: In the Indian Ocean, the Vema took 7 stations at 2670 fathoms. A heat-flow value of 2.02 was recorded. Orientation was impossible, and the net and flowmeter failed. Bioluminescence was visible in sunlight.
sum-1967-09-26.spoken: In the Indian Ocean, the Vema took seven stations at two thousand six hundred seventy fathoms. A heat-flow value of two point zero two was recorded. Orientation was impossible, and the net and flowmeter failed. Bioluminescence was visible in sunlight.

day-1967-09-27.caption: Wednesday, September 27th, 1967. Day 254 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Mauritius for Cape Town.
day-1967-09-27.spoken: Good morning. It's Wednesday, September twenty-seventh, nineteen sixty-seven. Day two hundred fifty-four of the voyage, at sea, bound from Mauritius for Cape Town.

log-p098-6.caption: Core 204: Pen. Core Head Buried C.L. 1880cm T.C. 210cm Light gray marl. It is believed the piston didn't work proper causing the three pipes to be full of flow in.
log-p098-6.spoken: Piston core two hundred four had a core length of eighteen eighty centimeters. The piston did not work properly, causing the three pipes to be full of flow-in.

log-p097-3.caption: Bio 726-731: Very well-defined scattering in surface layers. Abundant red copepod from previous stn has been abruptly replaced by a pink variety. Numerous albatross this area. Cf. 732-737 (night, same location) for vertical changes in migrant species concentration
log-p097-3.spoken: Plankton tows seven hundred twenty-six to seven hundred thirty-one found abundant red copepods replaced by a pink variety. Numerous albatross were seen in the area.

log-p097-5.caption: BT-71: Smoke flaked off of slide.
log-p097-5.spoken: Bathythermograph seventy-one was taken at one hundred fifty fathoms. Smoke flaked off of the slide.

log-p097-6.caption: IK-24: IK 24 sampled a daytime SL at about 180 Fm. Numerous hatchet fish + krill. Dusk migrations began just after completion of tow.
log-p097-6.spoken: Trawl IK twenty-four sampled a daytime sound-scattering layer at about one hundred eighty fathoms. It caught numerous hatchet fish and krill.

log-p097-0.caption: Core Camera 173: 30 - Pictures ORIENTATION NOT POSSIBLE
log-p097-0.spoken: Core camera one hundred seventy-three took thirty pictures, but orientation was not possible.

log-p097-1.caption: Core 205-A: No core or trigger core obtained. First pipe broke off about 1' from coupling. Cutting edge was also damaged.
log-p097-1.spoken: Piston core two hundred five-A failed to get a core. The first pipe broke off about one foot from the coupling, and the cutting edge was damaged.

log-p097-2.caption: Core Camera 174: 35 - PICTURES ORIENTATION NOT POSSIBLE DOUBLE FLASH ACTION - 20 PICTURES
log-p097-2.spoken: Core camera one hundred seventy-four took thirty-five pictures with a double flash action. Orientation was not possible, and twenty pictures were recorded.

sum-1967-09-27.caption: We worked in the Indian Ocean, taking 12 stations. Soundings reached 2360 and 2475 fathoms. We faced a piston failure and a broken pipe, so no core was obtained.
sum-1967-09-27.spoken: We worked in the Indian Ocean, taking twelve stations. Soundings reached two thousand three hundred sixty and two thousand four hundred seventy-five fathoms. We faced a piston failure and a broken pipe, so no core was obtained.

day-1967-09-28.caption: Thursday, September 28th, 1967. Day 255 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Mauritius for Cape Town.
day-1967-09-28.spoken: Good morning. It's Thursday, September twenty-eighth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day two hundred fifty-five of the voyage, at sea, bound from Mauritius for Cape Town.

log-p096-3.caption: Core 205: Pen. 234 cm. C.L. 720 cm. Piece of Core lost in separating pipes + 3 pieces mixed when they follow close. Lt Grey Marl changing to Green mineral Sand. There are 2 maybe 3 Turbidites. This Core should be Checked.
log-p096-3.spoken: Piston core two hundred five lost a piece of core while separating the pipes. three pieces were mixed together because they followed close.

log-p096-5.caption: Core Camera 175: 34- PICTURES ORIENTATION NOT POSSIBLE
log-p096-5.spoken: Core camera one hundred seventy-five took thirty-four pictures. Orientation was not possible.

log-p095-2.caption: JN 110: Bulk of sample consists of large pink copepods and phyto plankton. Abundant albatross + terns this area.
log-p095-2.spoken: The jet net caught mostly large pink copepods and phytoplankton. Abundant albatrosses and terns were seen in the area.

sum-1967-09-28.caption: We worked in the Indian Ocean at 2965 fathoms. Seven stations were completed, though core pieces were lost and mixed. We noted large copepods and abundant birds.
sum-1967-09-28.spoken: We worked in the Indian Ocean at two thousand nine hundred sixty-five fathoms. Seven stations were completed, though core pieces were lost and mixed. We noted large copepods and abundant birds.

day-1967-09-29.caption: Friday, September 29th, 1967. Day 256 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Mauritius for Cape Town.
day-1967-09-29.spoken: Good morning. It's Friday, September twenty-ninth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day two hundred fifty-six of the voyage, at sea, bound from Mauritius for Cape Town.

log-p095-6.caption: TK 25: Rough seas. Replaced old towing block system with a simpler, faster, safer arrangement, utilizing an expendable rope loop which may be cut to release wire.
log-p095-6.spoken: Rough seas led to replacing the old towing block system with a simpler, faster, and safer arrangement. It used an expendable rope loop that could be cut to release the wire.

log-p095-5.caption: CORE CAMERA 176: 25- PICTURES ORIENTATION NOT POSSIBLE
log-p095-5.spoken: Core camera one hundred seventy-six took twenty-five pictures, but orientation was not possible.

sum-1967-09-29.caption: In the Indian Ocean, the team took 8 samples at 1920 fathoms. Rough seas forced a towing system replacement, and pictures could not be oriented.
sum-1967-09-29.spoken: In the Indian Ocean, the team took eight samples at nineteen twenty fathoms. Rough seas forced a towing system replacement, and pictures could not be oriented.

day-1967-09-30.caption: Saturday, September 30th, 1967. Day 257 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Mauritius for Cape Town.
day-1967-09-30.spoken: Good morning. It's Saturday, September thirtieth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day two hundred fifty-seven of the voyage, at sea, bound from Mauritius for Cape Town.

log-p093-0.caption: Bio 750-755: Normal. Deep flowmeter failed to trip.
log-p093-0.spoken: The plankton tows were normal, but the deep flowmeter failed to trip.

log-p093-7.caption: JN 112: Difficult handling jet-net in foul weather. Received considerable battering during recovery. High winds + heavy seas precluded removal of sample until ship slowed for sonobuoy.
log-p093-7.spoken: Foul weather made handling the jet net difficult, and it received considerable battering during recovery. High winds and heavy seas prevented removing the sample until the ship slowed for a sonobuoy.

log-p093-1.caption: Core 208: Pen. ? C.L. 1095cm T.C. 70cm Gray foraminiferal marly ooze. Principle becomes 15-70cm mostly broken forams. It is believed that the core didn't trip till after the hit.
log-p093-1.spoken: Piston core two hundred eight brought up one thousand ninety-five centimeters of gray foraminiferal marly ooze. The core did not trip until after the hit.

log-p093-3.caption: Core Camera 178: 27 - Pictures. Orientation not possible. Film out of focus due to dirt on lens.
log-p093-3.spoken: Core camera one hundred seventy-eight took twenty-seven pictures, but they were out of focus due to dirt on the lens.

log-p093-2.caption: F6KNO 167A: NO RECORD - NO READABLE EQUILIBRIUM POINT
log-p093-2.spoken: Station F6KNO 167A produced no record, as there was no readable equilibrium point.

sum-1967-09-30.caption: In the Indian Ocean, the team took 12 stations. The flowmeter failed to trip, and the core did not trip until after it hit. No readable record was obtained, and the pictures were out of focus due to dirt.
sum-1967-09-30.spoken: In the Indian Ocean, the team took twelve stations. The flowmeter failed to trip, and the core did not trip until after it hit. No readable record was obtained, and the pictures were out of focus due to dirt.

day-1967-10-01.caption: Sunday, October 1st, 1967. Day 258 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Mauritius for Cape Town.
day-1967-10-01.spoken: Good morning. It's Sunday, October first, nineteen sixty-seven. Day two hundred fifty-eight of the voyage, at sea, bound from Mauritius for Cape Town.

log-p092-0.caption: JN 113: Surface temp took a radical "dip" during this tow. If this is an area of upwelling, the sample may reflect the ecological change Cf JN 114. Numerous albatross.
log-p092-0.spoken: The surface temperature took a radical dip during the jet net tow. Numerous albatrosses were seen.

sum-1967-10-01.caption: We were in the Indian Ocean today. The crew deployed 1 sonobuoy and 1 jet-net tow. We noted an unusual temperature dip and saw albatrosses.
sum-1967-10-01.spoken: We were in the Indian Ocean today. The crew deployed one sonobuoy and one jet-net tow. We noted an unusual temperature dip and saw albatrosses.

day-1967-10-02.caption: Monday, October 2nd, 1967. Day 259 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Mauritius for Cape Town.
day-1967-10-02.spoken: Good morning. It's Monday, October second, nineteen sixty-seven. Day two hundred fifty-nine of the voyage, at sea, bound from Mauritius for Cape Town.

log-p092-3.caption: Core Camera 179A: No pictures; strobe light did not flash- replaced coil, flash bulb and capacitor.
log-p092-3.spoken: Core camera 179A took no pictures because the strobe light did not flash. The coil, flash bulb, and capacitor were replaced.

log-p092-4.caption: Bio 756-758: Deep flowmeter failed to trip. Shallow net of CMPs split up both sides- irreparable. Vertical net was torn by high winds during the night- no replacements.
log-p092-4.spoken: The deep flowmeter failed to trip, and the shallow net split up both sides. The vertical net was torn by high winds during the night.

log-p092-7.caption: JN 114: Large pink krill actively swimming in sample.
log-p092-7.spoken: Large pink krill were actively swimming in the jet net sample.

sum-1967-10-02.caption: In the Indian Ocean, we took 7 samples at 2755 fathoms. The camera failed and gear tore, but we saw living krill.
sum-1967-10-02.spoken: In the Indian Ocean, we took seven samples at two thousand seven hundred fifty-five fathoms. The camera failed and gear tore, but we saw living krill.

day-1967-10-03.caption: Tuesday, October 3rd, 1967. Day 260 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Mauritius for Cape Town.
day-1967-10-03.spoken: Good morning. It's Tuesday, October third, nineteen sixty-seven. Day two hundred sixty of the voyage, at sea, bound from Mauritius for Cape Town.

log-p091-0.caption: CORE 210: Pen. 492 cm C.L. 29 cm T.C. 20 cm Core failed to trip. Lt. Brown marl with moderate burrowing. Mn fragments (local) present at top and at 14 cm.
log-p091-0.spoken: Piston core two hundred ten failed to trip, and Lt. Brown noted marl with moderate burrowing. Manganese fragments were present at the top and at fourteen centimeters.

log-p091-3.caption: Bio 759 761: No core MPS because of damage sustained on previous station
log-p091-3.spoken: No core Millipore samples were taken for Bio seven hundred fifty-nine and seven hundred sixty-one because of damage sustained on the previous station.

sum-1967-10-03.caption: We worked in the Indian Ocean at 2645 fathoms. A core failed to trip, and sampling was skipped due to damage. We recorded a heat flow of 0.8.
sum-1967-10-03.spoken: We worked in the Indian Ocean at two thousand six hundred forty-five fathoms. A core failed to trip, and sampling was skipped due to damage. We recorded a heat flow of zero point eight.

day-1967-10-04.caption: Wednesday, October 4th, 1967. Day 261 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Mauritius for Cape Town.
day-1967-10-04.spoken: Good morning. It's Wednesday, October fourth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day two hundred sixty-one of the voyage, at sea, bound from Mauritius for Cape Town.

log-p090-2.caption: Sono-Buoy 62: CHANNEL 15, SET AT 3 HOURS AND 60 FEET WATER TEMP 18.2°C PROFILER A CHANNEL 2 FAST TRAVERSE & 3.5 KC PDR DIED AFTER 70 MINUTES; 7.37 MILES; BT#78 IN AREA (S222) 1 REFRACTION FROM BASEMENT
log-p090-2.spoken: The precision depth recorder died after seventy minutes. The sonobuoy logged seven point three seven miles of data.

log-p090-0.caption: CORE 211: Pen. 450cm C.L. 205cm Tc. 205cm Marl changing from light brown to various shades of grayish greens. The core is highly layered and moderate burrowing is present in the upper parts. 2nd & 3rd Pipe Bent.
log-p090-0.spoken: Piston core two hundred eleven came up with the second and third pipes bent. It penetrated four hundred fifty centimeters and recovered two hundred five centimeters of marl.

log-p090-1.caption: CORE CAMERA 180: 22- PICTURES Orientation not possible Pictures still out of focus (Adj. lens)
log-p090-1.spoken: Core camera one hundred eighty took twenty-two pictures, but they were still out of focus. Orientation was not possible.

log-p090-3.caption: WATER BARREL 83 A: ON CORE 211 TELLTALE SLIDE INDICATES BARREL TRIPPED BEFORE REACHING BOTTOM. SAMPLE DISCARDED
log-p090-3.spoken: Water barrel eighty-three A tripped before reaching the bottom. The sample was discarded.

sum-1967-10-04.caption: In the Indian Ocean, we took 9 samples at 2642 fathoms. The heat flow was 1.4, but the PDR died after 70 minutes. We recovered a core, though the pictures were out of focus and the barrel sample was lost.
sum-1967-10-04.spoken: In the Indian Ocean, we took nine samples at two thousand six hundred forty-two fathoms. The heat flow was one point four, but the precision depth recorder died after seventy minutes. We recovered a core, though the pictures were out of focus and the barrel sample was lost.

day-1967-10-05.caption: Thursday, October 5th, 1967. Day 262 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Mauritius for Cape Town.
day-1967-10-05.spoken: Good morning. It's Thursday, October fifth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day two hundred sixty-two of the voyage, at sea, bound from Mauritius for Cape Town.

log-p089-0.caption: CORE 212: Pen. 520 cm. C.L. 643 cm TC 290 cm Typical "Red" clay homogeneous in color throughout. A pepering effect due to Mn micro nodules is present. Both Pipes Bent near coupling. 12- Pictures ORIENTATION NOT POSSIBLE
log-p089-0.spoken: Piston core two hundred twelve came up with both pipes bent near the coupling. The core was six hundred forty-three centimeters long, but orientation was not possible.

log-p089-2.caption: Bio 765-767: Two dark SLs. Deeper SL very narrow & compact + highly photophobic. Its vertical movements during this station correlate perfectly with amount of solar radiation. No CMPS because of efforts to locate cause of core trip failure.
log-p089-2.spoken: Two dark sound-scattering layers were seen. The deeper one moved vertically in perfect correlation with the amount of solar radiation.

sum-1967-10-05.caption: In the Indian Ocean, the Vema took 4 stations, including 1 piston core and 1 heat-flow measurement. The depth reached 2714 fathoms. Pipes bent, causing orientation to fail, and the sound-scattering layer behaved unusually.
sum-1967-10-05.spoken: In the Indian Ocean, the Vema took four stations, including one piston core and one heat-flow measurement. The depth reached two thousand seven hundred fourteen fathoms. Pipes bent, causing orientation to fail, and the sound-scattering layer behaved unusually.

day-1967-10-06.caption: Friday, October 6th, 1967. Day 263 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Mauritius for Cape Town.
day-1967-10-06.spoken: Good morning. It's Friday, October sixth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day two hundred sixty-three of the voyage, at sea, bound from Mauritius for Cape Town.

day-1967-10-07.caption: Saturday, October 7th, 1967. Day 264 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Mauritius for Cape Town.
day-1967-10-07.spoken: Good morning. It's Saturday, October seventh, nineteen sixty-seven. Day two hundred sixty-four of the voyage, at sea, bound from Mauritius for Cape Town.

day-1967-10-08.caption: Sunday, October 8th, 1967. Day 265 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Mauritius for Cape Town.
day-1967-10-08.spoken: Good morning. It's Sunday, October eighth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day two hundred sixty-five of the voyage, at sea, bound from Mauritius for Cape Town.

log-p089-4.caption: MP 147: Other samplings precluded by foul weather
log-p089-4.spoken: Foul weather prevented other samplings at the surface.

sum-1967-10-08.caption: We were about 500 nautical miles east of the Cape of Good Hope, in the Indian Ocean. Foul weather stopped work, so we took one Millipore filter sample.
sum-1967-10-08.spoken: We were about five hundred nautical miles east of the Cape of Good Hope, in the Indian Ocean. Foul weather stopped work, so we took one Millipore filter sample.

day-1967-10-09.caption: Monday, October 9th, 1967. Day 266 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Mauritius for Cape Town.
day-1967-10-09.spoken: Good morning. It's Monday, October ninth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day two hundred sixty-six of the voyage, at sea, bound from Mauritius for Cape Town.

log-p088-0.caption: Core 213: Pen. CL. 811cm TC. 122cm Foraminiferal marl ooze underlain by a bed of manganese nodules. No laminations or burrowings visible. 1st & 2nd pipe Bent. Cutting Edge Slightly Damaged
log-p088-0.spoken: Piston core two hundred thirteen came up with both pipes bent and a slightly damaged cutting edge. It recovered foraminiferal marl ooze over a bed of manganese nodules.

log-p088-7.caption: JN-117: Sample 770-V was accidentally combined with JN 117 in formalin-preserved bag. Consequently these two samplings were repeated on stn 226 taken nearly same location
log-p088-7.spoken: Sample seven hundred seventy-V was accidentally combined with jet net one hundred seventeen in a formalin-preserved bag. The two samplings had to be repeated at the nearby station.

log-p088-4.caption: Bio 768-770: No core MPS because storm destroyed nets - no spares left. Stations 225 + 226 are in close proximity, so samples should be similar.
log-p088-4.spoken: The storm destroyed the nets, leaving no spares, so no core samples were taken. The nearby stations were close enough that the samples should be similar.

log-p087-0.caption: CORE 215: Pen 405 cm. C.L. 403 cm TC 403 cm. Lt brown Foraminiferal marl changing to lt gray marl. Many layerings are present. The sediment is very compacted near the base of the core. Cutting edge was damaged.
log-p087-0.spoken: Piston core two hundred fifteen brought up light brown foraminiferal marl. The cutting edge was damaged.

log-p087-4.caption: JN 118: Extremely rich sample. Surface temp. recorder dropped more than 2.0°C during this tow, so rich sample may be due to interface between two masses of water
log-p087-4.spoken: Jet net one hundred eighteen caught an extremely rich sample. The surface temperature recorder dropped more than two point zero degrees Celsius during the tow.

sum-1967-10-09.caption: We were about 400 nautical miles southeast of the Cape of Good Hope, in the Indian Ocean. The day brought 14 stations, including 3 piston cores and 2 heat-flow measurements. Storms destroyed our nets, and damaged cutting edges caused us to repeat some samples.
sum-1967-10-09.spoken: We were about four hundred nautical miles southeast of the Cape of Good Hope, in the Indian Ocean. The day brought fourteen stations, including three piston cores and two heat-flow measurements. Storms destroyed our nets, and damaged cutting edges caused us to repeat some samples.

day-1967-10-10.caption: Tuesday, October 10th, 1967. Day 267 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Mauritius for Cape Town.
day-1967-10-10.spoken: Good morning. It's Tuesday, October tenth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day two hundred sixty-seven of the voyage, at sea, bound from Mauritius for Cape Town.

log-p086-0.caption: Core Camera 185: 6- PICTURES OCEAN FLOOR NOT POSSIBLE
log-p086-0.spoken: Core Camera one hundred eighty-five took six pictures, but photographing the ocean floor was not possible.

log-p086-1.caption: Bio 772-774: Intensive sound scattering near surface Correspondingly rich samples.
log-p086-1.spoken: Bio tows seven hundred seventy-two to seven hundred seventy-four found intensive sound scattering near the surface. The samples were correspondingly rich.

sum-1967-10-10.caption: We worked 6 stations about 200 nautical miles southeast of the Cape of Good Hope, in the Indian Ocean. The camera failed to photograph the ocean floor, but we found rich samples and a luminescent one with a preserved fish.
sum-1967-10-10.spoken: We worked six stations about two hundred nautical miles southeast of the Cape of Good Hope, in the Indian Ocean. The camera failed to photograph the ocean floor, but we found rich samples and a luminescent one with a preserved fish.

log-p086-5.caption: JN 120: Very rich, highly luminescent sample including a beautifully preserved bathylaconidian of the order salmoniformes. Rich sample possibly due to proximity to continental shelf
log-p086-5.spoken: Jet net one hundred twenty was very rich and highly luminescent. It included a beautifully preserved bathylaconidian of the order salmoniformes.

day-1967-10-11.caption: Wednesday, October 11th, 1967. Day 268 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Mauritius for Cape Town.
day-1967-10-11.spoken: Good morning. It's Wednesday, October eleventh, nineteen sixty-seven. Day two hundred sixty-eight of the voyage, at sea, bound from Mauritius for Cape Town.

leg-V2411-end.caption: Arriving Cape Town. Log: Very poor weather - 2 heavy gales. On this leg: 3,795 miles, 440 hours under way and 45 hours on station, averaging 9.5 knots.
leg-V2411-end.spoken: Vema arrives in Cape Town. From the voyage log: Very poor weather. Two heavy gales. On this leg: three thousand seven hundred ninety-five miles, four hundred forty hours under way and forty-five hours on station, averaging nine point five knots.

day-1967-10-12.caption: Thursday, October 12th, 1967. Day 269 of the voyage, in port at Cape Town.
day-1967-10-12.spoken: Good morning. It's Thursday, October twelfth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day two hundred sixty-nine of the voyage, in port at Cape Town.

day-1967-10-13.caption: Friday, October 13th, 1967. Day 270 of the voyage, in port at Cape Town.
day-1967-10-13.spoken: Good morning. It's Friday, October thirteenth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day two hundred seventy of the voyage, in port at Cape Town.

day-1967-10-14.caption: Saturday, October 14th, 1967. Day 271 of the voyage, in port at Cape Town.
day-1967-10-14.spoken: Good morning. It's Saturday, October fourteenth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day two hundred seventy-one of the voyage, in port at Cape Town.

day-1967-10-15.caption: Sunday, October 15th, 1967. Day 272 of the voyage, in port at Cape Town.
day-1967-10-15.spoken: Good morning. It's Sunday, October fifteenth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day two hundred seventy-two of the voyage, in port at Cape Town.

day-1967-10-16.caption: Monday, October 16th, 1967. Day 273 of the voyage, in port at Cape Town.
day-1967-10-16.spoken: Good morning. It's Monday, October sixteenth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day two hundred seventy-three of the voyage, in port at Cape Town.

leg-V2412-start.caption: Leg 12 of 13: Cape Town to Rio de Janeiro. Chief scientist T.D. Aitken.
leg-V2412-start.spoken: Leg twelve of thirteen begins. Vema sails from Cape Town for Rio de Janeiro, with T. D. Aitken as chief scientist.

day-1967-10-17.caption: Tuesday, October 17th, 1967. Day 274 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Cape Town for Rio de Janeiro.
day-1967-10-17.spoken: Good morning. It's Tuesday, October seventeenth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day two hundred seventy-four of the voyage, at sea, bound from Cape Town for Rio de Janeiro.

log-p085-2.caption: Core Camera 186-A: No Pictures. Bad conditions and some bad waves.
log-p085-2.spoken: Core camera one hundred eighty-six-A came back with no pictures. Bad conditions and some bad waves prevented the shots.

sum-1967-10-17.caption: We were about 200 nautical miles west of the Cape of Good Hope, in the South Atlantic. The team took 4 samples, including 1 piston core and 1 heat-flow measurement. Bad conditions prevented the camera from taking any pictures.
sum-1967-10-17.spoken: We were about two hundred nautical miles west of the Cape of Good Hope, in the South Atlantic. The team took four samples, including one piston core and one heat-flow measurement. Bad conditions prevented the camera from taking any pictures.

day-1967-10-18.caption: Wednesday, October 18th, 1967. Day 275 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Cape Town for Rio de Janeiro.
day-1967-10-18.spoken: Good morning. It's Wednesday, October eighteenth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day two hundred seventy-five of the voyage, at sea, bound from Cape Town for Rio de Janeiro.

sum-1967-10-18.caption: We were about 500 nautical miles west of the Cape of Good Hope, in the South Atlantic. The crew deployed 1 sonobuoy to gather data.
sum-1967-10-18.spoken: We were about five hundred nautical miles west of the Cape of Good Hope, in the South Atlantic. The crew deployed one sonobuoy to gather data.

day-1967-10-19.caption: Thursday, October 19th, 1967. Day 276 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Cape Town for Rio de Janeiro.
day-1967-10-19.spoken: Good morning. It's Thursday, October nineteenth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day two hundred seventy-six of the voyage, at sea, bound from Cape Town for Rio de Janeiro.

log-p085-5.caption: Core 218: Pen. 389. C.L. 923 cm. T.C. 40 cm. Brown marl with manganese nodules ranging in size from 5x4x2 cm to micro nodules, layer of Bentonite present between 32-40 cm. This layer is broken. Core may not have tripped
log-p085-5.spoken: Piston core two hundred eighteen contained brown marl with manganese nodules. A layer of bentonite was present, but the core may not have tripped.

log-p084-1.caption: BODS CAMERA 186-B: No Pictures
log-p084-1.spoken: Bottom camera one hundred eighty-six-B came back with no pictures.

day-1967-10-20.caption: Friday, October 20th, 1967. Day 277 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Cape Town for Rio de Janeiro.
day-1967-10-20.spoken: Good morning. It's Friday, October twentieth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day two hundred seventy-seven of the voyage, at sea, bound from Cape Town for Rio de Janeiro.

log-p083-0.caption: Camera 131: 11- Pictures Good Compass Pictures SBD mont only. - Did not Sound Nephel Down due to Burned out motor!
log-p083-0.spoken: The bottom camera took eleven good pictures, but the nephelometer could not be lowered because its motor burned out.

sum-1967-10-20.caption: In the South Atlantic, we took 5 stations, including 1 bottom-camera lowering and 1 sonobuoy. The water was 2745 fathoms deep. A nephelometer motor burned out.
sum-1967-10-20.spoken: In the South Atlantic, we took five stations, including one bottom-camera lowering and one sonobuoy. The water was two thousand seven hundred forty-five fathoms deep. A nephelometer motor burned out.

day-1967-10-21.caption: Saturday, October 21st, 1967. Day 278 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Cape Town for Rio de Janeiro.
day-1967-10-21.spoken: Good morning. It's Saturday, October twenty-first, nineteen sixty-seven. Day two hundred seventy-eight of the voyage, at sea, bound from Cape Town for Rio de Janeiro.

log-p083-7.caption: Core Camera 185-D: No Returns Did not advance
log-p083-7.spoken: Core camera one hundred eighty-five-D returned no pictures and the film did not advance.

sum-1967-10-21.caption: In the South Atlantic, the crew took 5 stations at 1725 fathoms. They lowered a piston core, a camera, and a nephelometer. The camera failed to record.
sum-1967-10-21.spoken: In the South Atlantic, the crew took five stations at seventeen twenty-five fathoms. They lowered a piston core, a camera, and a nephelometer. The camera failed to record.

day-1967-10-22.caption: Sunday, October 22nd, 1967. Day 279 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Cape Town for Rio de Janeiro.
day-1967-10-22.spoken: Good morning. It's Sunday, October twenty-second, nineteen sixty-seven. Day two hundred seventy-nine of the voyage, at sea, bound from Cape Town for Rio de Janeiro.

log-p082-2.caption: Core 221A: Pen: 180 cm C.L. 0cm One pipe which was very bent. No Trigger core either.
log-p082-2.spoken: Piston core 221A came up with a very bent pipe. It penetrated one hundred eighty centimeters, but the core length was zero centimeters.

log-p082-6.caption: Core Camera 186-E: No Pictures Did not advance - worked on deck Not in water
log-p082-6.spoken: Core camera one hundred eighty-six-E did not take any pictures. It did not advance and was not in the water.

sum-1967-10-22.caption: We were in the South Atlantic, taking 7 stations. A bent pipe meant no core, and the camera failed to take pictures.
sum-1967-10-22.spoken: We were in the South Atlantic, taking seven stations. A bent pipe meant no core, and the camera failed to take pictures.

day-1967-10-23.caption: Monday, October 23rd, 1967. Day 280 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Cape Town for Rio de Janeiro.
day-1967-10-23.spoken: Good morning. It's Monday, October twenty-third, nineteen sixty-seven. Day two hundred eighty of the voyage, at sea, bound from Cape Town for Rio de Janeiro.

log-p081-7.caption: Core Camera 186G: No flash - no picture.
log-p081-7.spoken: Core camera 186G had no flash. It did not take a picture.

sum-1967-10-23.caption: We were about 600 nautical miles northeast of Tristan da Cunha, in the South Atlantic. The team completed 7 stations, including 2 bathythermograph drops. The camera on the corer failed to take a picture.
sum-1967-10-23.spoken: We were about six hundred nautical miles northeast of Tristan da Cunha, in the South Atlantic. The team completed seven stations, including two bathythermograph drops. The camera on the corer failed to take a picture.

day-1967-10-24.caption: Tuesday, October 24th, 1967. Day 281 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Cape Town for Rio de Janeiro.
day-1967-10-24.spoken: Good morning. It's Tuesday, October twenty-fourth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day two hundred eighty-one of the voyage, at sea, bound from Cape Town for Rio de Janeiro.

sum-1967-10-24.caption: We were about 500 nautical miles east of Tristan da Cunha, in the South Atlantic. The crew completed 10 stations, including 2 bathythermograph drops. We saw animal life on the bottom at 1400 fathoms.
sum-1967-10-24.spoken: We were about five hundred nautical miles east of Tristan da Cunha, in the South Atlantic. The crew completed ten stations, including two bathythermograph drops. We saw animal life on the bottom at fourteen hundred fathoms.

log-p077-2.caption: CAMERA 137: 13 PICTURES - 13 HITS SEDIMENT, SOME ANIMAC LIFE, POLYS.
log-p077-2.spoken: Camera one hundred thirty-seven took thirteen pictures of the sediment. It showed some animal life and polyps.

day-1967-10-25.caption: Wednesday, October 25th, 1967. Day 282 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Cape Town for Rio de Janeiro.
day-1967-10-25.spoken: Good morning. It's Wednesday, October twenty-fifth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day two hundred eighty-two of the voyage, at sea, bound from Cape Town for Rio de Janeiro.

log-p075-1.caption: Dredge 3A: No Sample. It is believed dredge didn't Hit bottom. Wire Angle 56°
log-p075-1.spoken: Dredge 3A came back with no sample. The crew believed it did not hit the bottom.

log-p076-6.caption: Core 226: Pen - C.L. Jar Sample The one pipe was very bent and cutting edge damaged. Basalt fragments found in core catcher
log-p076-6.spoken: Piston core two hundred twenty-six came up with a very bent pipe and a damaged cutting edge. Basalt fragments were found in the core catcher.

log-p075-2.caption: Core 227: Pen - C.L. Jar Sample of Basalts Manganese Fragments. Pipe bent & cutting edge damaged.
log-p075-2.spoken: Piston core two hundred twenty-seven brought up a jar sample of basalts and manganese fragments. The pipe was bent and the cutting edge was damaged.

sum-1967-10-25.caption: We were about 400 nautical miles east of Tristan da Cunha in the South Atlantic. The team took 8 samples, including 2 piston cores and 1 dredge haul. A damaged pipe and basalt fragments were found, though the dredge missed the bottom.
sum-1967-10-25.spoken: We were about four hundred nautical miles east of Tristan da Cunha in the South Atlantic. The team took eight samples, including two piston cores and one dredge haul. A damaged pipe and basalt fragments were found, though the dredge missed the bottom.

day-1967-10-26.caption: Thursday, October 26th, 1967. Day 283 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Cape Town for Rio de Janeiro.
day-1967-10-26.spoken: Good morning. It's Thursday, October twenty-sixth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day two hundred eighty-three of the voyage, at sea, bound from Cape Town for Rio de Janeiro.

sum-1967-10-26.caption: We were about 300 nautical miles northeast of Tristan da Cunha, in the South Atlantic. The crew worked at 4 stations, including a bottom-camera lowering. The water depth was 2188 fathoms.
sum-1967-10-26.spoken: We were about three hundred nautical miles northeast of Tristan da Cunha, in the South Atlantic. The crew worked at four stations, including a bottom-camera lowering. The water depth was two thousand one hundred eighty-eight fathoms.

day-1967-10-27.caption: Friday, October 27th, 1967. Day 284 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Cape Town for Rio de Janeiro.
day-1967-10-27.spoken: Good morning. It's Friday, October twenty-seventh, nineteen sixty-seven. Day two hundred eighty-four of the voyage, at sea, bound from Cape Town for Rio de Janeiro.

log-p074-4.caption: Camera 141: 20 Hits - 4 Pictures Flash (stored light batteries low voltage) did not work, track & trails some bottom life.
log-p074-4.spoken: The flash did not work on camera one hundred forty-one because the batteries were low. The track showed some bottom life.

log-p074-5.caption: Nephelometer 139: Did not see hit, laid some wire on bottom No layer
log-p074-5.spoken: The nephelometer did not see a hit. Some wire was laid on the bottom, and no layer was found.

log-p074-2.caption: Core 229: Pen. 550cm C.L. 407cm T.C. 280cm Lt. Tan foraminiferal marl with slight burrowing. Core dated as Pliocene by Dr. Saito
log-p074-2.spoken: Piston core two hundred twenty-nine brought up light tan foraminiferal marl. Dr. Saito dated the core as Pliocene.

log-p073-2.caption: Core #230: Pen 380 cm CL 876 cm TC ~375 cm Lt. Tan foraminiferal marl. Slight burrowing near upper part of the core. Dated as Pleistocene by Dr. Saito.
log-p073-2.spoken: Piston core two hundred thirty brought up light tan foraminiferal marl. Dr. Saito dated the sediment as Pleistocene.

log-p073-5.caption: Nepholo-meter 140: No LAYEN!
log-p073-5.spoken: The nephelometer at station one hundred forty did not work.

sum-1967-10-27.caption: We worked about 200 nautical miles north of Tristan da Cunha. Soundings reached 1890 and 2250 fathoms. A scientist identified Pliocene age, and we saw bottom life when a flash failed.
sum-1967-10-27.spoken: We worked about two hundred nautical miles north of Tristan da Cunha. Soundings reached eighteen ninety and two thousand two hundred fifty fathoms. A scientist identified Pliocene age, and we saw bottom life when a flash failed.

day-1967-10-28.caption: Saturday, October 28th, 1967. Day 285 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Cape Town for Rio de Janeiro.
day-1967-10-28.spoken: Good morning. It's Saturday, October twenty-eighth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day two hundred eighty-five of the voyage, at sea, bound from Cape Town for Rio de Janeiro.

log-p072-2.caption: CAMERA 143A: 17 Hits - 0 Pictures Not enough film (to shoot at a length)
log-p072-2.spoken: Bottom camera 143A hit the floor seventeen times but took no pictures. There was not enough film to shoot at that length.

log-p072-3.caption: NEPHO-METER 141A: No Trace On Film, Light Was Out When Unit Surfaced - Not Checked At All Now.
log-p072-3.spoken: Nephelometer 141A showed no trace on the film. The light was out when the unit surfaced, so it was not checked.

log-p071-1.caption: Camera 143-2: 12 HIT - 12 PICTURES TRACES & TRAILS (SOME ANIMAL LIFE) SEDIMENT.
log-p071-1.spoken: Camera one hundred forty-three-two took twelve pictures of the sea floor. The photos showed traces and trails from some animal life in the sediment.

log-p071-3.caption: Surface Plankton 780SF: Abnormal amount of Copepods were caught in this surface tow
log-p071-3.spoken: The surface plankton tow caught an abnormal amount of copepods.

sum-1967-10-28.caption: We worked about 200 nautical miles northwest of Tristan da Cunha. The camera and nephelometer failed, but we saw animal life and many copepods. Soundings reached 1700 and 1782 fathoms.
sum-1967-10-28.spoken: We worked about two hundred nautical miles northwest of Tristan da Cunha. The camera and nephelometer failed, but we saw animal life and many copepods. Soundings reached seventeen hundred and seventeen eighty-two fathoms.

day-1967-10-29.caption: Sunday, October 29th, 1967. Day 286 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Cape Town for Rio de Janeiro.
day-1967-10-29.spoken: Good morning. It's Sunday, October twenty-ninth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day two hundred eighty-six of the voyage, at sea, bound from Cape Town for Rio de Janeiro.

log-p070-1.caption: Nepholo-meter 142: No Canyon!
log-p070-1.spoken: The nephelometer reading at station one hundred forty-two showed no canyon.

log-p071-5.caption: Core 233: Pen 300 cm. C.L. 317 cm Lt. Tan Foraminiferal marl ooze, with slight burrowing. Dated as Pleistocene by Dr. Saito.
log-p071-5.spoken: Piston core two hundred thirty-three came up with three hundred seventeen centimeters of light tan foraminiferal marl ooze. Dr. Saito dated it as Pleistocene.

log-p070-5.caption: Core 234: Pen ~250 cm C.L. 588 cm T.C. 240 cm Lt. Tan Foram sand changing to foramiferous marl ooze at about 21 cm. Slight burrowing present. Core dated as Pleistocene by Dr Saito.
log-p070-5.spoken: Piston core two hundred thirty-four was dated as Pleistocene by Dr Saito. It contained light tan foraminiferal sand changing to foraminiferal marl ooze.

sum-1967-10-29.caption: We were about 300 nautical miles northwest of Tristan da Cunha, in the South Atlantic. The crew took 13 samples and found a Pleistocene core. They also noticed an unexpected absence of a canyon.
sum-1967-10-29.spoken: We were about three hundred nautical miles northwest of Tristan da Cunha, in the South Atlantic. The crew took thirteen samples and found a Pleistocene core. They also noticed an unexpected absence of a canyon.

day-1967-10-30.caption: Monday, October 30th, 1967. Day 287 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Cape Town for Rio de Janeiro.
day-1967-10-30.spoken: Good morning. It's Monday, October thirtieth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day two hundred eighty-seven of the voyage, at sea, bound from Cape Town for Rio de Janeiro.

sum-1967-10-30.caption: We worked about 400 nautical miles northwest of Tristan da Cunha in the South Atlantic. The crew took 6 stations, including a piston core and a heat-flow measurement of 2.6.
sum-1967-10-30.spoken: We worked about four hundred nautical miles northwest of Tristan da Cunha in the South Atlantic. The crew took six stations, including a piston core and a heat-flow measurement of two point six.

day-1967-10-31.caption: Tuesday, October 31st, 1967. Day 288 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Cape Town for Rio de Janeiro.
day-1967-10-31.spoken: Good morning. It's Tuesday, October thirty-first, nineteen sixty-seven. Day two hundred eighty-eight of the voyage, at sea, bound from Cape Town for Rio de Janeiro.

sum-1967-10-31.caption: We were in the South Atlantic, taking 7 stations. Dr. Saito identified Pliocene age in the 2173 fathom sounding.
sum-1967-10-31.spoken: We were in the South Atlantic, taking seven stations. Dr. Saito identified Pliocene age in the two thousand one hundred seventy-three fathom sounding.

log-p068-3.caption: Core 236: Pen. 622 cm. C.L. 990 TC 698cm Lt. Tan Foraminiferal marl heavily burrowed. The core was dated as Pliocene by Dr. Saito.
log-p068-3.spoken: Piston core two hundred thirty-six brought up light tan foraminiferal marl. Dr. Saito dated the core as Pliocene.

day-1967-11-01.caption: Wednesday, November 1st, 1967. Day 289 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Cape Town for Rio de Janeiro.
day-1967-11-01.spoken: Good morning. It's Wednesday, November first, nineteen sixty-seven. Day two hundred eighty-nine of the voyage, at sea, bound from Cape Town for Rio de Janeiro.

log-p067-3.caption: CAMERA 148-2: 2 PICTURES 30 HITS. TELLTALE WITH CORAL AT SECOND PICTURE. 2 LIGHT STRICKEN NEGATIVES SHOWING MANGANESE NODULES.
log-p067-3.spoken: Camera one hundred forty-eight-two captured thirty hits, including coral and manganese nodules. Two of the negatives were light stricken.

log-p067-0.caption: CORE 237: Pen. 823cm CL 1195cm TC 740cm. Lt Tan changing to Darker Brown Foraminiferal marl. Base of core is formed by a Mn layer 7cm Thick, Dated as Eocene by Dr. Saito.
log-p067-0.spoken: Piston core two hundred thirty-seven brought up a thin manganese layer at the bottom. Dr. Saito dated that layer as Eocene.

sum-1967-11-01.caption: Vema worked in the South Atlantic at 2240 fathoms. Dr. Saito found an Eocene layer, and film showed coral and nodules. The team completed 8 stations including a heat-flow measurement of 2.05.
sum-1967-11-01.spoken: Vema worked in the South Atlantic at two thousand two hundred forty fathoms. Dr. Saito found an Eocene layer, and film showed coral and nodules. The team completed eight stations including a heat-flow measurement of two point zero five.

day-1967-11-02.caption: Thursday, November 2nd, 1967. Day 290 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Cape Town for Rio de Janeiro.
day-1967-11-02.spoken: Good morning. It's Thursday, November second, nineteen sixty-seven. Day two hundred ninety of the voyage, at sea, bound from Cape Town for Rio de Janeiro.

log-p066-6.caption: CAMERA 14 9/9: 9 PICTURES 29. WIDE SOME FAUNA - SEDIMENT TRIPYON LIGHT LOST AGAIN.
log-p066-6.spoken: Camera fourteen took nine pictures of some fauna and sediment. The light was lost again.

log-p065-5.caption: Nepholometer 148-000: NO LAYEN. NEPHO NOT RUNNING, BATTERIES DISCHARGED COMPLETELY.
log-p065-5.spoken: Nephelometer one hundred forty-eight was not running because its batteries were discharged completely.

log-p064-0.caption: Core 240: Pen 1089 cm C.L. 1092 cm TC 1020 cm Lt Tan foraminiferal marl changing to dark brown Marl. Heavy burrowing in the upper sections of the core. Dated as Upper Pliocene by Dr. Saito.
log-p064-0.spoken: Piston core two hundred forty showed heavy burrowing in its upper sections. Dr. Saito dated the sediment as Upper Pliocene.

sum-1967-11-02.caption: In the South Atlantic, the Vema completed 18 stations. We took 3 piston cores and 2 heat-flow measurements, reading 1.8 and 1.66. The camera light failed again, and batteries ran out. We found a named scientist in heavy burrowing Pliocene age.
sum-1967-11-02.spoken: In the South Atlantic, the Vema completed eighteen stations. We took three piston cores and two heat-flow measurements, reading one point eight and one point six six. The camera light failed again, and batteries ran out. We found a named scientist in heavy burrowing Pliocene age.

day-1967-11-03.caption: Friday, November 3rd, 1967. Day 291 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Cape Town for Rio de Janeiro.
day-1967-11-03.spoken: Good morning. It's Friday, November third, nineteen sixty-seven. Day two hundred ninety-one of the voyage, at sea, bound from Cape Town for Rio de Janeiro.

log-p063-2.caption: BT #103: Lost BTuCC16145, Used BT*8151B
log-p063-2.spoken: The crew lost bathythermograph number one hundred three. They used a different unit, number 8151B, instead.

log-p064-4.caption: Core 241: Pen. ~ 700 cm C.L. 1100 cm TC 690 cm Various tan foraminiferal marl oozes and marls. A foram sand layer is present between 645-660 cm. The core was dated as Pleistocene by Dr. Saito.
log-p064-4.spoken: Piston core two hundred forty-one contained a layer of foraminiferal sand between six hundred forty-five and six hundred sixty centimeters. Dr. Saito dated the core as Pleistocene.

log-p064-6.caption: Camera 151 30: 30 Negatives 30 Aids No nephel - out of battery No good camera - film short. Traces and trails Sediment.
log-p064-6.spoken: The bottom camera for station one hundred fifty-one came back with no good pictures because the film was short. The nephelometer also failed due to a dead battery.

sum-1967-11-03.caption: In the South Atlantic, the crew worked at 13 stations, including 2 sonobuoys and 2 piston cores. Soundings reached 2098 and 2170 fathoms. A camera failure meant no good pictures, but an instrument was replaced after being lost.
sum-1967-11-03.spoken: In the South Atlantic, the crew worked at thirteen stations, including two sonobuoys and two piston cores. Soundings reached twenty ninety-eight and two thousand one hundred seventy fathoms. A camera failure meant no good pictures, but an instrument was replaced after being lost.

day-1967-11-04.caption: Saturday, November 4th, 1967. Day 292 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Cape Town for Rio de Janeiro.
day-1967-11-04.spoken: Good morning. It's Saturday, November fourth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day two hundred ninety-two of the voyage, at sea, bound from Cape Town for Rio de Janeiro.

sum-1967-11-04.caption: We were in the South Atlantic. The crew deployed 1 sonobuoy. It was a quiet day of science aboard Vema.
sum-1967-11-04.spoken: We were in the South Atlantic. The crew deployed one sonobuoy. It was a quiet day of science aboard Vema.

day-1967-11-05.caption: Sunday, November 5th, 1967. Day 293 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Cape Town for Rio de Janeiro.
day-1967-11-05.spoken: Good morning. It's Sunday, November fifth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day two hundred ninety-three of the voyage, at sea, bound from Cape Town for Rio de Janeiro.

log-p062-0.caption: Core 243: Pen. - CL. Jar, No Trigger Core White limestone scraped from core catcher Cutting Edge containing recrystallized forams. Core Dated as Paleocene by Dr Saito.
log-p062-0.spoken: Piston core two hundred forty-three brought up white limestone with recrystallized forams. Dr. Saito dated the core as Paleocene.

log-p062-1.caption: FGMAD 199A: No Record - No Penetration
log-p062-1.spoken: Station FGMAD 199A failed to penetrate the sea floor, so no record was obtained.

log-p062-2.caption: Camera 153-13: 13 - NAGATOWAS 15 HITS ABUNDANT FAUNA ROCK BOTTOM CRANBRO PARTITIONS.
log-p062-2.spoken: Camera one hundred fifty-three to thirteen took fifteen hits on a rock bottom. The photos showed abundant fauna and partitions.

log-p062-6.caption: Core 245: Pen. - CL. Jar, No Trigger Core Pieces or Aggregate of hydrozoans, pteropods, & forams cemented together by white marl. Dated as Pleistocene.
log-p062-6.spoken: Piston core two hundred forty-five recovered pieces of hydrozoans and pteropods cemented by white marl. It was dated as Pleistocene.

log-p061-2.caption: CAMERA 154-17: 17 VALATIVES - 20 HITS COMPASS PICTURE LOOKING FAIR. 20th HIT AT 444 FMS. (FAUNA AND FLORA) LARGE ROCKS - RIPPLE MARKS
log-p061-2.spoken: Camera one hundred fifty-four to seventeen took twenty hits, with the twentieth at four hundred forty-four fathoms. The pictures showed fauna, flora, large rocks, and ripple marks.

sum-1967-11-05.caption: In the South Atlantic, the Vema took 5 piston cores and 3 other stations. We found Paleocene limestone and a rock bottom with abundant fauna. The day also included 3 bottom-camera lowerings and 1 sonobuoy.
sum-1967-11-05.spoken: In the South Atlantic, the Vema took five piston cores and three other stations. We found Paleocene limestone and a rock bottom with abundant fauna. The day also included three bottom-camera lowerings and one sonobuoy.

day-1967-11-06.caption: Monday, November 6th, 1967. Day 294 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Cape Town for Rio de Janeiro.
day-1967-11-06.spoken: Good morning. It's Monday, November sixth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day two hundred ninety-four of the voyage, at sea, bound from Cape Town for Rio de Janeiro.

day-1967-11-06-again.caption: Monday, November 6th, 1967 (again). Day 294 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Cape Town for Rio de Janeiro.
day-1967-11-06-again.spoken: Good morning. It's Monday, November sixth, nineteen sixty-seven, again. Having crossed the date line eastbound, Vema lives this date twice. Day two hundred ninety-four of the voyage, at sea, bound from Cape Town for Rio de Janeiro.

sum-1967-11-06.caption: We were about 600 nautical miles southeast of Rio de Janeiro. The crew made 5 stations, including a heat-flow measurement of 1.2. The dredge came up empty.
sum-1967-11-06.spoken: We were about six hundred nautical miles southeast of Rio de Janeiro. The crew made five stations, including a heat-flow measurement of one point two. The dredge came up empty.

log-p060-3.caption: Dredge 3B: Surfaced Empty. Doubtful if dredge hit Bottom
log-p060-3.spoken: Dredge 3B surfaced empty. The crew doubted if the dredge hit the bottom.

log-p060-4.caption: Camera 157-9: 9 Pictures - 11 Hits Some Flora Solid Rock Cliffs and Ledges
log-p060-4.spoken: Camera one hundred fifty-seven-nine took nine pictures and made eleven hits. It showed some flora, solid rock cliffs, and ledges.

day-1967-11-07.caption: Tuesday, November 7th, 1967. Day 295 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Cape Town for Rio de Janeiro.
day-1967-11-07.spoken: Good morning. It's Tuesday, November seventh, nineteen sixty-seven. Day two hundred ninety-five of the voyage, at sea, bound from Cape Town for Rio de Janeiro.

sum-1967-11-07.caption: We were about 500 nautical miles southeast of Rio de Janeiro in the South Atlantic. The team completed 12 stations, including 3 bottom-camera lowerings and 2 heat-flow measurements. We saw flora and rock cliffs, though a light unit failed.
sum-1967-11-07.spoken: We were about five hundred nautical miles southeast of Rio de Janeiro in the South Atlantic. The team completed twelve stations, including three bottom-camera lowerings and two heat-flow measurements. We saw flora and rock cliffs, though a light unit failed.

log-p058-0.caption: Camera 159A: 32 - HITS 6 VOLT PULSE FROM STEREO LIGHT UNIT FAILED DUE TO A SODON CONNECTION BROKEN.
log-p058-0.spoken: Camera 159A got thirty-two hits, but the stereo light unit failed. A solder connection had broken.

log-p058-6.caption: Nephelometer Meter 149-A: Forgot T. Put in light Look at Nephel Sheet for this station.
log-p058-6.spoken: The crew forgot to turn on the light for the nephelometer. They noted to check the sheet for this station.

day-1967-11-08.caption: Wednesday, November 8th, 1967. Day 296 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Cape Town for Rio de Janeiro.
day-1967-11-08.spoken: Good morning. It's Wednesday, November eighth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day two hundred ninety-six of the voyage, at sea, bound from Cape Town for Rio de Janeiro.

sum-1967-11-08.caption: We were about 500 nautical miles southeast of Rio de Janeiro in the South Atlantic. The team took 6 samples and measurements. We forgot to turn on the light.
sum-1967-11-08.spoken: We were about five hundred nautical miles southeast of Rio de Janeiro in the South Atlantic. The team took six samples and measurements. We forgot to turn on the light.

log-p057-3.caption: T-GRAD 203A: NO RECORD - NO PENETRATION
log-p057-3.spoken: Heat-flow station 203A got no record. The probe did not penetrate the sea floor.

log-p057-4.caption: Camera 160-11: 11 NEGATIVES 30 HITS TRIGGER WEIGHT LOST AFTER 11th PICKUP. TRACK AND TRAILS FAUNA AND FLORA SEDIMENT
log-p057-4.spoken: Camera one hundred sixty to eleven took eleven negatives and thirty hits. The trigger weight was lost after the eleventh pickup, and the film showed track and trails fauna and flora.

day-1967-11-09.caption: Thursday, November 9th, 1967. Day 297 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Cape Town for Rio de Janeiro.
day-1967-11-09.spoken: Good morning. It's Thursday, November ninth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day two hundred ninety-seven of the voyage, at sea, bound from Cape Town for Rio de Janeiro.

sum-1967-11-09.caption: We worked about 300 nautical miles south of Rio de Janeiro in the South Atlantic. The probe failed to penetrate, and a trigger weight was lost, revealing fauna. We completed 7 stations, including 1 piston core and 1 sonobuoy.
sum-1967-11-09.spoken: We worked about three hundred nautical miles south of Rio de Janeiro in the South Atlantic. The probe failed to penetrate, and a trigger weight was lost, revealing fauna. We completed seven stations, including one piston core and one sonobuoy.

day-1967-11-10.caption: Friday, November 10th, 1967. Day 298 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Cape Town for Rio de Janeiro.
day-1967-11-10.spoken: Good morning. It's Friday, November tenth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day two hundred ninety-eight of the voyage, at sea, bound from Cape Town for Rio de Janeiro.

log-p049-2.caption: T-GRAD 206: 4 PROBES IN MUD - APPARENTLY CORER PENETRATED FULLY IN SPITE OF NO TRIP. MUST USE CAUTION IN FIGURING THERMAL GRADIENT DUE TO THE VERTICAL QUESTION H.F. = 1.45 mu cal/cm2/sec
log-p049-2.spoken: Heat-flow station two hundred six used four probes in the mud. The corer penetrated fully despite no trip, so caution was needed for the thermal gradient. The heat flow was one point four five microcalories per square centimeter per second.

log-p048-4.caption: T-Grad 207: DUE TO VERY SHALLOW PENETRATION ONLY BOTTOM PROBE IN MUD. PROB- ABLY CORER FELL OVER AFTER REACHING BOTTOM SO VALUE OF THIS MEAS. IS SMALL. H.F. = 3.44 ucal/cm2/sec

log-p034-5.spoken: The camera run was aborted because of the trouble described above.

log-p034-1.caption: CORE 261A: RETURNED RIG TO THE SURFACE AFTER LOWERING TO 1500 FMS, TO CHECK CONDITION. LOWERED TO 700 FMS, AND HAD TROUBLE WITH WATER BRAKE - CROSSED WITH HYDROWIRE - QUIT.
log-p034-1.spoken: The coring rig was lowered to fifteen hundred fathoms to check its condition. It was then lowered to seven hundred fathoms, but the water brake crossed with the hydro wire, so the work was quit.

log-p034-2.caption: PGMHD #213A: NO RECORD - SEE ABOVE
log-p034-2.spoken: No record was obtained for this station because of the trouble described above.

sum-1967-12-08.caption: About 200 nautical miles north of Barbados, the Vema took 10 samples. A water brake crossed with wire forced a stop. Later, a parted wire lost the current meter and camera.
sum-1967-12-08.spoken: About two hundred nautical miles north of Barbados, the Vema took ten samples. A water brake crossed with wire forced a stop. Later, a parted wire lost the current meter and camera.

day-1967-12-09.caption: Saturday, December 9th, 1967. Day 327 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Rio de Janeiro for Miami.
day-1967-12-09.spoken: Good morning. It's Saturday, December ninth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day three hundred twenty-seven of the voyage, at sea, bound from Rio de Janeiro for Miami.

sum-1967-12-09.caption: We were about 200 nautical miles east of Puerto Rico, in the Caribbean. The team completed 2 other stations and 2 jet-net tows today.
sum-1967-12-09.spoken: We were about two hundred nautical miles east of Puerto Rico, in the Caribbean. The team completed two other stations and two jet-net tows today.

log-p032-3.caption: Camera 170: 8 frames poorly lighted - discovered faulty capacitor
log-p032-3.spoken: Camera one hundred seventy took eight poorly lighted frames. The crew discovered a faulty capacitor was the cause.

day-1967-12-10.caption: Sunday, December 10th, 1967. Day 328 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Rio de Janeiro for Miami.
day-1967-12-10.spoken: Good morning. It's Sunday, December tenth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day three hundred twenty-eight of the voyage, at sea, bound from Rio de Janeiro for Miami.

log-p032-2.caption: Core Camera 191A: Malfunction - film ran thru prematurely
log-p032-2.spoken: Core camera 191A malfunctioned because the film ran through prematurely.

sum-1967-12-10.caption: We worked about 100 nautical miles northeast of Puerto Rico, in the Caribbean. The camera film malfunctioned due to a faulty capacitor. We completed 8 stations, including 2 jet-net tows and 1 heat-flow measurement.
sum-1967-12-10.spoken: We worked about one hundred nautical miles northeast of Puerto Rico, in the Caribbean. The camera film malfunctioned due to a faulty capacitor. We completed eight stations, including two jet-net tows and one heat-flow measurement.

day-1967-12-11.caption: Monday, December 11th, 1967. Day 329 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Rio de Janeiro for Miami.
day-1967-12-11.spoken: Good morning. It's Monday, December eleventh, nineteen sixty-seven. Day three hundred twenty-nine of the voyage, at sea, bound from Rio de Janeiro for Miami.

day-1967-12-11-again.caption: Monday, December 11th, 1967 (again). Day 329 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Rio de Janeiro for Miami.
day-1967-12-11-again.spoken: Good morning. It's Monday, December eleventh, nineteen sixty-seven, again. Having crossed the date line eastbound, Vema lives this date twice. Day three hundred twenty-nine of the voyage, at sea, bound from Rio de Janeiro for Miami.

log-p030-0.caption: Core Camera 191: 3 FRAMES ONLY - NO BOTTOM PIX. DUE TO CORE RIG GOING IN FULLY.
log-p030-0.spoken: Core camera one hundred ninety-one took only three frames and no bottom pictures. The core rig went in fully, which caused the problem.

log-p030-1.caption: Camera 171: 30 FRAMES EACH PARTLY OVERLAPPING & DOUBLE EXPOSING ADJACENT FRAMES DUE TO FAULTY TRANSPORT. BOTTOM SOFT MUD WITHOUT FEATURES.
log-p030-1.spoken: Camera one hundred seventy-one had a faulty transport, so thirty frames were partly overlapping and double exposing. The bottom was soft mud without features.

sum-1967-12-11.caption: We worked about 300 nautical miles northwest of Puerto Rico in the North Atlantic. The camera failed due to a rig issue, and faulty film transport ruined the photos.
sum-1967-12-11.spoken: We worked about three hundred nautical miles northwest of Puerto Rico in the North Atlantic. The camera failed due to a rig issue, and faulty film transport ruined the photos.

day-1967-12-12.caption: Tuesday, December 12th, 1967. Day 330 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Rio de Janeiro for Miami.
day-1967-12-12.spoken: Good morning. It's Tuesday, December twelfth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day three hundred thirty of the voyage, at sea, bound from Rio de Janeiro for Miami.

log-p030-5.caption: Core Camera 192A: LIGHT FAILED TO WORK
log-p030-5.spoken: Core camera 192A failed to work because its light did not function.

sum-1967-12-12.caption: We were about 300 nautical miles east of the Bahamas, in the North Atlantic. The team collected 8 samples and took 1 heat-flow measurement of 1.48. The light failed to work.
sum-1967-12-12.spoken: We were about three hundred nautical miles east of the Bahamas, in the North Atlantic. The team collected eight samples and took one heat-flow measurement of one point four eight. The light failed to work.

day-1967-12-13.caption: Wednesday, December 13th, 1967. Day 331 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Rio de Janeiro for Miami.
day-1967-12-13.spoken: Good morning. It's Wednesday, December thirteenth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day three hundred thirty-one of the voyage, at sea, bound from Rio de Janeiro for Miami.

log-p028-0.caption: Core Camera 192: 4 FRAMES TAKEN, NONE ON BOTTOM
log-p028-0.spoken: Core camera one hundred ninety-two took four frames, but none showed the sea floor.

sum-1967-12-13.caption: We worked about 200 nautical miles east of the Bahamas in the North Atlantic. The camera failed to photograph the bottom, and a net broke without repair tools. We took 10 samples at a depth of 2819 fathoms.
sum-1967-12-13.spoken: We worked about two hundred nautical miles east of the Bahamas in the North Atlantic. The camera failed to photograph the bottom, and a net broke without repair tools. We took ten samples at a depth of two thousand eight hundred nineteen fathoms.

log-p027-0.caption: JN 160: Welds on jet-net fins gave way during recovery. No heli-arc equipment on board for repair.
log-p027-0.spoken: The welds on the jet-net fins gave way during recovery. There was no heli-arc equipment on board to repair it.

day-1967-12-14.caption: Thursday, December 14th, 1967. Day 332 of the voyage, at sea, bound from Rio de Janeiro for Miami.
day-1967-12-14.spoken: Good morning. It's Thursday, December fourteenth, nineteen sixty-seven. Day three hundred thirty-two of the voyage, at sea, bound from Rio de Janeiro for Miami.

leg-V2413-end.caption: Arriving Miami. Log: Stop at Barbados for fuel - fuel consumption high due adverse weather - currents and very heavy marine growth on bottom. On this leg: 5,600 miles, 612 hours under way and 63 hours on station, averaging 9.5 knots. For the whole voyage, the log counts 53,968 miles, 5,787 hours under way, 1,075 hours on station, 288 days at sea and 46 in port.
leg-V2413-end.spoken: Vema arrives in Miami. From the voyage log: A stop at Barbados for fuel. Fuel consumption was high, from adverse weather, currents, and very heavy marine growth on the bottom. On this leg: five thousand six hundred miles, six hundred twelve hours under way and sixty-three hours on station, averaging nine point five knots. For the whole voyage, the log counts fifty-three thousand nine hundred sixty-eight miles, five thousand seven hundred eighty-seven hours under way, one thousand seventy-five hours on station, two hundred eighty-eight days at sea and forty-six in port.

intro.caption: R/V Vema, Voyage 24, 1967: around the world, west-about.
intro.spoken: This is the research vessel Vema, on Voyage twenty-four, in nineteen sixty-seven. Lamont Geological Observatory's schooner is sailing around the world, west-about, and we follow her day by day.
